proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.02 for ordinary settings changes; vision is avoided unless iOS or a browser page exposes no structured state. The dominant cost is the optional verification snapshot.
proposals.security_concerns: Mutations remain under the owner's existing maximum-access policy, but the system must show the exact scope before acting, preserve pre/post receipts, and never claim a surface was changed without a fresh read. Browser credentials and phone content stay on their respective surfaces.
missing: A first-class postcondition/verification field on action plans and receipts
Structured read actions for common Mac, browser, and iOS state that can be compared before and after
A cross-surface transaction coordinator with explicit partial-success semantics and a single job identity
A pendant response format for concise confirmed/partial/unverified results

proposals.user_asks: “Hold onto this task and carry it out when the right context appears—only while I’m available, before it expires, and using the browser session that is already signed in.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner should be able to delegate intent from the pendant without forcing an immediate action: for example, queue a form draft until the Mac is awake and the right site is open, or ask to send a prepared reply only during a chosen time window. Today the relay, Mac, and browser can each do pieces, but none owns a durable, context-sensitive escrow with expiry, preconditions, and a final handoff back to the owner. This makes the system useful while the owner is walking away from the keyboard without turning an ambiguous command into an unsafe blind automation.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background planner to normalize the intent into explicit preconditions, expiry, and an action graph; use deterministic context watchers and browser/Mac actions to execute; reserve realtime for accepting the spoken request and reporting the final outcome.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the escrow on the pendant within 2 seconds. Evaluate conditions on event arrival or a low-frequency schedule. Once conditions match, execute within 10 seconds and give the owner a short confirmation or a request for clarification.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02 per escrow, dominated by one planning call; condition checks and job state are local/relay-side. No repeated model call is needed while waiting.
proposals.security_concerns: Never execute an expired or materially changed intent. Show the exact action, target account/site, preconditions, and expiry in the pending record; require a fresh owner confirmation when the action is consequential or the browser session changed. Keep credentials in the browser and transmit only intent/status.
missing: A durable relay-side escrow record with explicit preconditions, expiry, cancellation, and a stable intent ID
Context events from the Mac (awake/unlocked/active app/network) and browser (session/URL/page state) that can satisfy or invalidate preconditions
A planner/executor contract that revalidates the page and action immediately before dispatch
Pendant UI for listing, cancelling, and distinguishing waiting, expired, blocked, and completed escrows

proposals.user_asks: “Make this a private moment everywhere right now, and restore my exact workspace when I say I’m back.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently make one spoken privacy command cover the Mac display, browser capture/session, iPhone Mirroring, and the pendant's own audio behavior. A hive-level privacy mode would immediately stop screen/browser observation, pause queued remote work, mute or stop spoken output, and obscure sensitive windows; a later return command would restore the prior app/tab/session focus instead of leaving the workspace scrambled. This is a felt benefit when another person walks into the room, not another audit feature.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the short voice command and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic Mac/browser/iOS actions perform the privacy transition and restore snapshot; no expensive model is needed unless the prior workspace cannot be restored structurally.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 300 ms and apply local mute/visual concealment within 1 second. Complete cross-surface suspension within 3 seconds; restore only after an explicit return command.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero per invocation after implementation; at most one lightweight state snapshot. No cloud transcript or screenshot should be needed for the privacy transition.
proposals.security_concerns: The privacy command must be recognized locally or with a cached phrase when the relay is unreachable. It must fail closed for capture and speech, avoid persisting screenshots or page text, and make restoration opt-in rather than automatically reopening sensitive content.
missing: A pendant/relay emergency privacy state that takes precedence over active voice and queued jobs
Mac actions for atomic workspace snapshot, concealment, and restore, including browser and iPhone Mirroring state
Browser-extension and iOS hooks that suspend capture/automation and acknowledge the mode
A visible local indication that privacy mode is active even when the network is down

proposals.user_asks: “Find the thing I saw last week—search my signed-in browser, Mac files, and recent notes together, show me the evidence, and open the exact place it came from.”
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface is searched separately, so the owner has to remember whether a fact was in Safari, a downloaded file, or a local note. A unified personal retrieval action would search only sources the owner already authorized, rank matching claims, retain the source URL/path and timestamp, and let the Mac or browser reopen the exact source. The answer would be grounded in evidence rather than a model's unsupported recollection.
proposals.model_tier: Use local indexes and cheap embeddings/keyword search first; use gpt-5.6-luna only to interpret the natural-language query and reconcile candidates. Realtime is only the voice interface.
proposals.latency_budget: Return likely matches in 3 seconds and stream more candidates within 10 seconds. Opening a selected source should take under 5 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.01 for indexed retrieval; occasional embedding/index maintenance is the dominant background cost. Raw page content remains local to each source.
proposals.security_concerns: Search only explicitly permitted roots and current authenticated browser sessions; return evidence snippets with source metadata, not broad data dumps. Never index passwords, tokens, or private browser fields, and disclose when a result is only a weak match.
missing: A unified, permission-aware retrieval index spanning local files, browser provenance/findings, and notes
Connectors that emit stable source locators and freshness/deletion updates from each surface
A result schema carrying evidence, confidence, source kind, and an open/reveal action
Pendant-friendly disambiguation when several sources match

proposals.user_asks: When I say “finish this and tell me when it is truly done,” carry the request from the pendant through the relay to the Mac/browser, survive a disconnect, and come back with one spoken proof of what changed—or an exact failure and the recovery choice.
proposals.why_useful: Today a request can execute on the Mac yet leave the wearer unsure whether the browser action, local mutation, or relay acknowledgement actually completed. This gives the owner one dependable answer, including after walking away from the Mac or losing the pendant link.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to interpret the short spoken request and report the result; use the relay's background worker for supervision, receipts, and retry decisions.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge dispatch locally in under 500 ms; normal completion under 10 s; after link loss, resume/poll in the background and speak the proof on reconnection rather than burning realtime turns.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus cheap background polling; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per invocation, dominated by the initial voice turn, not polling.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must never claim success from a missing heartbeat. Browser claims need URL/title provenance, and destructive actions retain the existing owner confirmation policy. Send only action metadata and bounded result excerpts to the relay; do not export page contents or shell environment.
missing: A durable transaction record joining pendant turn ID, relay job, Mac job, action ledger, and browser provenance
A supervisor that closes/reconciles ledgers, distinguishes an interrupted step from a completed step, and resumes only replay-safe actions
A compact completion-proof event that the pendant can cache and read aloud offline

proposals.user_asks: I have both boards plugged into my Mac. Let me say “test the pendant” and get a spoken pass/fail: enumerate both USB devices, run a bounded dual-UART capture, exercise an audio loopback, and tell me which chip, clock, frame counter, or cable failed.
proposals.why_useful: The hardware is live but the granted serial diagnostic schema still cannot resolve, so the owner currently has to know scripts and inspect logs. This turns today's bench setup into a one-sentence truth test and catches the failure before blaming LTE, the relay, or the model.
proposals.model_tier: Use a deterministic local diagnostic runner for enumeration, UART framing, and loopback math; use the cheap background tier to summarize logs. Reserve realtime only for the final spoken sentence if the pendant is connected.
proposals.latency_budget: Return a local pass/fail in 5 s, with a 30 s ceiling for a full capture. Never leave a serial reader running after the test or open the microphone.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost when the deterministic report is used; under $0.01 for an optional spoken summary. Mac CPU and a few MB of rotating logs dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only device probes and synthetic loopback samples only. Do not upload raw UART logs or PCM by default; redact tokens and offer a local path plus hashes. The runner must use the two known device-path families and fail closed if a path changes rather than opening an arbitrary serial device.
missing: A real resolved bounded USB-serial diagnostic capability (the granted schema remains unresolved)
A host-side framing/parser for nRF9160 and ESP32 health counters
A synthetic 24 kHz loopback command and a report route consumable by the pendant
A cleanup watchdog for capture processes and rotation of bench logs

proposals.user_asks: When I put the pendant back on after being away, tell me only what changed because of me or needs my decision: which browser pages changed, which Mac jobs finished or failed, and which queued requests became stale. Let me ask “why?” and hear the causal timeline, not a generic morning brief.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can inspect jobs, browser sessions, and scheduled briefs separately, but cannot recover the meaning of an absence. This gives them a trustworthy re-entry point after a commute, sleep, or link outage without replaying every notification or pretending stale work succeeded.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic event correlation and timestamp/state comparison first; use a cheap background model to compress the resulting causal chains. Use realtime only for the owner's short spoken follow-up questions.
proposals.latency_budget: Prepare the absence delta in the background as soon as a link returns; first spoken answer within 2 seconds, with deeper “why?” explanations under 5 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: event indexing and state hashes dominate; roughly $0.005–$0.02 for an optional summary, with no model call when there are no meaningful changes.
proposals.security_concerns: Store hashes, timestamps, action outcomes, and provenance pointers rather than page contents or microphone audio. Browser page text remains behind the existing session boundary. Clearly label inferred causality versus directly observed events, and never turn an expired authorization into a new action.
missing: A durable cross-surface event timeline keyed by owner absence intervals and link epochs
Mac snapshots for foreground app, active browser tab, job state, and completion/failure transitions
Browser change cursors or page-watch diffs that expose meaningful changes without exporting whole pages
A relay-side causal correlator that marks stale, superseded, and externally changed work
A pendant query/result protocol for concise delta playback and follow-up why-chain retrieval

proposals.user_asks: If a logged-in browser task reaches a choice I need to make, read me a short decision packet on the pendant—what the page says, the safe options, and what each changes. Let me answer “option two,” then apply exactly that choice and read back the resulting page state.
proposals.why_useful: Today browser automation can read and click, but an owner away from the screen cannot participate in a consequential multi-option decision without asking for a vague click. This preserves the owner's judgment while making the browser, pendant, relay, and Mac act as one conversational workflow.
proposals.model_tier: Use the browser harness for structured extraction and page-state verification; use a cheap reasoning model to produce the bounded option packet. Realtime is reserved for the spoken choice and acknowledgement.
proposals.latency_budget: Extract and speak a packet in 3 seconds; apply the selected option within 5 seconds; if the page changed, invalidate the packet instead of acting on stale refs.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per decision, dominated by one short reasoning turn; browser inspection and state checks are local/relay work.
proposals.security_concerns: Send only the minimum fields needed to explain the choice. Bind the spoken answer to a page URL, session, snapshot hash, and short-lived nonce; reject it after navigation or content change. Preserve existing confirmation requirements for sending, purchasing, deleting, or other high-impact actions.
missing: A structured browser decision extractor that returns labeled options, consequences, and required fields rather than only refs
A pendant-sized decision-packet and answer protocol with nonce and snapshot binding
Browser result verification that proves the selected state changed as described
A relay correlation record joining spoken answer, browser command, and resulting provenance

proposals.user_asks: When I say “read the chart” on my pendant, inspect the chart or dashboard that is open in my logged-in browser, explain the important trend and any anomaly in plain speech, and let me ask for the exact values or a comparison without sending the page away from my Mac.
proposals.why_useful: Structured page reading is not enough for canvas charts, visual dashboards, and dense authenticated views. This lets the owner use information trapped behind the browser while preserving the browser session and keeping page contents local to the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Use a local Mac/browser capture and vision model for the chart; use a cheap summarizer for the spoken explanation. Realtime handles only the owner's follow-up question when low latency matters.
proposals.latency_budget: First spoken trend within 4 seconds; exact-value follow-up within 3 seconds; do not capture continuously—only on an explicit request.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.08 per chart request depending on image resolution and vision inference; no cost when the page has an accessible structured table.
proposals.security_concerns: The screenshot and extracted values stay on the Mac unless the owner explicitly asks for relay delivery. Redact unrelated browser regions, account identifiers, and neighboring tabs. Keep a provenance pointer to the URL and capture timestamp, not a permanent screenshot by default.
missing: A browser chart-understanding action that crops the relevant canvas or chart region and returns values/trends with confidence
Mac-local vision access to the authenticated browser surface without exposing unrelated tabs
A spoken follow-up protocol for exact values and comparisons tied to the same capture hash
A retention policy that deletes chart pixels after the answer while retaining optional derived claims

proposals.user_asks: “Continue the task that was running when the Mac or agent restarted, without doing any already-completed steps, and tell me exactly what resumed and what was skipped.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a restart leaves jobs permanently marked processing, cancellation cannot stop an active shell, and the ledger is never closed or joined to its job. This would make long Mac/browser workflows dependable rather than silently abandoned or dangerously repeated. It is the single most useful reliability capability: the owner can launch a real task and trust that a crash is an interruption, not an invisible loss or duplicate side effect.
proposals.model_tier: background for boot reconciliation and deterministic resume; realtime only to explain the resumed/skipped steps over the pendant
proposals.latency_budget: Reconcile within 5 seconds of local-agent boot; resume immediately after the owner asks or the configured policy permits it; spoken status under 2 seconds after querying
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for ledger reconciliation and idempotency; one short realtime response only when the owner asks. Dominant cost is durable local bookkeeping, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Resume only actions whose ledger replaySafety says safe and whose prior step is durably settled; never infer completion from a missing receipt. Persist a resume report locally and expose only the minimum command/output needed to the pendant. High-impact actions remain explicitly marked non-resumable and are reported as skipped.
missing: Boot-time reconciliation that marks processing jobs interrupted instead of leaving them immortal
orchestrator closeLedger on every terminal path and a real planMeta.jobId join
Pass an abort signal to exec/execFile so cancellation can actually terminate a child
Per-action idempotency enforcement wired to executionContext, plus a typed resume report

proposals.user_asks: “Send this exact authenticated webpage to my iPhone so I can continue there, preserving the page, selected text, and the reason I wanted it.”
proposals.why_useful: The browser has sessions the relay cannot reach and the iPhone has the owner's mobile context, but today the handoff between them is manual. A pendant request could capture the active Safari tab and selection, create a provenance-backed handoff artifact, then use Mac iPhone Mirroring to open/share it on the real phone. This is only possible by combining browser authority, Mac control, iOS control, and the always-available relay.
proposals.model_tier: background/cheap model to package title, URL, selection, and provenance; realtime only for the short confirmation and failure explanation
proposals.latency_budget: Capture and stage in under 3 seconds; phone handoff in under 10 seconds; if iPhone is unavailable, retain a queued handoff and tell the owner immediately
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one small model call for a concise handoff note; dominant work is browser command round-trips and iPhone Mirroring, not tokens
proposals.security_concerns: Never copy page body by default. Transfer URL, title, explicit selected text, and source/provenance record only; warn if the page is a sensitive authenticated host. Require the owner’s spoken confirmation only when the destination app or share target would expose content outside the device. Queue encrypted local metadata if the phone is offline.
missing: A typed browser export/handoff artifact route that accepts URL, selection, provenance ID, and destination
An iOS action for opening a URL or receiving a local handoff payload through the existing Mirroring harness
A relay command that binds one pendant utterance to the currently focused browser tab without guessing among tabs

proposals.user_asks: “That Mac action failed—diagnose the real cause, repair only the failed step, and finish the task without rerunning steps that already changed anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The current shell path flattens exit status, drops pid and environment provenance, and has no retry; a failure is often reported as an opaque string and the owner must start over. A failure-aware repair loop would inspect structured stderr/exit code and the durable action receipt, choose a safe correction (for example the missing project cwd or a transient browser host), and continue exactly from the failed step. It makes the Mac feel like an agent that recovers, not a command launcher.
proposals.model_tier: cheap model for classification and deterministic repair candidates; realtime only for ambiguous or irreversible repairs
proposals.latency_budget: Diagnosis under 1 second after failure; one bounded repair attempt within 10 seconds; stop and report rather than loop after a single unsuccessful repair
proposals.cost_estimate: One small inference only on failures; normal successful tasks cost nothing extra. Dominant cost is collecting bounded stderr and a second action execution.
proposals.security_concerns: Capture exit code, signal, pid, cwd, argv and a salted environment fingerprint—not secret environment values. Retry only the failed step with an idempotency key and never replay a settled mutation. Keep raw command output local; send a redacted failure capsule to the relay. Do not auto-repair destructive or externally visible actions.
missing: Structured shell receipts containing exit code/signal/pid and original-vs-rewritten action
Failure classifier and one-attempt repair planner wired to executionContext idempotency
A durable step cursor that distinguishes failed, settled, and unknown-after-crash states

proposals.user_asks: “Make this page safe to share with my colleague, show me exactly what was removed, and put the sanitized copy on my iPhone without sending anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The browser can reach authenticated content, while the Mac and iPhone can move it between surfaces, but the owner cannot currently ask the system to perform a privacy-preserving handoff. This would turn a risky copy/paste workflow into a reviewable transformation: identify secrets and personal data, produce a reversible redaction preview, and stage—not transmit—the result on the phone.
proposals.model_tier: background model for local redaction and classification; realtime only to read the short diff and ask for confirmation if confidence is low
proposals.latency_budget: Preview in under 8 seconds for a normal page; no external send until the owner explicitly confirms after seeing the diff
proposals.cost_estimate: One moderate model call over extracted claims rather than the whole page; browser and phone orchestration dominate latency
proposals.security_concerns: Process authenticated page contents locally where possible. Never upload the unsanitized page to the relay. Keep original and sanitized artifacts separate, attach source URL and redaction reasons, and require confirmation before any share/send action. Treat credentials, tokens, financial identifiers, and private names as high-sensitivity.
missing: A local structured redaction engine with deterministic detectors and confidence-scored model findings
A reviewable artifact/diff format that the iPhone harness can open without sending
A browser-to-Mac byte handoff for selected content with provenance and content sensitivity labels

proposals.user_asks: “At the end of the day, show me every change the hive made on my Mac, browser, and phone, with the before-and-after evidence, and let me undo only the changes I choose.”
proposals.why_useful: Today receipts, jobs, browser provenance, and phone actions are separate. The owner cannot get one trustworthy account of what the whole system changed, especially when several nodes acted in sequence. A cross-surface change ledger would make delegation safe to use daily: it would identify each mutation, show evidence of its result, and offer selective reversal rather than an all-or-nothing undo.
proposals.model_tier: background model to summarize and cluster completed receipts; deterministic code owns the ledger, evidence hashes, and undo routing
proposals.latency_budget: Continuously append receipts; daily digest generated in under 5 seconds and read in under 30 seconds; individual undo status under 2 seconds
proposals.cost_estimate: Small summarization call per digest; storage and evidence capture dominate cost, with no realtime inference required for normal use
proposals.security_concerns: Keep raw screenshots, page text, and phone content local. Store hashes, timestamps, actor surface, target, and reversible operation metadata in the relay-visible summary. Mark irreversible actions honestly and never fabricate a before-state. Selective undo must refuse when the target has changed since the original mutation.
missing: A shared cross-surface action identity and append-only change ledger
Before/after evidence adapters for Mac, browser, and iOS actions
Conflict-aware selective undo that checks current state before reversing a mutation
A pendant-readable digest and stale/irreversible-state vocabulary

proposals.user_asks: “Before you submit this form, verify every field against what I said, flag anything the website changed or inferred, and tell me the exact final payload.”
proposals.why_useful: Authenticated browser forms are where a small model mistake can become a real-world commitment. The owner can ask the system to fill fields today, but cannot obtain a semantic contract check between spoken intent, the rendered form, and the final submission payload. This capability would catch stale pages, hidden defaults, altered totals, and mismatched recipients before the irreversible click.
proposals.model_tier: background model for field-level comparison and anomaly explanation; realtime for the final spoken summary and explicit submit confirmation
proposals.latency_budget: Validation in under 3 seconds after the form is filled; final payload summary under 10 seconds for complex forms
proposals.cost_estimate: One small structured comparison call per submission; browser snapshots and DOM extraction dominate latency
proposals.security_concerns: Keep secrets and full field values local; send the relay only field labels, sensitivity classes, hashes, and mismatches. Never log passwords, payment numbers, or tokens. Treat submit as a separate action from fill and refuse to claim success until the browser reports the resulting state.
missing: A browser DOM/form serializer that captures visible, hidden, defaulted, and disabled fields with provenance
A spoken-intent-to-field schema with typed values and uncertainty rather than free text
A pre-submit transaction barrier that computes and presents the final payload before dispatch
Post-submit verification tied to the same form transaction

proposals.user_asks: When I ask “why didn't that work?”, give me one timeline from my button press through relay, Mac job, and USB device logs, and identify the first missing acknowledgement rather than making me repeat the story.
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface has a partial truth: the pendant knows a press, the relay knows a turn, the Mac knows a job, and the chips emit UART logs. A single causal answer would turn silent failures into an actionable diagnosis while the hardware is actually on the desk.
proposals.model_tier: background for timeline assembly and correlation; realtime only to summarize the already-built incident when the owner asks
proposals.latency_budget: Capture events continuously with sub-second append; answer in under 3 seconds from indexed records. Do not stream raw audio or UART indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing storage cost; one short background correlation invocation per incident, dominated by log parsing rather than model tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: UART may contain identifiers and Mac job output may contain sensitive paths or command text. Keep raw logs local, send only hashes, timestamps, state transitions, and redacted excerpts to relay; require explicit opt-in before including command stdout in a spoken answer.
missing: A correlation record carrying one turn/request ID across pendant event, relay delivery, Mac job, and serial capture
A bounded local UART capture/indexer that tags nRF9160 and ESP32 lines with monotonic timestamps
A read-only incident query and redaction layer

proposals.user_asks: Run a five-minute desk check and tell me whether the pendant, ESP32 audio bridge, Mac agent, and relay can complete a real speak-and-act turn, with the exact failing link and a copy-paste recovery command.
proposals.why_useful: The chips are physically connected now but not LTE-registered. A bounded bench test can validate the USB reality without pretending it proves wearable operation, preventing hours of debugging the wrong layer before I wear it.
proposals.model_tier: cheap background model for deterministic checks and parsing; escalate to realtime only if the owner is simultaneously speaking to the pendant
proposals.latency_budget: Start within 2 seconds, finish within 5 minutes, with progress after each phase: enumerate, UART health, audio loopback, authenticated relay round trip, cleanup.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost if implemented as a fixed state machine; one short summarization call only on failure. Storage is capped, timestamped diagnostics under 1 MB per run.
proposals.security_concerns: Never upload raw microphone/audio or unrestricted UART. Use generated tones and synthetic text, redact bearer tokens and paths, and make relay execution a separate explicit phase because the device is not LTE-registered.
missing: A real host serial runner and framing parser (the granted schema is unresolved; current workaround is existing dual-chip capture scripts through run_shell)
A generated-tone audio loopback assertion between ESP32 and pendant
A test-only relay echo endpoint and a cleanup/rollback phase
A single structured bench report route

proposals.user_asks: When I say “I have to go,” freeze the thing we were doing into a resumable handoff: save the exact conversation turn, browser page and form state, Mac project/window context, pending actions, and what still needs my decision; later I can press the pendant and hear the shortest truthful resume briefing before continuing.
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped conversation or a sudden interruption loses the owner's place across bodies. This would make the system feel continuous rather than like several unrelated assistants, especially when the owner is moving away from the Mac or the link disappears.
proposals.model_tier: cheap background model to compress the handoff and extract unresolved decisions; realtime only for the spoken resume briefing
proposals.latency_budget: Capture a durable handoff in under 2 seconds after the phrase or button event; resume briefing under 1 second from cached state. Browser/Mac restoration may take up to 10 seconds and must report each unavailable surface honestly.
proposals.cost_estimate: One short summarization call per handoff, usually a few cents or less; storage is compact metadata plus references, not screenshots or audio by default.
proposals.security_concerns: A handoff may contain authenticated URLs, draft text, or private conversation content. Keep sensitive page contents and screenshots local, encrypt the handoff store, expire stale browser credentials and drafts, and require an explicit physical button press before reopening or submitting anything.
missing: A first-class resumable-handoff object with immutable source references, unresolved-decision fields, expiry, and partial-availability status
A browser freeze/restore primitive that preserves a tab plus unsent form state without submitting it
A Mac context checkpoint and restore operation for project, window, and focused document
Pendant-side indexing of handoff IDs and a compact offline spoken summary
A cross-surface resume transaction that can restore in dependency order and never claim a step succeeded merely because the checkpoint existed

proposals.user_asks: Keep working on a multi-step task even when my Mac sleeps or disconnects: pause at a verified checkpoint, let the relay wait or do only safe cloud work, then resume on the Mac exactly where it stopped and tell me what changed while it was away.
proposals.why_useful: Today a laptop disconnect turns an ongoing task into an ambiguous failure. The pendant and relay can remain present, but they cannot hand a partially completed browser/Mac workflow back and forth with a truthful checkpoint.
proposals.model_tier: background model for checkpoint validation and plan compression; realtime only when the owner asks for a live status or gives a new instruction
proposals.latency_budget: Checkpoint after every externally visible step in under 500 ms; detect Mac loss within 10 seconds; resume within 5 seconds of reconnecting, with spoken status if the owner is wearing the pendant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: durable state-machine records dominate; model calls only when compressing a long plan or resolving a changed page. No continuous realtime inference while paused.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must not replay Mac-local mutations or browser submissions without the Mac's fresh attestation. Encrypt checkpoints, expire authenticated browser references, and distinguish verified completion from merely dispatched work. Owner must be able to discard a paused task from the pendant.
missing: A portable checkpoint format containing step preconditions, observed postconditions, idempotency keys, and a safe-to-run-on-relay classification
Mac reconnect handshake that reports which checkpoint side effects actually occurred
Relay-side dormant task storage and wake notification, without pretending it can access Mac-only sessions
Browser action resume that revalidates URL/page identity before continuing
Pendant controls for pause, discard, and truthful progress summaries

proposals.user_asks: When a website asks for a one-time code, let me say “use the latest code” to the pendant; read the matching message from my real iPhone through Mac mirroring, fill only the waiting browser field, and erase the code from every transcript and log afterward.
proposals.why_useful: This is a daily moment where the owner must shuttle a code between devices. The browser session, real phone, Mac control, and wearable voice are each present but cannot perform this narrowly scoped handoff without exposing the secret to ordinary history.
proposals.model_tier: deterministic extraction first; a small model only to identify the currently focused OTP field and match the newest message. No realtime model is needed unless the owner is speaking live.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds from the spoken request; fail closed if there are multiple plausible codes, the browser target changed, or the message is older than a configurable window.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero per use with local OCR/accessibility and structured DOM; occasional small-model extraction costs cents at most.
proposals.security_concerns: The code is a high-sensitivity ephemeral secret. Keep it in memory only, never send it to the relay or LLM, never place it in Mac shell history, redact action receipts and screenshots, verify the exact origin and focused field, and require a physical press if confidence is not unambiguous. Delete the value immediately after submit or timeout.
missing: A local-only iOS message reader over the existing Mac iPhone Mirroring surface
Browser-side OTP-field identity and origin binding
An in-memory secret channel between iOS reader and browser executor with zero durable plaintext
A scrubber that guarantees OTP values do not enter speech transcripts, job records, screenshots, or model context

changes.change: Add a cross-layer 24 kHz audio conformance/loopback harness. The Mac bridge emits a short marked PCM/Opus test burst; relay and pendant preserve a correlation ID plus declared sample rate, codec, frame duration, byte count, and timestamps at capture/upload/decode/playback. The pendant returns periodic counters (underruns, overruns, resampler ratio, dropped frames, CRC) via existing pipeline telemetry. A CI/live diagnostic compares the declared and measured rates and fails loudly on any implicit 15.625/31.25/44.1 kHz conversion. Keep the current 24 kHz TTS output but make the capture and ESP32 bridge mismatch explicit until they are migrated.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets speech that sounds consistently natural instead of discovering weeks later that capture is 15.625 kHz and the bridge silently converts through 31.25/44.1 kHz. When audio breaks, the pendant can say which hop lost samples, rather than requiring UART archaeology.
changes.effort: Medium: shared telemetry schema in relay/Mac bridge, a small nRF9160 counter packet, ESP32 instrumentation, and a host loopback test. No new pendant peripheral; use the existing full-duplex I2S and pipeline event path.
changes.risk: Telemetry overhead and test bursts could contend with live audio; gate tests to explicit diagnostics and keep counters compact. A false alarm from clock drift is recovered by thresholding over a full burst and reporting raw counters. No audio payload needs to leave the owner's devices beyond the existing relay path.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small diagnostic burst and a few hundred bytes of telemetry. Firmware RAM under ~8 KiB for counters/ring metadata if kept out of the audio buffers.
changes.latency_impact: No live-path latency change; diagnostic mode adds one test-burst round trip, roughly under a second on LTE.
changes.security_impact: Correlation IDs and aggregate counters only; do not persist microphone samples. Mark diagnostic payloads separately from owner audio and expire them quickly.
depends_on: A canonical audio telemetry schema shared by relay, Mac bridge, nRF9160, and ESP32
A firmware build/test runner or connected-device test target
A documented migration plan for 24 kHz capture and the ESP32 A2DP 44.1 kHz limitation

changes.change: Replace the prototype HUZZAH32 bridge's 31.25→44.1 kHz path with a production Bluetooth-audio bridge that runs one explicit 24→48 kHz conversion (or 24→44.1 only at the final A2DP boundary), has hardware I2S clocking, and exposes underrun/clock telemetry. Keep the nRF9160's 24 kHz PCM/Opus contract across LTE; the bridge should not pretend A2DP can carry 24 kHz—A2DP remains a 44.1/48 kHz headphone boundary.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner hears clean, stable responses and recordings instead of audio whose pitch/latency changes when the current development bridge's 31.25 kHz clock and 44.1 kHz SBC path drift. It also makes 24 kHz quality real through the network while honestly handling the unavoidable headphone conversion once.
changes.effort: Medium hardware redesign: select a Bluetooth-audio SoC/module with documented 48 kHz I2S and source profile, add clocked I2S and power/charging, port the existing bridge protocol, then certify with the conformance harness.
changes.risk: Headphone interoperability may force 44.1 kHz fallback; retain both 44.1/48 profiles and a deterministic resampler. Module replacement can introduce pairing regressions; recover with the existing ESP32 bridge during bring-up. Physical redesign is required because the HUZZAH32 prototype is not a shippable product.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype module/BOM roughly $15–$40 plus board work; production power target under ~100 mA active, versus the current ESP32 board's higher dev-board draw. No meaningful per-call API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Removes one unnecessary resampling stage and should reduce jitter; conversion itself adds under 2 ms with a bounded small buffer.
changes.security_impact: Audio remains local between pendant and headphones after relay delivery; pairing keys must be stored in protected flash and diagnostic telemetry must exclude samples.
depends_on: Cross-layer audio conformance telemetry
A product decision whether headphones remain A2DP or move to LE Audio
A validated 24 kHz capture/Opus profile on the nRF9160

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution lease and handoff journal. Every voice goal becomes a durable intent envelope with owner-visible goalId, required capabilities (for example authenticated Safari versus public web), preferred executor, lease expiry, and a resumable step cursor. The relay publishes heartbeats for pendant reachability; the Mac agent publishes local-agent and browser-extension reachability; the browser bridge publishes tab/session leases. If the chosen executor disappears, the relay does not blindly retry: it records the exact unavailable dependency, keeps the envelope pending, and on reconnect resumes from the last completed receipt. For public work it may hand off to Browser Run; for private work it waits for Safari and says so on the pendant. Emit a one-line spoken status when a lease is lost or recovered, plus a dashboard timeline linking each handoff to existing action receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request such as “check this logged-in page and prepare a draft” will survive leaving the Mac, a sleeping laptop, or a temporarily offline extension without duplicate clicks or a mysterious failure. The owner hears whether it is waiting for their private browser, has moved to the server, or completed, and can resume from the pendant rather than starting over.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared envelope schema and D1/local durable stores, heartbeat endpoints, lease expiry/reconciliation, Browser Run eligibility routing, browser tab reattachment, and pendant status events. Reuse existing action IDs, receipts, journal, and routing stats; add fault-injection tests for Mac sleep, extension disconnect, relay restart, and duplicate reconnect.
changes.risk: A stale lease could cause duplicate work or two executors to act concurrently; require idempotency-key ownership and fencing tokens, with reconciliation preferring the receipt already persisted. A handoff must never move authenticated page data to Browser Run; capability requirements must mark private-session-only. Recovery is to inspect the journal and cancel or resume the envelope.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible when idle (heartbeat traffic and D1 writes); roughly 1–3 extra small model calls only when routing ambiguity or reconciliation needs semantic judgment. LTE status messages are tiny; no page contents leave the Mac unless the existing browser policy permits it.
changes.latency_impact: No added latency for direct online execution beyond one local envelope write. Failure recovery adds seconds for heartbeat detection and extension reconnection; spoken status can be immediate from the relay.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and prevents cross-executor replay, but introduces durable metadata about goals and session availability. Store only capability labels and opaque session/tab IDs in the relay; keep URLs and authenticated evidence on the Mac unless explicitly returned.
depends_on: The existing actionReceipts/idempotency implementation (chg-5fc73ce3)
A resumable browser queue with progress polling (the unimplemented portion of chg-14accc01)
A relay-to-Mac heartbeat/lease endpoint and a pendant status-event path
Explicit private-session-only versus public-web capability metadata

changes.change: Give the production pendant a deliberate privacy-presence control: a capacitive skin/contact or proximity sensor plus a long-press gesture, backed by a small secure-state flag. When the owner removes the pendant or long-presses, it emits a signed privacy event; the relay immediately suppresses spoken/private content, the Mac agent locks or obscures designated sensitive windows and pauses browser extraction, and the dashboard shows the fleet in privacy mode. Re-presence plus an explicit short press restores the prior task without discarding its cursor or receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could walk into a meeting, hand the Mac to someone, or simply take off the pendant and know that private browser findings and spoken answers stop everywhere—not just on the device. Returning does not force them to restart a long-running task.
changes.effort: New pendant enclosure/sensor and firmware event, secure event signing, relay fleet privacy state with replay protection, Mac window/privacy adapter, browser extraction pause/resume, and dashboard status. Design the event as fail-safe for content delivery but never as a destructive computer lock; test removal, LTE loss, relay restart, and accidental sensor contact.
changes.risk: A false removal could interrupt audio or pause work; debounce and require a configurable hold time, while preserving the task state. A lost or dead pendant must not leave the Mac permanently locked—privacy state expires conservatively and can be cleared in the dashboard or by a local explicit action. Window hiding is platform-specific and must not claim success without a receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$6 added BOM for a contact/proximity sensor, glue/enclosure changes, and a few milliwatts only while sensing; negligible API cost beyond one small fleet event and receipts per transition.
changes.latency_impact: Local sensor-to-relay event target under 1 second when connected; on LTE loss, the pendant can immediately stop its own playback and mark the Mac state unknown. Restoration waits for authenticated presence and a heartbeat, typically a few seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making absence a signed, fleet-wide signal. Do not send microphone audio or page contents with the event. Use a hardware-backed device key and monotonic event counter so an intercepted old 'present' event cannot undo privacy mode.
depends_on: A hardware-backed pendant identity and signed event channel
A relay-wide privacy-state protocol understood by Mac and browser nodes
Typed Mac/browser privacy actions with truthful receipts
A production enclosure with a reliable skin/contact or proximity sensor

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface execution trace and continuation ledger. The pendant/relay assigns a traceId and intentId at utterance time; every relay dispatch, Mac job, shell command, browser command, retry, and result receipt carries that ID. Persist a compact append-only event record on the Mac and relay (with payload redaction and a 30-day TTL), reconcile duplicate/out-of-order events by idempotency key, and expose one GET /continuations/:traceId plus a relay push topic. When the pendant reconnects, it receives a concise status (running, waiting for Mac/browser, completed, failed with next retry time) rather than losing the task. Add a background reconciler that marks stale leases, retries only retry-safe operations, and emits a human-readable completion/failure receipt. This is deliberately observability and recovery only: it does not gate or refuse any FULL_CONTROL action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner says “do this” and walks away or the pendant link drops, they can later ask “what happened?” and get one trustworthy answer spanning shell, Safari, Mac, and relay—not a partial job list. Failures become actionable (“browser was offline; resumed at 9:14”) instead of silent or duplicated work, and repeated retries stop rerunning completed steps.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared trace schema and propagation in relay, executor, browserBridge, and jobTracker; small durable event store and reconciler; dashboard/pendant status view; integration tests for disconnect, restart, duplicate, and out-of-order delivery.
changes.risk: Trace records could leak URLs, shell commands, or private snippets; redact arguments and store hashes/metadata by default, encrypt relay records, and make detailed evidence opt-in. Reconciliation bugs could duplicate mutations, so only actions already declared idempotent/retry-safe are auto-retried; all others are reported as needing continuation, never replayed automatically. Recover by disabling the reconciler while retaining raw receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic ID/event handling and a cheaper background reconciler; roughly 1–3 KB of metadata per action before retention, with relay storage and dashboard reads dominating rather than model tokens.
changes.latency_impact: No added latency on the first action beyond generating an ID and one local append (<10 ms target). Reconnect status is immediate from persisted state; background reconciliation may add seconds only after failures.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding authority. Use scoped trace tokens, redact command text/DOM content and credentials, encrypt relay-at-rest data, and enforce owner-device pairing for continuation queries. Never expose raw shell/environment values in pendant speech.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 (implemented per-action receipts)
relay durable state and paired-device identity
chg-14accc01's resumable browser queue or equivalent lease API
a stable Mac job lifecycle event hook

changes.change: Add a cross-node execution ledger and recovery coordinator above the existing Mac job store and browser command queue. Each workflow is a versioned DAG whose steps carry an idempotency key, device/session affinity, precondition fingerprint, receipt links, retry budget, and an explicit outcome enum (succeeded, failed-before-effect, failed-after-effect, or unknown). The relay owns the durable ledger and leases; Mac and browser agents atomically claim steps, report heartbeats, and expose a read-only reconciliation operation. On reconnect, reconcile unknown steps from local receipts/page state before retrying. Render one compact pendant/dashboard timeline rather than separate Mac and browser histories.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A lost connection will no longer force the owner to guess whether an order lookup, file operation, or draft was already done. Long tasks can resume safely across sleep, browser restarts, and relay reconnects without duplicate side effects.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new relay D1 schema and coordinator, adapters in jobTracker/browser bridge, reconciliation handlers, and dashboard timeline; staged rollout can start with read-only workflows and simulated disconnect tests.
changes.risk: A faulty reconciliation rule could classify an effect incorrectly or retry a non-idempotent action. Default unknown to paused, preserve all raw receipts, and provide operator replay/repair tooling; do not delete existing job history.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible steady-state storage and request overhead; roughly one small D1 write per transition/heartbeat. Background model cost only for ambiguous human-readable recovery summaries.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds to normal step dispatch; reconnect recovery is bounded by heartbeat plus one reconciliation round, typically under 30 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Ledger contains sensitive URLs, snippets, and local paths, so encrypt sensitive fields, scope records to the paired owner, and apply existing audio/job retention. It must not become a new channel for raw page contents.
depends_on: Existing Mac action receipts and browser command IDs must be exposed as stable references
Relay↔Mac authentication and pairing already present
A typed, read-only reconciliation endpoint on both Mac and browser surfaces
Dashboard and pendant status rendering for paused/unknown steps

changes.change: Add a local execution preflight and result normalizer that runs before arbitrary shell actions without blocking them: resolve the project/workspace from known roots and recent successful cwd values, snapshot PATH/tool availability and relevant app permissions, classify the command's expected output shape, and attach exit code, signal, duration, cwd, redacted environment/tool versions, stdout/stderr byte counts plus bounded tail, and an undoability hint to the existing receipt. For failures, automatically suggest one deterministic retry (for example corrected cwd, missing executable path, or expired GUI session) and record whether the retry was attempted.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent will stop wasting turns hunting for the project or asking the same status question, and spoken results will say whether a command failed before doing anything, ran successfully with noisy output, or needs a Mac permission/session repair.
changes.effort: Medium: a preflight module, receipt schema extension, workspace index, and tests against the already-proven pmset/scutil/df/git/osascript commands.
changes.risk: Capturing environment or output tails could leak secrets; redact known token/password patterns, never persist full environment, cap output, and let the owner disable command-output retention. A bad automatic retry could repeat a mutation, so only retry commands classified as read-only or explicitly idempotent.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; one local process and small receipt metadata per action. Saves planner tokens and repeated failed commands.
changes.latency_impact: Usually 10–100 ms for cached facts; skip expensive scans when a matching cwd/tool fingerprint is fresh.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding gates or narrowing FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Store receipts locally, send only summaries to relay, and preserve existing unrestricted execution policy.
depends_on: Stable action receipts and journal endpoints (now present)
A local workspace/cwd index with bounded retention
Output redaction and receipt-size limits

changes.change: Create an owner-visible causal provenance graph for every multi-surface request. At planning time, record the request version, selected surfaces, facts actually used (with freshness and confidence), routing decisions, model tier, generated action arguments, device/session identity, data sent off-device, and each resulting receipt. At completion, materialize a signed, compact explanation with links between cause and effect, including discarded alternatives and the exact uncertainty that caused a pause or fallback. Expose it as a pendant-sized spoken answer and an expandable Mac dashboard view; allow the owner to correct a fact or revoke a provenance edge without deleting the underlying execution receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant says something was done—or failed—the owner can ask “why did you use Safari instead of the Mac, what did you rely on, and what left my computer?” and receive a trustworthy answer grounded in the actual run, not a reconstructed model story. This makes a multi-device personal agent understandable enough to delegate consequential work to it.
changes.effort: High: define a versioned provenance schema, instrument planner/routing/relay/Mac/browser boundaries, sign and retain append-only edges, build redaction and sensitivity handling, and add spoken plus dashboard renderers.
changes.risk: Provenance can expose private page text, file paths, or credentials and can become misleading if agents write free-form explanations. Store references and hashes by default, redact sensitive values, separate observed facts from inferences, and generate explanations only from recorded edges. Preserve raw receipts if the owner edits or revokes a displayed edge.
changes.cost_impact: Small local/relay storage and serialization overhead per step; no extra model call for the graph. A cheap background model may summarize a large graph, while realtime only reads a precomputed short explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible dispatch overhead (structured edge writes); explanation retrieval should be sub-second for normal jobs and under a few seconds for long workflows.
changes.security_impact: Adds an auditable record of data movement, but increases the sensitivity of retained metadata. Encrypt the graph, scope it to the paired owner, apply field-level TTLs, and never include raw secrets in relay payloads or speech.
depends_on: Stable cross-surface request and step IDs across relay, Mac, and browser
Existing Mac job/action receipts and browser command receipts
A durable owner-scoped store with append-only integrity checks
A dashboard/pendant renderer that distinguishes observed evidence from inferred explanation

changes.change: Add a fail-fast preflight and reconciliation layer before browser actions are dispatched. The Mac bridge publishes a signed capability heartbeat (extension online, session/tab identity, queue depth, last-seen age); the relay planner converts an offline or stale heartbeat into a waiting dependency instead of sending the action. On reconnect, reconcile each queued command by requestId/idempotencyKey against browser receipts, mark completed commands, and execute only unacknowledged steps. Emit blocked/resumed/expired events to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request will no longer burn 45 seconds and end in a generic browser-offline failure. The owner hears that the Mac portion is continuing, gets a precise recovery instruction, and the browser portion resumes safely after Safari is available without duplicate clicks or submissions.
changes.effort: Medium-high: bridge heartbeat and reconciliation protocol, relay durable dependency state, planner integration, pendant event plumbing, and tests for disconnects during navigation and submit.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could cause either unnecessary waiting or duplicate execution. Use short leases, monotonic command sequence numbers, idempotency keys, and receipt reconciliation; expire commands with an explicit explanation rather than guessing. Roll back by treating the runner as fail-fast as it is now.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/relay storage and heartbeat traffic; no additional model calls for retries. One background summarization call only when status needs natural-language explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms preflight when healthy; avoids the current ~45 s timeout when offline. Reconnect latency is heartbeat interval plus one reconciliation round.
changes.security_impact: Heartbeat carries capability/session metadata, never page text or credentials. Bind commands to authenticated extension ID plus tab/session lease; reject commands whose lease or idempotency scope has changed.
depends_on: Shared typed capability snapshot between Mac bridge and relay
Durable job dependency/receipt schema
Browser command request IDs and tab/session affinity (the still-open browser reliability change)

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution health and recovery coordinator. Before dispatch, relay polls a compact Mac-agent capability lease (agent reachable, browser bridge online, accessibility/screen-recording state, pending-job count, supported action families) and chooses Mac shell, typed Mac action, browser bridge, or durable queue accordingly. Every dispatched step carries a jobId, idempotency key, checkpoint, and deadline; failures are normalized into transient (retry/backoff), unavailable (park until a health transition), or permanent (surface-specific explanation). On reconnect, resume only from the last acknowledged checkpoint and publish one signed result receipt containing attempted route, exact failure, retry history, and final state. This is observability/recovery, not an approval gate; FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say one thing and leave. Instead of silently spending 45 seconds on a browser action while the extension is offline, the system immediately says what is unavailable, parks the work, resumes when Safari or the Mac returns, and avoids duplicate shell/browser mutations after a dropped link.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a small health lease endpoint and typed state schema in local-agent, relay-side coordinator and durable queue, idempotent checkpoint persistence, and unified spoken/result formatting. Existing /ops/snapshot, /browser/status, /jobs, receipts, and journal provide most inputs.
changes.risk: A stale lease could select the wrong route or retry a non-idempotent action. Leases need short TTLs, action idempotency classes, and an explicit 'unknown outcome' state that never retries automatically. Recovery is replayed from receipts and can be manually abandoned; no existing execution path is removed.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost: deterministic health checks and retry logic; only final explanation needs background/planner inference. Small D1/R2 or local job-store growth for checkpoints and receipts.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for cached health; avoids long doomed attempts (currently an offline browser navigate took about 45 seconds). Reconnect work is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Health leases must omit page content and secrets, authenticate Mac↔relay, bind results to jobId/idempotency key, and redact command env/stderr before relay storage. Existing unrestricted shell authority is preserved.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface job identity/idempotency schema
Local-agent read-only health snapshot with stable machine-readable fields
Relay-to-Mac authenticated callback or polling for parked-job wakeups

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution ledger and recovery coordinator. Every delegated plan gets a durable job/step DAG with stable step IDs, parent/child dependencies, attempt records, start/end timestamps, command or browser action fingerprints, exit/HTTP/UI outcomes, touched-resource summaries, and a monotonic receipt chain. The Mac shell adapter records argv-equivalent parsing when possible but preserves the original command string, cwd, environment-difference hash, stdout/stderr size plus redacted excerpts, signal/timeout, and resource probes. A classifier labels failures as retryable, session/device unavailable, failed-before-effect, effect-uncertain, or irreversible. Recovery policies are declarative: retry only steps marked idempotent or proven to have failed before effect; otherwise stop downstream dependents, preserve the evidence, and create a resume token. Browser steps use tab/session affinity and page fingerprints; Mac steps use receipt snapshots and existing undo metadata. A relay worker polls/pushes state, and the pendant receives only a compact status plus job ID. Dashboard exposes 'resume from step', 'retry failed step', and 'show evidence', while retaining the owner's no-gate maximum-access policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A failed overnight task will no longer force the owner to rerun a whole workflow or wonder whether an email/form/file change already happened. They get an honest stopping point, automatic safe continuation, and a single resume action that avoids duplicate side effects.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new durable schema/worker, adapters in executor.js and browser bridge, failure classifier, relay notification, dashboard state view, and integration tests for timeout, disconnect, duplicate delivery, and uncertain side effects.
changes.risk: A classifier could wrongly call a step retryable and duplicate an external effect, or a stale browser session could produce misleading evidence. Default uncertain states to stop (not block owner actions), require explicit idempotency declarations for automatic retries, and preserve raw receipts for forensic review. If the coordinator dies, the existing executor and receipts continue operating; recovery can be manual.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2/storage and polling cost; approximately $0.001–$0.01 per job for ledger writes and background classification, plus occasional vision/model retries. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible overhead per action (one local ledger write, generally <50 ms); recovery reports arrive asynchronously. Durable writes may add modest latency before acknowledging a multi-step job.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without reducing capability: raw shell commands and private browser data stay on the Mac/local-agent boundary, while relay/dashboard receive typed summaries and redacted evidence. Encrypt ledger at rest, limit job visibility to the owner's identity, and expire raw stdout/page excerpts separately from durable step metadata.
depends_on: The existing actionReceipts.js result/undo integration and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts.
The browser request-ID/session-affinity work already present in browserBridge.js/browserSessions.js.
A durable backend job runner and authenticated relay-to-Mac job status channel, which are still absent.

changes.change: Add a first-class encrypted Work Handoff Bundle protocol. At pack time, Mac-planner asks local Mac and browser adapters for typed state records (window/app identity, file path plus content hash, terminal cwd and job ID, browser tab/session ID plus URL/title and redacted anchor hashes, draft identifiers, and the current goal). A local model compiles these into an ordered task graph with 'safe to restore', 'needs revalidation', and 'reference only' classifications; private bodies remain local and the relay stores only encrypted manifests and short-lived opaque pointers. The pendant receives a compact spoken index. On resume, the target Mac requests each record, revalidates hashes/session ownership, restores tabs/windows/focus where possible, and reports omissions instead of fabricating continuity; from the pendant, the owner can ask for any thread and get its next concrete step. Add expiry, per-record deletion, and a provenance trail for every restored item.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave a complicated task without losing their place or leaving a vulnerable Mac session open. Returning later—or asking from the pendant—restores the actual working context and tells them honestly what changed while they were away.
changes.effort: Medium-high: local state collectors and restore adapters, encrypted manifest storage, redaction/sensitivity rules, browser and terminal identity hooks, and end-to-end interruption/resume tests.
changes.risk: Some applications cannot restore state safely, browser pages can change, and stale file hashes may make a restoration misleading. Treat each item independently, require revalidation before opening or editing changed resources, preserve the original snapshot for comparison, and degrade to a spoken summary rather than claiming success. If bundle storage fails, leave the live Mac session untouched.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring storage and encryption overhead; roughly $0.002–$0.02 per bundle plus occasional model summarization. No pendant hardware change required.
changes.latency_impact: Packing adds local collection time (typically seconds); restoration is asynchronous after the initial acknowledgement and should not block the pendant conversation.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy over sending whole desktop/browser snapshots to the relay by keeping sensitive payloads local and expiring encrypted manifests. Requires strict owner identity binding, no cookie/token export, and audit/delete controls for every bundle.
depends_on: A durable relay job/storage facility with authenticated owner binding.
Browser tab/session affinity and typed results from the existing browser bridge.
Mac action receipts and local-agent observability for terminal jobs and app state.
A pendant/relay protocol for retrieving compact handoff summaries.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface browser availability supervisor. The relay/mac agent records extension heartbeats and a short-lived capability lease; before dispatching any browser action, the Mac performs a cheap local health read. If the lease is stale, fail the action immediately (not after the current ~45-second browser timeout), classify it as 'device unavailable' rather than action failure, retain the idempotent job in a dead-letter/waiting state, and notify the pendant. When a fresh Safari bridge heartbeat arrives, resume only unstarted action IDs and send one completion/failure receipt. Include outage start, last heartbeat, retry count, and the exact reattachment instruction in the spoken status.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request made from the pendant will no longer burn nearly a minute per browser step or look like the account/site is broken when Safari is simply closed or the extension is offline. The owner gets a truthful spoken 'waiting for Safari' status and automatic continuation when the Mac/browser comes back, without duplicate form submissions or repeated navigation.
changes.effort: Medium: add lease/heartbeat state to the Mac bridge, a preflight in browser dispatch, a waiting/dead-letter job state with idempotent resume, relay event propagation, and pendant notification copy; test crash/reconnect and stale command cleanup.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat could delay a healthy but briefly reconnecting bridge; use a short preflight timeout and explicit manual retry. A reconnect during a step could create ambiguity, so resume only after receipt says the step never started or the action ID is safely idempotent. Keep pending commands bounded and expire them with a visible reason.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost: deterministic health checks and event forwarding; one small D1/SQLite state record per lease/job. Saves expensive planner retries and 45-second local timeouts.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy browser actions gain only a few milliseconds for the local preflight; offline actions return in under a second instead of ~45 seconds and reconnect jobs resume on the next heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: No page contents or cookies leave the Mac. Heartbeats carry extension ID, capability state, and timestamps only; bind leases to the paired device and never treat a heartbeat as authorization to submit a pending irreversible action.
depends_on: A browser bridge heartbeat endpoint that reports online/offline and pending-command ownership
Durable action IDs/receipts already implemented in the Mac harness
Relay-to-pendant job status events and a waiting/resume state in the job tracker

changes.change: Add a shell execution envelope and recovery record around every run_shell invocation without changing the owner's unrestricted FULL_CONTROL policy. Persist command text plus SHA-256, resolved cwd, start/end monotonic times, timeout, exit code/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts and bounded tails, environment fingerprint (names and hashes only), and whether the process spawned children. For failures, deterministically classify timeout, missing executable, permission, nonzero exit, and transport crash; attach a suggested retry strategy and allow the planner to retry only transient classes with a fresh job/action ID while linking attempts under one parent operation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac task fails, the agent can say what actually happened—wrong directory, missing tool, timeout, or a command error—and recover from transient failures instead of blindly repeating or asking the owner to diagnose. The owner can audit exactly what ran without dumping secrets such as tokens or full environment variables.
changes.effort: Medium: wrap computerControl.runShell's child-process result, redact/size-limit output, add parent/attempt links to existing receipts and journal, implement deterministic failure taxonomy and bounded retry policy, and expose a concise dashboard/pendant completion receipt.
changes.risk: Output can contain secrets; redact known token/key/password patterns and store only bounded tails with configurable retention. Retrying arbitrary shell is not always safe, so default automatic retry only for process launch/transport/timeouts when the command is marked retry-safe; otherwise report a one-click/manual retry. Child-process accounting is platform-specific and may be unavailable for some commands.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost; a few KB of local journal storage per attempt with retention cleanup. Avoids planner calls for straightforward diagnosis and transient recovery.
changes.latency_impact: A few milliseconds of wrapper overhead; transient retry adds bounded delay only when needed. Failure reporting becomes immediate and structured rather than requiring another low-latency model turn.
changes.security_impact: Preserves unrestricted execution and no approval gates. Store command/output locally with permissions, hash the command for correlation, redact environment values, and send only the summary/error class to relay unless the owner explicitly requests diagnostic details.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /journal observability
A bounded local retention policy for shell transcripts
A planner/executor contract that marks an action retry-safe without blocking other actions

changes.change: Add a shell execution flight recorder and failure-recovery loop without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: record command hash, exact argv/string, cwd, selected environment names (not values), start/end timestamps, exit/signal, stdout/stderr byte counts plus capped tails, and host resource snapshot; on timeout/nonzero exit, automatically run a small fixed diagnostic bundle (cwd, disk, network, process, permissions), classify the failure, and retry only when the planner marks the command idempotent. Store a content-addressed compressed transcript linked to the existing receipt and expose a single job timeline in /jobs/:id and the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task fails, the agent can explain whether it was a bad path, missing permission, timeout, or unavailable network and recover instead of asking the owner to repeat it. The owner gets a trustworthy answer about what ran, while retaining the deliberately unrestricted capability.
changes.effort: Medium: executor instrumentation, bounded transcript storage/redaction, typed failure schema, retry metadata, and dashboard timeline; no shell-policy change.
changes.risk: Command output can contain secrets and large logs; redact common credential patterns, cap output, encrypt or short-retain transcripts, and allow deletion. Automatic retries could duplicate side effects, so retries are opt-in per command and disabled after ambiguous termination. Recovery is to fall back to the current one-shot executor.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and CPU overhead per job; roughly cents per GB-month for retained compressed logs. Diagnostic commands add negligible local cost and avoid repeated expensive model turns.
changes.latency_impact: Successful commands gain only milliseconds; failed commands take a few seconds for diagnostics and optional retry, while the owner receives an immediate queued/running status.
changes.security_impact: Improves accountability without gates. Do not persist full environment values, stdin, or unrestricted page contents; hash/redact sensitive fields and make transcript access follow existing Mac-agent auth.
depends_on: Existing job receipts and /jobs/:jobId lifecycle
A bounded local transcript store and authenticated observability endpoint
Planner support for explicit idempotent=true retry intent

changes.change: Create an ephemeral 'active-context capsule' protocol shared by Mac agent and browser extension. On request, the Mac issues a single-use token bound to the focused window and browser tab; the extension or accessibility adapter returns only a selected visible/semantic region, source metadata, redacted text or low-resolution crop, and a content hash. The relay expires the capsule after one answer or 60 seconds and links the evidence hash to the job receipt without storing raw pixels.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask about exactly what is in front of them and trust that the answer came from the current page, not an old tab or an invented context, while reducing the chance that private screen contents leak or linger.
changes.effort: Medium-high: cross-process focus attestation, browser/Mac adapters, secret-field redaction, token expiry, typed evidence schema, and a small dashboard evidence viewer.
changes.risk: Focus can change during capture or accessibility APIs can fail; return an explicit stale/unknown result and never silently substitute another tab. Redaction can miss novel secrets, so default to minimal regions and short-lived transport. Recovery is a fresh capsule request.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring cost; mostly local metadata/OCR, with a small model call only when visual interpretation is needed. Short-lived capsule storage is bounded and automatically deleted.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under a second for token negotiation and extraction; avoids sending full screenshots and usually reduces model latency and token cost.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens least-retention and provenance without adding an approval gate. It needs authenticated local IPC, per-request nonce binding, encrypted relay transport, and deletion verification.
depends_on: Mac focused-window API
Browser extension active-tab attestation
Relay ephemeral payload store and expiry sweeper
Pendant capture indicator and evidence replay control

changes.change: Add an end-to-end 24 kHz audio negotiation and validation protocol: the relay advertises codec/rate/frame parameters, the pendant acknowledges them, and every stream begins with a short loopback/test-vector exchange carrying sequence numbers, CRC, encode/decode timing, underrun counters, and resampler mode. Persist only the last health counters and negotiated profile; automatically fall back to the existing 16 kHz uplink/24 kHz downlink profile when the 24 kHz path misses its latency budget.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely consistent wideband playback instead of silently hearing a degraded or glitchy stream. When it fails, the pendant can say whether the cause was network loss, relay transcoding, decoder CPU saturation, or the Mac TTS path, rather than making the owner debug three machines.
changes.effort: Medium: shared protocol fields in relay and Mac bridge, a small fixed-point test vector in firmware, and telemetry/receipt display in the dashboard; validate on the current nRF9160 DK before selecting product silicon.
changes.risk: A negotiation bug could leave the pendant silent or produce incompatible frames. Keep the current profile as a versioned fallback, require a timeout before switching, and make the test-vector path run before user audio only.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 2–4 KB flash and under 2 KB RAM for counters/test buffers on the pendant. Test packets add a few hundred bytes per session.
changes.latency_impact: Adds approximately 100–250 ms once per session for validation; steady-state target remains 60 ms frames, with fallback if decode plus encode exceeds the observed ~87% single-core combined load.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry should contain counters and negotiated formats only, not audio content. Authenticate the profile exchange with the existing paired relay/session identity.
depends_on: A relay telemetry schema and dashboard view for negotiated audio profiles
A Mac bridge receipt path that records TTS sample rate and resampling decisions
The owner's requested 24 kHz superwideband path being enabled in the production audio pipeline

changes.change: Introduce a cross-surface causality ledger with a signed trace envelope. Every pendant utterance, relay decision, model call, Mac job, browser command/result, retry, and TTS segment receives a trace ID, parent span ID, sequence number, monotonic duration, wall-clock estimate, actor, sensitivity label, and outcome.
