changes.change: Add a command-outcome and recovery ledger around run_shell without changing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: capture bounded stdout/stderr plus exit code, signal, timeout, cwd, duration, environment fingerprint (never secrets), and a normalized failure class (not-found, permission, dependency, transient-network, parse, timeout, unknown). Persist content-addressed output artifacts and link them to the existing action receipt/job. On failure, record a resumable checkpoint and generate a machine-readable retry plan (same command, adjusted timeout/cwd, or an explicitly different alternative) so the relay can say what failed and resume only the unfinished step rather than replaying a whole multi-action job.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac task fails after you leave, the pendant can tell you exactly whether it was a missing file, timeout, or network problem and continue from the failed step. Large output need not be stuffed into conversation, while you retain a trace you can inspect; retries stop wasting time repeating already-completed shell work.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper and D1/job schema changes, artifact store with size/redaction limits, failure classifier, retry-plan serializer, and relay/dashboard rendering. Add integration tests for timeout, nonzero exit, truncation, and resumed multi-step jobs.
changes.risk: Capturing command output can expose private file contents or tokens; redact common credential patterns, cap inline output, encrypt or access-control artifacts, and expire them independently of receipts. A bad classifier could suggest an unsafe alternative, so alternatives are advisory data for the trusted planner, never auto-executed as a different command. Preserve raw receipt and allow manual retry of the exact original.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost for ordinary runs; modest storage for bounded artifacts (for example 256 KB inline plus compressed object spill). A cheaper background classifier or deterministic rules handle most failures; use the expensive model only when recovery reasoning is requested.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero execution overhead for metadata capture; artifact hashing adds milliseconds. Failure explanation can be immediate from deterministic classes, with slower model analysis only on demand.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a sensitive output archive. Keep artifacts local or encrypted, apply TTL and per-job access controls, omit environment values and redact secrets before persistence. No new authorization gate is introduced, honoring maximum-access policy.
depends_on: Existing actionReceipts.js receipt IDs and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
A durable job/checkpoint store so completed action IDs survive process restarts
A bounded local artifact store and relay endpoint for fetching selected failure evidence

changes.change: Add a local workspace inventory service that periodically indexes developer-relevant roots (home, Documents, Desktop, configured project roots) into a compact manifest: repo path, branch/status summary, package/build markers, recently modified files, and filesystem watch timestamps. Expose a read-only resolver used before shell planning (e.g. resolve 'owner project' or 'the repo with package.json and agentic-gadget') and return ranked candidates with exact paths and freshness; never guess a cwd silently when confidence is low.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent stops wasting several turns hunting for a project or running commands in the wrong directory. Saying “run the tests in my agent project” can become a fast, accurate action even after the Mac reboots or the project moves within the home folder.
changes.effort: Medium: initial scanner with macOS filesystem APIs, FSEvents/incremental refresh, manifest schema and TTL, local-agent read route, and planner integration. Keep indexing bounded to configured roots and ignore build/cache/node_modules contents.
changes.risk: Paths and repository names are sensitive metadata; keep the index local, redact secrets and file contents, enforce per-job access, and provide an exclude list. Stale manifests can misroute work, so every resolved candidate should include freshness and be verified with a cheap existence/git check immediately before execution.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost for indexing or deterministic resolution; small local disk footprint (typically KB–MB) and low background CPU during changes. Reduces expensive planner turns and shell retries.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond to tens of milliseconds for lookup; an occasional initial scan may take seconds but runs outside an owner interaction.
changes.security_impact: Adds a searchable map of private paths, so encrypt or permission the manifest and avoid indexing secrets/content. It does not change unrestricted execution or introduce approval gates.
depends_on: A local-agent read-only route for workspace resolution
Mac filesystem watch/incremental scan implementation
Planner support for using a resolved cwd while displaying the selected path in the action receipt

changes.change: Add a failure-aware command journal and recovery runner between the existing Mac executor and job/receipt APIs. Every run_shell, run_applescript, typed action, and browser action emits one normalized step record: parent job/request ID, surface, argv or action type (with secrets redacted), cwd, start/end, timeout, exit code, bounded stdout/stderr hashes plus short excerpts, and reversible/irreversible classification for observability only. A classifier maps failures to stable categories (not-found, permission, timeout, dependency-offline, stale-browser-tab, bad-input, unknown). For known reversible categories it selects a versioned repair recipe with explicit precondition and postcondition probes, runs at most two attempts, and writes a linked before/after receipt; unknown failures become a durable diagnosis task rather than an unbounded retry. Expose GET /jobs/:id/failure and POST /jobs/:id/recover plus a compact event to relay/pipeline so the pendant can say what failed and whether recovery completed.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac fails while the owner is away from the keyboard, they get a concrete explanation and an automatic, bounded attempt at recovery instead of “something went wrong” or repeated blind retries. The owner can later audit exactly what changed and undo where supported, without giving up the deliberate maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: shared step schema and redaction, executor instrumentation, 6–10 built-in recipes with pre/post probes, two routes, and relay event wiring; add fault-injection tests for timeout, missing app, stale browser tab, and partial completion.
changes.risk: Capturing command text/output can leak sensitive data; redact known secret patterns, cap excerpts, hash full output, and retain only short-lived diagnostics. A repair recipe can make an incorrect but reversible change; require preconditions, postcondition verification, max-attempt limits, and automatic rollback through existing undo where available. If the runner crashes, the linked receipt remains marked unknown rather than falsely successful.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost for local classification and cached recipes; roughly $0.003–$0.02 only when a background model must interpret an unknown error. Small local disk/database growth from bounded receipts; no new hardware.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms instrumentation overhead to normal actions. Known diagnosis/recovery starts immediately; unknown cases add one background model round trip and become durable rather than blocking the voice turn.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without reducing owner-authorized access or adding confirmation gates. Store redacted command metadata, not secrets; isolate browser evidence to its existing authenticated session and never include page tokens in relay events.
depends_on: A single correlation/request ID shared by relay, Mac, and browser jobs
A documented receipt schema and retention/redaction policy
A small recipe registry with preconditions/postconditions and explicit retryability
Relay subscription to job failure/completion events

changes.change: Implement the granted mac_read_diagnostics adapter as a fixed-query local-agent endpoint, not a shell passthrough. Support the eight declared checks with typed JSON (OS/model/user/uptime, battery, network interfaces, Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, audio, agent health, processes, disk), per-check timeout, unavailable/error state, timestamp, and a single snapshot ID. Have get_mac_status and planning consume the same snapshot so a spoken answer and a subsequent action cannot mix observations from different moments.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can answer whether the Mac is actually reachable, online, low on space, or unhealthy without opening a microphone or running opaque commands. More importantly, it stops the agent from making decisions from stale or contradictory status facts and makes failures explainable.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: typed collector on the Mac, route authentication, schema validation, per-check timeouts, and adapter wiring; add tests for offline and permission-denied checks.
changes.risk: Some checks expose personal device metadata. Return only requested fields, omit process arguments and network identifiers unless explicitly needed, and apply short retention. A stale snapshot could mislead; every result carries timestamp/age and unknown is preferred to guessed.
changes.cost_impact: No model/API cost; negligible local CPU, disk, and network overhead. One compact JSON snapshot per status request.
changes.latency_impact: Typical response under 300 ms with parallel bounded collectors; slow checks degrade individually instead of blocking the whole response.
changes.security_impact: Narrow fixed queries reduce accidental shell exposure while preserving the owner's maximum-access action policy. Use existing local-agent authentication and never return secrets, command text, or raw process arguments.
depends_on: A real implementation behind the already-granted mac_read_diagnostics schema
Shared typed status schema consumed by get_mac_status and mac-planner
Local-agent authentication and request correlation IDs

changes.change: Add an offline-capable job-notification channel to the pendant: accept authenticated compact events (working, completed, blocked, failed), map them to distinct LED/haptic patterns, retain only the latest event plus a small acknowledged flag in flash, coalesce repeated progress events, honor a hardware mute/quiet state, and emit the associated job ID on a button press so the relay can speak details. The firmware must fail closed on malformed/unauthenticated events and continue normal button/audio behavior when the relay is unavailable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that a Mac or authenticated-browser task completed or needs attention without staring at a screen or starting a voice exchange. A single press turns an abstract vibration into a useful spoken result, while offline retention prevents a completion notification from disappearing during a brief link loss.
changes.effort: Medium: event authentication and compact queue in firmware, three or four signal patterns, acknowledgement/mute behavior, relay delivery and replay tests, and a small preference surface for quiet hours.
changes.risk: Too many signals could become annoying or reveal private activity. Coalesce to one latest state per job, suppress intermediate progress, support mute/quiet hours, and encode no sensitive text in the physical pattern. If flash wear or link loss occurs, drop old events and preserve normal pendant operation; never block audio or button handling.
changes.cost_impact: No model/API cost. Firmware storage is a few hundred bytes plus wear-leveled event metadata; average power impact is negligible because signaling uses existing LED/haptic hardware, with short vibration bursts adding only transient draw.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second notification after relay delivery; no impact on normal voice latency. Acknowledgement lookup adds one relay round trip only when the owner presses the button.
changes.security_impact: Requires device-bound authenticated event delivery and opaque job IDs. The pendant stores no command, page, account, or transcript content; relay authorization remains the source of truth.
depends_on: Authenticated Mac/browser-to-relay lifecycle events
Pendant firmware event parser and LED/haptic pattern API
Button event carrying acknowledged job ID to relay
Owner-configurable mute and quiet-hour preferences

changes.change: Add a reconnectable process lease for long-running run_shell work. When a shell action is intentionally marked long-running, launch it under a local supervisor with a durable jobId/lease, process-group ID, monotonic output cursor, heartbeat, and bounded spool on disk; decouple process lifetime from the HTTP request and Mac bridge connection. GET /jobs/:jobId and relay_job_status should report running/stalled/exited with the last cursor and timestamps; a reconnect operation should stream only unseen output, and cancel should terminate the whole process group. Do not auto-retry or change FULL_CONTROL_MODE; this is continuity and explicit recovery, not a gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A research, build, export, or backup task keeps working when the pendant conversation ends or the relay briefly disconnects. On return, the owner hears exactly whether it finished, where it stopped, and the new output only—without accidentally launching a second copy or losing the useful tail of a long command.
changes.effort: Medium-high: supervisor process, durable spool/lease state, cursor API, bridge reconnect handling, process-group cancellation, crash recovery and cleanup, dashboard and relay status integration.
changes.risk: Detached processes can outlive the owner's intent or consume CPU/disk. Require an explicit long-running intent in the action payload, enforce an owner-configured maximum duration and spool quota, mark leases stale after heartbeat loss, and expose cancel; on agent restart, reconcile child processes by supervisor metadata and report unknowns rather than killing unrelated processes. Output may contain secrets, so local-only raw spool with redacted summaries to relay and TTL deletion.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model calls for normal execution; small local disk/RAM spool and one supervisor process per active job. Relay status remains a cheap read.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement in under 100 ms; reconnect status is sub-second plus output transfer, instead of waiting for a 120-second request timeout.
changes.security_impact: Preserves the owner's deliberate unrestricted execution while adding lifecycle visibility, not permission checks. Process IDs, cwd, and output tails need local access controls; never expose raw spool to unauthenticated relay clients.
depends_on: GET /jobs/:jobId
POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel
GET /journal/:jobId
GET /ops/snapshot
describe:relay_job_status
existing action receipts and durable job tracker

changes.change: Add a content-addressed shell transcript recorder inside the existing FULL_CONTROL executor. For every run_shell action, persist argv/command, resolved cwd, start/end timestamps, timeout, exit code, signal, bounded stdout/stderr, and SHA-256 hashes of full streams; redact environment secrets and tokenize likely credentials before the relay sees them. Link the transcript to the existing actionReceipt/actionId and relay correlation ID, expose a streaming tail plus a compact failure classification, and garbage-collect raw output by TTL while retaining hashes and summaries.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac says a job failed, the owner can see whether it timed out, used the wrong directory, lost network, or returned a nonzero result instead of asking the agent to guess and rerun. It also makes the deliberate unrestricted shell trustworthy through visibility without adding gates or reducing capability.
changes.effort: Medium: executor wrapper, encrypted local transcript store, redaction tests, GET transcript/tail routes, and dashboard rendering. No planner policy change required.
changes.risk: Command output can contain credentials or sensitive file contents; redaction can miss novel formats, so keep raw transcripts local by default and apply short TTL/size caps. Avoid replaying transcripts as commands. If recording fails, execution must still complete and the receipt must say observability is partial.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; roughly tens of KB per ordinary command and bounded to a configurable per-job quota. Hashing and local append are low CPU overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Typically <20 ms overhead before the command and buffered writes after completion; streaming tail adds small local I/O only.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability while preserving FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Raw stdout/stderr stay on the Mac unless explicitly requested; relay receives redacted bounded data and hashes. No new authorization gate.
depends_on: Existing actionReceipts linkage (chg-5fc73ce3)
A local durable journal/TTL sweeper
Read-only authenticated observability route for transcript metadata and tails

changes.change: Add an execution preflight and adaptive recovery layer that runs before queued Mac/browser work: snapshot bridge/browser/permission health, classify the likely failure (offline extension, missing Accessibility/Screen Recording, timeout, transient app error), attach the preflight and model-tier receipt to the job, and either (a) immediately retry only transient failures with bounded backoff, or (b) return a concrete owner-facing repair instruction and keep the job resumable rather than spending repeated 45-second attempts. Do not block or gate actions; this is observability and recovery only.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can tell the owner why something failed and recover automatically instead of silently burning time on impossible browser actions. Today the agent has 5 queued browser commands while the extension is offline, and recent failures take ~45 seconds each; the owner should get one actionable status and a continuation when Chrome/Safari returns.
changes.effort: Medium: shared preflight module, failure classifier, resumable job state, and receipt fields across local-agent and relay job status.
changes.risk: A bad classifier could retry a non-transient action or misdiagnose a permission issue. Bound retries, preserve idempotency keys, and expose the exact raw failure and preflight snapshot in the journal; resume only from the failed action boundary.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and one cheap local status check per job; reduces wasted realtime/model calls and repeated browser polling.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for local preflight, but avoids 45-second offline waits; retries are background and bounded.
changes.security_impact: Receipts must redact command arguments and page content while retaining health flags. No new privileges or restrictions.
depends_on: Durable job receipts already present (chg-5fc73ce3)
Authenticated /ops/snapshot, /journal, and browser status observability
Idempotency-aware job runner and relay_job_status continuation

changes.change: Propagate a single request/job correlation id and routing receipt from planner through relay → Mac job creation → every action receipt, with a small backfill reconciler for existing jobs. Expose tier, escalation, model, latency, and token estimate on /journal/:jobId and relay_job_status; mark genuinely external jobs as unknown rather than leaving most actions unattributed.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a task is slow or fails, the owner gets an honest explanation of whether the delay came from the model, relay, Mac execution, or a disconnected browser. The live router already reports useful tier data (57% of recent requests avoided planner and one background request escalated), but 112 of 147 retained actions currently have no tier attribution.
changes.effort: Medium: request-id propagation across relay and local-agent schemas, receipt join, and a read-only migration for retained jobs.
changes.risk: Incorrect joins could report the wrong model or expose internal prompts. Use immutable IDs, confidence/unknown states, and never include prompt text in receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage; enables cheaper routing decisions and avoids redundant diagnostic model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero metadata overhead; reconciliation can run asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Receipts need model metadata only, with argument/page-content redaction preserved.
depends_on: Existing /routing statistics
Existing action receipts and journal
Relay job records and relay_job_status

changes.change: Add an offline-aware command lifecycle between the existing browser queue and job receipts. Before dispatching any browser_* action, read bridge liveness and, when offline, immediately persist a typed `waiting_for_browser` result (with health timestamp and no 45-second action timeout). Keep the original job/action id and park it rather than enqueueing duplicates. On POST /browser/heartbeat or the poll loop, claim parked actions atomically and resume incomplete IDs; write one receipt transition (`waiting_for_browser` → `running` → `completed|failed`). Emit a compact relay event for the transition so the pendant can speak the status, while `/jobs/:id` remains the source of truth.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Safari tasks stop burning time and generating duplicate commands when the extension is closed. The owner hears the real reason immediately, can walk away, and receives one trustworthy completion or failure instead of repeated timeout noise.
changes.effort: Medium: browser queue state transition and atomic claim, executor preflight, heartbeat hook, receipt schema extension, and relay event projection; add crash/reconnect and duplicate-action tests.
changes.risk: A reconnect race could run an action twice or resume a stale private-page goal. Preserve stable action IDs, claim leases, and terminal receipts; on crash, recover only unexpired waiting/running leases and report ambiguous actions rather than replaying them blindly. This changes timing/status, not authorization or the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and health requests; materially fewer planner retries and browser round trips. No additional model call is required for the state machine.
changes.latency_impact: Offline response falls from the observed ~45 seconds to about 1–2 seconds; reconnect adds at most one heartbeat interval (target 5–10 seconds).
changes.security_impact: No new data access. Keep page contents in the browser bridge; relay receives only job ID, state, and sanitized error. Retain existing receipts and authenticated session affinity.
depends_on: A durable browser job runner/queue (chg-16bc5dee) or equivalent command persistence
Existing browser heartbeat/poll/result routes and action receipts (chg-14accc01, chg-5fc73ce3)
A relay event path that can deduplicate notifications by job ID

changes.change: Turn the existing /ops/snapshot permission state into a live 'Mac reachability' panel and machine-readable preflight: show Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser bridge, and relay states separately with the exact blocked surfaces (for example mac-vision unavailable while shell remains usable), last-seen timestamps, and deep links/actions to open the relevant System Settings pane. Attach the same compact preflight summary to failed job receipts and expose it to the relay, without preventing any action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can understand why a visual or browser task failed and fix only the missing permission, instead of hearing a generic failure or repeatedly retrying a capability the Mac cannot currently provide. Shell and other working surfaces remain available.
changes.effort: Small to medium: normalize /ops/snapshot permission fields, add a dashboard card and typed failure metadata, and map common macOS settings destinations; test stale/offline transitions.
changes.risk: Permission details can become stale or expose local app names. Timestamp every observation, limit relay speech to the relevant missing capability, and never claim readiness from cached data without labeling it. Opening settings should be an ordinary reversible Mac action, not an approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; one lightweight status poll and a small UI/event payload.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds to failures and makes diagnosis faster; no impact on successful actions.
changes.security_impact: Read-only permission metadata is local; do not transmit host fingerprints or full application lists to the relay. Deep links should remain on-device.
depends_on: GET /ops/snapshot
GET /ops/status
GET /browser/status
mac_read_diagnostics
mac_execute_typed_actions

changes.change: Add a sensitivity firewall between context retrieval and all planner traces, job receipts, /thinking streams, relay telemetry, and dashboard views. Classify entities/facts into public, personal, sensitive, and secret; pass only a short capability token/reference for sensitive or secret facts to the action executor, never the plaintext. Redact existing trace chunks and logs at serialization time, preserve provenance and a non-secret reason such as “credential-like fact withheld,” and add a per-job retention/deletion hook. The firewall must cover long-term memory, browser page extracts, shell output, and spoken summaries, with an explicit allowlist for a user-requested private task.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A live job trace currently includes unrelated long-term facts such as “bike lock code” alongside project context. Anyone or any surface that can read /jobs, /thinking, relay telemetry, or a dashboard could receive secrets that were not needed for the task. The owner gets the same useful actions and receipts without accidental disclosure through logs, model prompts, or the pendant’s spoken channel.
changes.effort: Medium: typed sensitivity metadata in the context graph, a redacting serializer shared by Mac and relay, secret-reference plumbing for executors, migration/redaction of stored traces, and focused tests proving secrets do not appear in planner prompts or receipts.
changes.risk: Over-redaction could make a legitimate private task fail or produce an unhelpful explanation; recover by allowing a narrowly scoped per-job sensitivity grant and recording only its expiry and purpose. Existing stored logs need a one-time scrub, with an audit count but not the recovered plaintext.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; small CPU/storage overhead for classification and redaction. One migration pass over Mac JSON/D1 records.
changes.latency_impact: Typically under 20 ms locally; negligible relay overhead. Secret classification can be deterministic, with background model assistance only for ambiguous new facts.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves containment: plaintext sensitive facts stay in the minimum execution surface, while receipts carry hashes, provenance, and redaction markers. Must ensure capability references cannot be resolved by untrusted dashboard or voice clients.
depends_on: A typed context projection/selection service (the existing context-compiler backlog work)
A shared receipt/log serializer used by /jobs, /thinking, /journal, relay telemetry, and dashboard
Per-fact sensitivity and retention metadata in the context graph
An executor API that accepts scoped secret references without echoing their values

changes.change: Add a tamper-evident, append-only cross-surface execution ledger. The pendant, relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge each emit signed step events with task id, idempotency key, input hash, result hash, monotonic sequence, and local timestamp; the relay periodically seals a Merkle root and syncs missing segments after reconnection. The dashboard and spoken agent can then distinguish confirmed execution, locally completed-but-unsynced work, duplicate suppression, and genuinely unknown outcomes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac, relay, or browser disconnects, the owner should be able to know whether something actually happened rather than receiving a vague success or failure. This gives them a trustworthy answer such as “the reminder was created locally at 9:02; the relay received the receipt at 9:03” and prevents silent duplicate actions after retries.
changes.effort: Medium-high: event schema and signing keys per surface, durable local queues, relay sealing and reconciliation, and dashboard/voice rendering. Existing receipts can be migrated as unsigned historical records.
changes.risk: Clock differences, lost local storage, or key rotation could create apparent gaps. Recover with monotonic per-device sequence numbers, explicit unknown intervals, key-version metadata, and never claiming continuity when a segment is missing.
changes.cost_impact: Small local storage and relay D1/R2 growth; no routine model cost. Merkle sealing is inexpensive CPU work and can run in the background.
changes.latency_impact: Action execution need not wait for global sealing; local append is synchronous and under a few milliseconds, while cross-device verification happens asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Improves integrity and accountability but introduces signing-key lifecycle and metadata-privacy concerns. Keep payloads as hashes/references, encrypt detailed evidence, and rotate/revoke per-device keys.
depends_on: A durable conversation checkpoint and exactly-once ledger contract
Persistent local event queues on pendant, Mac agent, and browser bridge
Per-surface signing keys provisioned during pairing
Relay reconciliation and dashboard support for explicit unknown outcomes

changes.change: Implement an exactly-once notification outbox for browser-watch and Mac-job events. Normalize each event to a stable fingerprint (watch/session + source revision + semantic change hash), store one outbox row with delivery states for pendant speech, dashboard, and optional iOS push, and require each consumer to acknowledge that row. Retries may redeliver transport packets but must not create a second spoken/dashboard item; recovery events should reference the original event. Add a compact reconciliation endpoint that reports pending, acknowledged, suppressed-duplicate, and expired notifications.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner hears one useful “your order shipped” rather than the same change repeatedly, and can see whether an important event is waiting, spoken, or merely failed delivery. It also prevents a disconnected browser or sleeping pendant from turning retries into notification spam.
changes.effort: Medium: D1 outbox schema and unique fingerprint constraint, relay delivery workers, acknowledgement plumbing in pendant/dashboard/iOS, and migration of existing page-watch reports.
changes.risk: An over-aggressive fingerprint could suppress a real update; include source revision and a bounded time window, and expose suppressed items in the dashboard for inspection. If speech delivery fails after acknowledgement, the dashboard remains the durable fallback. Do not put authenticated page excerpts in generic relay logs.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1 writes per distinct event and no model calls for dedupe; one cheap background classifier only when raw watch payloads cannot be normalized deterministically. Speech cost falls because duplicate announcements disappear.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms deterministic outbox write; delivery asynchronously within the existing relay heartbeat/pipeline cadence.
changes.security_impact: Store opaque event IDs and encrypted/private payload references in relay; send excerpts only over the paired authenticated channel. Acknowledgements must be scoped to the paired owner/device, not a public URL.
depends_on: Existing page-watch reports in /logs and browser result receipts
Relay D1 job/history store and durable audio pipeline
GET /browser/status plus browser heartbeat transitions
Existing dashboard shared by web, menubar WKWebView, and iOS Capacitor
A per-watch source revision/fingerprint field, which does not currently exist

changes.change: Add a non-blocking capability preflight and fail-fast dispatch contract across the Mac agent, browser bridge, and relay. Before a browser_* action is queued, read the existing /ops/status (or a cached heartbeat) and attach a capability snapshot: browser online/lastSeen, pending-command count, accessibility and screen-recording readiness, relay reachability, and an expected execution deadline. If the target is offline, do not spend the action timeout waiting: return a typed `unavailable` receipt immediately with the exact recovery instruction (for example, open Safari and enable/poll the AI Pendant Browser Bridge), retain the user's intent as a durable queued job only when the request was explicitly asynchronous, and re-check on heartbeat to resume it. The same snapshot should be embedded in /jobs, /journal, and spoken completion/failure summaries so the planner can choose shell, browser, or relay instead of blindly retrying.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a browser request can sit for roughly 45 seconds and then fail even though the Mac and relay are healthy; the owner gets no useful answer until the timeout. This makes the pendant respond immediately, choose another reachable surface when possible, and resume genuinely background work after the browser returns—without adding approval gates or reducing the owner's maximum-access policy.
changes.effort: Medium: shared health schema, dispatch middleware, heartbeat-triggered resumer, and typed receipt/UI rendering; no new model required.
changes.risk: A stale cached heartbeat could report a surface as available when it is not, or an intent could resume after the owner forgot it. Bound cache age, preserve idempotency keys, mark queued work clearly, and provide cancel/delete through existing job controls. Never claim an action ran from a preflight result.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves failed planner/tool retries and ~45-second waits. Small local D1/job-store growth for health snapshots and queued intent metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions add a cheap local health lookup; unavailable browser actions return in milliseconds instead of timing out. Resumed jobs begin on the next bridge heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: No new data access; health metadata should omit URLs/titles and expose only capability state. Existing unrestricted shell policy remains unchanged.
depends_on: A stable browser heartbeat/online contract in the existing /browser/heartbeat and /browser/status routes
Durable job lifecycle and idempotency semantics behind /jobs and /jobs/:jobId/cancel
A shared typed receipt schema consumed by /journal and dashboard

changes.change: Add a durable execution-ledger join that attaches routing receipt, planner trace, parent job, action receipt, evidence capsule IDs, and undoability to one immutable record. Backfill links when a job finishes, and expose filters for model tier, command type, failure class, latency, and whether the action was a write. Treat missing joins explicitly as 'unattributed' rather than silently dropping them.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The Mac currently reports 146 actions and 77 writes, but 112 actions are unattributed to a model tier; the owner cannot reliably answer which agent spent time, what actually ran, or why a failure happened. A single human-readable history would make the pendant's 'what happened?' answer trustworthy and reveal waste such as repeated browser attempts.
changes.effort: Medium: define a stable executionId and correlation propagation through planner/router/executor, add a small append-only ledger plus a repair pass over recent jobs, then add dashboard and relay summary queries.
changes.risk: Correlation bugs could duplicate or misjoin records. Preserve existing job and receipt files as source of truth, make the ledger append-only/idempotent, and mark uncertain joins rather than guessing. No action behavior or owner policy changes.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; small local JSONL/SQLite storage and negligible CPU. Dashboard queries may add a few milliseconds.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero on execution if linkage is emitted in-memory; asynchronous persistence after receipt completion.
changes.security_impact: Keep command text, URLs, and evidence local by default; relay receives only redacted summaries unless explicitly requested. This is observability, not a new permission gate.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and /jobs/:jobId/receipts
Existing /routing and routingStats records
Existing /journal and /journal/:jobId
A stable correlation ID propagated by mac-planner/mac-vision/browser actions

changes.change: Add lease/TTL semantics and supersession for browser commands: every queued command records session, prerequisite health snapshot, expiry, and supersedes key; when the extension is offline, coalesce repeated idempotent probes, stop dispatching stale work, and emit one deferred receipt. On heartbeat, revalidate the session before releasing only still-valid commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The live Mac has 7 pending browser commands while offline, and repeated browser navigation attempts have all consumed roughly 45 seconds before failing. This prevents stale clicks or navigations from replaying after the owner has moved on, while preserving useful work and making recovery quick when Safari returns.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: extend browser command records, add queue sweeper and dedupe index, validate session/URL before dispatch, and surface deferred/expired states in job receipts.
changes.risk: A legitimate long-running task could expire or a coalescing key could merge commands that were intentionally distinct. Default TTLs by action type, never coalesce writes, and keep an explicit force/continue path for the planner.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/CPU; saves browser round trips and planner retries. No additional model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate offline classification; recovery dispatch starts on the first healthy heartbeat instead of waiting for timeout.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing stale authenticated actions from replaying. Preserve session affinity and do not broaden data access.
depends_on: Existing browser command queue and /browser/poll
GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat
Existing request IDs/idempotency keys and action receipts
The execution-ledger correlation proposed above

changes.change: Add end-to-end data-residency and sensitivity labels to every cross-surface artifact, not just raw browser pages: classify source fields and derived summaries as device-local, relay-safe, or owner-approved-to-share; propagate the label through Mac jobs, browser evidence capsules, relay notifications, audio queues, and pendant speech. The relay should receive a redacted event or a cryptographic reference when the source is local-only, while the Mac can still perform the full private computation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should be able to ask the pendant for a spoken answer about private browser, Mail, or Mac data without having to wonder whether the underlying content or an audio copy left the Mac. Today there is no consistent guarantee across the Mac agent, browser bridge, relay, and durable audio path; this would make private cross-device assistance trustworthy while retaining the hive's reach.
changes.effort: Large: define a small label taxonomy and provenance envelope, add propagation and redaction at every serialization boundary, encrypt/localize private artifacts, and expose a per-job residency explanation in the dashboard and completion receipt.
changes.risk: Incorrect classification could leak sensitive content or unnecessarily prevent useful delivery. Default unknown data to local-only, preserve source provenance, make redaction deterministic and testable, and allow the owner to explicitly promote a specific artifact. This is a data-handling safeguard, not an action-approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model calls for deterministic labels and redaction; modest local storage and relay metadata overhead. Summaries may require one extra background pass when redaction is semantic rather than structural.
changes.latency_impact: Usually under 100 ms for labels; semantic redaction may add roughly 1–3 seconds. Private Mac computation remains local and does not wait on relay upload.
changes.security_impact: Substantially reduces accidental exfiltration through relay logs, durable audio, browser evidence, and spoken notifications. Requires encryption at rest and strict rejection of unlabeled cross-surface payloads.
depends_on: Mac job and action receipts
Browser evidence capsules and authenticated session metadata
Relay persistent state and durable audio paths
Pendant notification/speech delivery
A shared provenance envelope carried across planner, Mac, browser, and relay

changes.change: Add a cross-surface liveness supervisor and dead-letter recovery loop. The relay periodically reads Mac /ops/status, /browser/status, /jobs, and /routing; tracks per-surface heartbeats, pending-command age, timeout/error rates, permission readiness, and attribution completeness. When a browser command is queued but the extension is offline or repeatedly times out, move it to a durable dead-letter record (preserving idempotency key and tab/session affinity), stop blind retries, and issue one compact pendant/Mac notification explaining the exact recovery step. On heartbeat recovery, revalidate the tab/session and offer a bounded resume; classify receipts with the originating tier/model so unattributed work is eliminated. This is telemetry/recovery only and does not gate FULL_CONTROL actions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently gets 45-second repeated browser failures and seven stranded commands with no proactive explanation. They would instead hear once that Safari/extension is offline or blocked, know which request was preserved, and have it resume safely when the bridge returns—while Mac shell remains maximally capable.
changes.effort: Medium: relay state machine plus a small Mac observability adapter, dead-letter persistence, heartbeat scheduler, and pendant notification payloads; ~2–3 engineering days including failure-injection tests.
changes.risk: A false offline diagnosis could delay an otherwise recoverable action; mitigate with timestamps, one bounded retry after heartbeat, and explicit queued/failed/resumable states. Never replay a non-idempotent action without its existing idempotency key and session revalidation. No new data beyond existing job/action receipts, URLs, and error metadata leaves the Mac.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero model cost: deterministic polling and state transitions; roughly a few D1 writes per incident and small relay egress. Avoids expensive planner retries and repeated 45-second browser calls.
changes.latency_impact: Heartbeat polling adds negligible background load; recovery notification is near real time. It reduces user-visible failure latency by detecting offline state before waiting through a command timeout.
changes.security_impact: Read-only access to current authenticated observability endpoints; preserves existing unrestricted execution policy. Do not include page contents or secrets in relay telemetry—send status, IDs, timestamps, and sanitized error classes only.
depends_on: Existing authenticated read-only /ops/status, /browser/status, /jobs, /journal, and /routing endpoints
Durable relay D1 state and pendant notification/audio pipeline
Existing job idempotency keys, receipts, and browser tab/session affinity

changes.change: Add a failure-aware continuation layer above the unrestricted executor. For every action, persist a typed outcome (transport/offline, permission, timeout, command error, semantic mismatch) plus stderr/exit status, observed bridge state, and the last successful receipt. Before retrying, consult an idempotency-key circuit breaker: suppress identical retries after a configurable failure threshold, refresh the relevant prerequisite (for example browser heartbeat/session reattachment or Mac permission status), then resume only from the last successful action. Surface a compact recovery plan and a `resume job` operation through /jobs and the relay, while preserving FULL_CONTROL_MODE and never blocking an owner-requested action; retries must be explicit in the job trace. Attribute every action to its routing tier/model and retain the failed command's redacted argv/env metadata.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a browser bridge disappears or a permission is missing, the owner gets an intelligible diagnosis and a job that can continue instead of six silent duplicate failures or starting over. A spoken “finish that” can resume the unfinished work safely, while the owner can see whether the issue was offline, permission, timeout, or the command itself. This directly addresses the live state: 16 failed actions, 112 actions without tier attribution, and one browser navigation repeated six times with a 100% failure rate.
changes.effort: Medium: extend jobTracker/action receipts with normalized failure fields and continuation checkpoints; add a small retry/circuit-breaker module, prerequisite probes, resume endpoint, and relay status serialization; add tests for browser-offline, permission-denied, timeout, and successful resume.
changes.risk: A bad classifier could label a recoverable failure permanent or resume from an unsafe checkpoint. Recovery: default to no automatic retry after the threshold, preserve the complete trace, allow explicit force-retry from the owner, and make each continuation idempotent. Do not transmit command contents or secrets to the relay; send only category, counts, and redacted diagnostics.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; mostly local JSON/D1 metadata. A cheaper deterministic classifier avoids spending planner tokens on routine failure diagnosis; escalate only ambiguous semantic failures.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds for local classification. Prerequisite refresh may add 1–3 seconds, but avoids repeated 120-second shell/browser attempts and avoids rerunning completed steps.
changes.security_impact: No reduction in the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy. Improve auditability by hashing/redacting argv, environment, and stderr before relay export; keep raw diagnostics local and apply retention limits.
depends_on: Existing action receipts and jobTracker persistence
Existing /jobs, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, /jobs/:jobId/cancel, and relay_job_status surfaces
Browser heartbeat/session state and Mac observability endpoints (/ops/status, /browser/status)
Routing attribution hooks in routingStats.js

changes.change: Make routing metadata an end-to-end trace context rather than an in-memory planner receipt. Generate a requestId at the pendant/relay boundary and propagate it through relay jobs, Mac /plan and /execute, browser commands, action receipts, and journal entries; record tier, model, prompt/completion token estimates, escalation reason, latency, and final outcome on every action. Add a deterministic preflight router that consults /ops/status (browser online, required permissions, relay reachability) and routes simple status/recovery queries to deterministic/background tiers, while marking impossible browser work as `waiting_for_surface` instead of repeatedly invoking the planner.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask what happened and receive one coherent answer: which device acted, what failed, how long it took, and whether model spend was justified. The system will stop wasting expensive planner calls when the browser is offline and will give a useful “reconnect Chrome” explanation instead. Today routing reports 7 requests but 112 journal actions have no tier attribution, so cost and failure explanations are incomplete.
changes.effort: Medium: introduce a trace-context object shared by relay and local-agent requests; persist compact routing receipts with jobs; update browser command envelopes and journal serializers; add preflight rules and dashboard aggregation.
changes.risk: Metadata can become noisy or accidentally include sensitive prompts. Keep command text out of cross-device receipts, store only hashes/intent labels and token counts, enforce bounded retention, and tolerate missing context without failing execution. Preflight must be advisory/status classification only, consistent with FULL_CONTROL_MODE and the owner's no-gates policy.
changes.cost_impact: Slightly more local storage and D1 writes; reduces planner spend by avoiding doomed retries and selecting deterministic/background handling for status work.
changes.latency_impact: A local preflight is sub-100 ms; propagation is negligible. It removes multi-second model calls for known-offline surfaces.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without restricting capability. Relay receives redacted IDs and outcome categories, never raw shell commands, environment, cookies, or page contents.
depends_on: Existing routingStats.js and /routing endpoint
Existing jobTracker/actionReceipts/journal persistence
Relay job identifiers and browser request IDs
Read-only /ops/status and /browser/status telemetry

changes.change: Add a non-blocking failure-aware executor recovery loop. Before dispatching a browser or Mac action, consult the live surface-health signal; after the first failure, fingerprint the error (offline, timeout, permission/dialog, invalid target), record it against the idempotency key, and choose a bounded recovery: fast-fail repeated known-offline commands instead of spending another 45 seconds, retry a timeout once with a fresh request ID only when the target is still healthy, and for public URLs offer the relay/public-browser backend. Never block or refuse an action globally: this is an execution optimization and diagnosis layer, with the original unrestricted command path retained. Emit a recovery receipt linking the failed attempt, retry, health snapshot, and final outcome.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A stuck Safari dialog or offline extension currently turns each attempt into an unexplained 45-second wait and repeated failures. The owner gets a quick, truthful diagnosis and either a recovered result or a concrete next step, while successful unrestricted Mac work remains just as capable.
changes.effort: Medium: failure classifier and per-surface health cache in the local agent, idempotent retry coordinator, receipt schema/dashboard rendering, and one relay fallback adapter. Test against offline extension, dialog-blocked Safari, timeout, and successful retry.
changes.risk: A retry could duplicate a non-idempotent action if classification is wrong. Restrict automatic retries to actions explicitly marked safe-to-retry or to attempts whose receipt proves no effect; preserve the current no-gate policy and surface ambiguity as a report, not a refusal. Recovery metadata may expose URLs and command error text, so keep it in the authenticated job store.
changes.cost_impact: Small background CPU/storage increase; fewer planner turns and fewer 45-second dead waits should reduce model/API spend. Public-browser fallback may incur provider usage only when selected.
changes.latency_impact: Healthy actions gain only a health-cache lookup; known offline failures return in milliseconds instead of ~45 seconds. A single safe retry adds at most one action timeout.
changes.security_impact: No new authority beyond existing unrestricted Mac/browser execution. Error receipts must redact environment variables, command secrets, cookies, and page bodies; retain hashes and bounded diagnostic text.
depends_on: Expose a typed surface-health snapshot from the existing browser status and Mac-agent liveness paths
Add retry-safety/idempotency metadata to action receipts
Preserve existing durable job and receipt records so recovery remains auditable

changes.change: Teach the router a deterministic execution-recovery intent that consumes job/receipt/health data directly. Phrases such as “why did that fail?”, “try it again”, and “is Safari back?” should resolve to a compact diagnostic or safe retry plan without sending the full fleet context to the planner; escalate only when the classifier finds ambiguous side effects or needs a new plan. Attach the failed job ID and recovery fingerprint so the planner does not re-interpret the same 45-second failure from scratch.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After a Mac or browser action fails, the owner can ask a natural follow-up and get an immediate, accurate status or retry instead of paying for a full reasoning turn and waiting for the system to rediscover the same failure.
changes.effort: Small to medium: add intent patterns, receipt/health lookup, and escalation rules; add regression tests for offline, timeout, and successful retry conversations.
changes.risk: A terse follow-up like “try again” can refer to an unsafe prior mutation. Default deterministic handling only to read-only or explicitly retry-safe actions; otherwise return the existing receipt and ask the planner to interpret context, without adding a new approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces repeated planner prompts and token cost for routine recovery; negligible storage and compute.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second for receipt/status responses; safe retries retain the underlying action latency.
changes.security_impact: Queries remain authenticated and should return bounded/redacted receipt fields, never raw shell environment or browser session data.
depends_on: Failure fingerprints and recovery receipts from the integration change
A stable job-id/idempotency-key reference in follow-up utterance context

changes.change: Add a preflight-and-fallback middleware between planner and executor. For every planned action, declare required surface facts (e.g. browser_online, tab_attached, accessibility, screen_recording, vision_consent, relay_reachable). Read a short-lived capability snapshot from /ops/status and /browser/status, annotate each step as ready/deferred/fallbackable, and persist that decision in the job and receipt. Execute only ready steps; for fallbackable steps select a declared alternative (relay/public web, shell/status, or durable browser queue), then recheck the affected surface once after a failure. Emit one structured completion event containing completed, deferred, fallback, and reason codes for relay/pendant narration. This is observability and recovery, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a fast truthful answer instead of waiting through impossible actions: e.g. 'I can read the Mac, but browser work is queued because the extension is offline; I did the public portion now.' It also stops identical browser timeouts and makes partial completion understandable.
changes.effort: Medium: capability schema, planner annotations, executor middleware, fallback registry, and relay event formatting; add integration tests for offline extension, missing permissions, stale heartbeat, and successful recovery.
changes.risk: A stale health snapshot could incorrectly defer a newly available surface or choose an inferior fallback. Use TTLs, include snapshot timestamps in receipts, and allow one bounded recheck. Never silently substitute a public source for a private authenticated page.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; local HTTP checks and JSON receipts. Small storage increase per action for capability snapshot and reason codes.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 100–300 ms to local jobs; avoids current 45-second browser timeout loops. Fallback execution can proceed in parallel where dependencies allow.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making private/public boundary explicit and preventing accidental public fallback. Does not narrow FULL_CONTROL_MODE or add confirmations.
depends_on: A typed required-capabilities field in the existing action registry
A fallback registry that marks which alternatives are privacy-equivalent versus public-only
A relay event schema for deferred/fallback completion
The existing /ops/status and browser status endpoints being reachable from the executor

changes.change: Create a cross-surface postcondition verifier that runs after an action batch. The planner must attach a typed expected outcome to each write. After execution, the verifier retrieves the same browser tab/session or Mac foreground context, compares the observed state to the expectation, stores a provenance-bound verification record, and emits a four-state verdict: verified, unverified, unchanged, or contradicted. Aggregate verdicts across the batch and expose a redacted proof card to the relay/pendant; retain raw evidence locally. A receipt may remain successful while the user-facing result is 'completed but unverified' until this check passes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust 'done' to mean the intended world state was observed, not just that an API or keystroke returned without an error. When something is ambiguous, they get a precise next step and compact proof instead of having to inspect the Mac themselves.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed postconditions in the planner/action registry, same-context read-after-write adapters for Mac and browser, evidence correlation, verdict persistence, and redacted voice/dashboard rendering.
changes.risk: Some applications update asynchronously or expose nondeterministic text, causing false 'contradicted' results. Support settling windows, semantic predicates, and an explicit unverified state; never retry a mutation merely because verification is inconclusive.
changes.cost_impact: One extra read per write and occasional small standard-model semantic comparison; no realtime call required for normal operation. Raw evidence increases local storage modestly.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 0.5–10 seconds depending on the surface, but replaces false immediate success with an honest bounded result. Independent postconditions can be checked in parallel.
changes.security_impact: Raw private evidence stays on the Mac/browser bridge. Relay receives only redacted fields, hashes, timestamps, and verdict unless the owner explicitly requests proof. Same-tab/session binding reduces cross-account leakage.
depends_on: Action schemas that carry typed expected outcomes
Browser same-tab read-after-write with provenance
Mac observe support for application/document postconditions
A local evidence redaction and retention policy
Relay/pendant event support for proof cards and four-state verdicts

changes.change: Add an execution-aware router that compiles a request into typed subgoals (local status, Mac shell/action, authenticated browser, public research, narration), consults live /ops/status and /browser/status before planning, and routes each subgoal independently. Cache deterministic Mac diagnostics and fail fast on an offline browser instead of spending a 45-second browser timeout; retain the full planner only for ambiguous joins. Attach the routing tier, subgoal ID, and outcome to every job receipt so the current 112 unattributed actions become attributable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant answers faster and more reliably: a browser outage no longer stalls unrelated Mac work, repeated battery/Wi-Fi questions do not pay planner tokens, and the owner receives one coherent answer from whatever parts actually worked.
changes.effort: Medium: define subgoal schema, health capability matrix, planner handoff, and receipt propagation across relay and local agent; add replay tests for partial failure.
changes.risk: A compiler could split a task incorrectly or report a partial answer as complete. Recover by preserving the original goal, requiring a join step to mark completion, and falling back to the existing planner when confidence is low. No action is blocked; this only changes planning and observability.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces planner calls and repeated timeout retries; expected savings are material given the observed 28,971 planner-tier tokens across 3 requests and 16 failed actions. Small deterministic CPU/storage overhead.
changes.latency_impact: Health check <300 ms; independent subgoals can run concurrently. Failed browser work returns in seconds rather than ~45 seconds, while complex tasks may add a short join step.
changes.security_impact: Private tab data remains in the browser/local path; only typed status and provenance cross the relay. Existing unrestricted Mac execution policy remains unchanged.
depends_on: A shared subgoal/job schema across relay and local agent
Capability requirements and health preflight described in the recovery proposal
Receipt attribution for every action and routing tier

changes.change: Add a non-blocking execution preflight and failure-aware recovery ledger for cross-surface actions. Before dispatching browser_* work, sample the existing browser status/heartbeat state and attach a health snapshot (online, lastSeenAt, pending count, tab/session affinity) to the job. If offline or stale, fail fast with a typed reason instead of waiting 45 seconds; if online but a command times out, record one bounded retry only after a fresh heartbeat, then persist a recovery hint for the relay/pendant. Drain or expire stale queued commands by idempotency key so an extension reconnect cannot replay obsolete work. Keep FULL_CONTROL_MODE and all action permissions unchanged; this is observability, faster failure, and recovery, not a gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Browser requests would stop hanging for nearly a minute and then silently repeating. The pendant could say immediately whether the browser is disconnected, retry once when it genuinely returns, and avoid acting on stale commands after reconnection.
changes.effort: Medium: browser health snapshot in jobTracker/executor, typed failure states and bounded retry, plus queue expiry keyed by idempotencyKey; dashboard/relay rendering is a smaller follow-up.
changes.risk: A transient extension stall could be classified as offline or a retry could duplicate a non-idempotent action. Restrict automatic retry to reads and actions explicitly marked idempotent; preserve the existing receipt and expose every retry. Recovery is to rerun from the durable job record.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; saves model turns and local wait time. Small persistent metadata increase per job (health snapshot and retry record).
changes.latency_impact: Healthy browser actions add only a local status check; stale/offline actions return in under a second instead of ~45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: No new authority or data egress. Health metadata contains extension/tab state and should remain in the authenticated local journal; do not include page contents in failure telemetry.
depends_on: Existing GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat routes
Existing GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:jobId, receipts, journal, and idempotency keys
Browser extension emitting reliable lastSeenAt/command acknowledgement

changes.change: Create a single /readiness contract and dashboard/pendant renderer that fuses /ops/status, /browser/status, relay reachability, permission state, and the last 10 journal failures into four independent booleans: shell, app automation, screen/vision, and authenticated browser. Emit a stable blocker code (for example BROWSER_EXTENSION_OFFLINE, ACCESSIBILITY_MISSING, SCREEN_RECORDING_MISSING) with lastSeen, remediation URL/action, and affected queued job IDs. This is reporting only: it must never block FULL_CONTROL actions or silently retry them.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner hears one accurate answer—what the Mac can do right now and the single next fix—rather than seeing generic failures after 45-second browser timeouts. It also prevents an offline extension from being mistaken for a dead Mac or relay.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: schema, reducer, tests against contradictory states (agent ready=false but requiredMissing empty), and dashboard/pendant presentation.
changes.risk: Stale health data could mislead; include timestamps, a short TTL, and an explicit unknown state. Do not expose URLs, tab titles, or command output in the spoken summary.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible; all inputs are local status endpoints and existing receipts, reducing expensive planner retries.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local aggregation; can be polled or pushed on state transitions.
changes.security_impact: Read-only metadata only. Permission remediation must open System Settings but never grant privileges automatically. Preserve unrestricted shell policy.
depends_on: GET /ops/status and /ops/snapshot
GET /browser/status
GET /journal and job receipts
Relay health payload
Dashboard and pendant status-event plumbing

changes.change: Add an encrypted, versioned workspace-checkpoint store distinct from conversational memory. A checkpoint records only resumable handles and metadata: Mac app/window/focus identities, terminal cwd and project/branch, browser session/tab identifiers and URLs, active job IDs with receipt cursors, and the relay task/pipeline identifier. Capture atomically on explicit 'save my workspace', clean shutdown, and detected bridge loss; retain a small ring of checkpoints. Provide a deterministic restore planner that reopens/reattaches what still exists, marks conflicts instead of guessing, and emits a per-item restored/skipped/changed receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After a restart or dropped connection, the owner can say 'continue where I left off' and recover their actual working context instead of manually hunting through apps, tabs, and unfinished jobs. This is continuity across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser—not another single-surface action.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema and encryption, Mac app/window and terminal collectors, browser reattachment, relay linkage, atomic checkpointing, restore conflict UI, and crash-recovery tests.
changes.risk: Window titles, paths, and URLs can be sensitive; encrypt locally, omit content and credentials, support exclusions, and expire old checkpoints. A vanished tab or changed file must be reported as a conflict, never silently substituted. Restore should only reopen or focus; it must not submit, send, delete, or overwrite.
changes.cost_impact: Small local storage and negligible API cost; deterministic restore avoids repeated planner calls. Optional reconciliation can use a cheap model only when identifiers conflict.
changes.latency_impact: Capture under 3 seconds; restore begins within 2 seconds and continues asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: No cookies, passwords, page bodies, microphone data, or document contents leave the Mac. Relay receives only an encrypted checkpoint reference or explicitly permitted metadata.
depends_on: A durable encrypted local checkpoint store
Mac window/focus and terminal-state collector
Browser session/tab reattachment API with stable identifiers
Relay task/pipeline checkpoint linkage
Per-item restore receipts and dashboard/pendant status presentation

changes.change: Turn the existing non-blocking observeBeforeAction signal into a capability-aware fallback hint for the planner. Before dispatch, collect a short-lived readiness snapshot (Accessibility, Screen Recording, browser-extension online/pending age, app automation grants, shell reachability) and annotate the action with viable alternate mechanisms. If a GUI/browser action is unavailable, the planner should automatically choose an equivalent permitted route (for example AppleScript or shell for a Mac setting, authenticated browser bridge versus public fetch) when semantics are equivalent; otherwise fail immediately with the exact missing permission/endpoint and a one-line owner fix. This is advisory routing only: FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unrestricted and no action is refused by policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent stops wasting 45 seconds retrying a browser or GUI action that cannot work on this Mac. It either completes through another surface or tells the owner exactly why it cannot, which is especially valuable from a pendant where a generic failure is hard to act on.
changes.effort: Moderate: normalize existing /ops/status and browser status into a cached readiness object, make executor observations available to the planner/relay, add equivalence mappings for common Mac intents, and include the chosen route plus unavailable alternatives in the receipt.
changes.risk: Fallbacks can have different semantics (AppleScript may affect the wrong app or shell may lack UI context), so mappings must be conservative and explain the substitution. Readiness can go stale between observation and dispatch; mark timestamps and treat it as a hint, never a guarantee. Do not expose permission details or URLs beyond the authenticated owner surfaces.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost: deterministic readiness and route selection avoid planner calls and repeated failed browser timeouts. Small local status probes per job, cached for seconds.
changes.latency_impact: Cuts known-unavailable browser attempts from ~45 seconds to immediate alternate execution or actionable failure; adds only a small preflight probe.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no gates. Permission state and route diagnostics remain local/owner-authenticated; relay receives only a concise reason and selected route. Fallback mappings must preserve existing unrestricted owner policy.
depends_on: Existing read-only /ops/status or /ops/snapshot and /browser/status endpoints
Existing non-blocking observeBeforeAction hook in action receipts
Existing executor route dispatch and relay job completion summaries

changes.change: Add a shell-specific execution adapter beneath FULL_CONTROL_MODE (not a policy gate): launch every run in a tracked process group with a durable job manifest containing cwd, exact command, start time, pid/process-group id, timeout, and redacted environment keys. Append stdout/stderr to a bounded per-job log with monotonically increasing byte/sequence cursors; emit started/heartbeat/output/exit/signal/timeout events to the existing journal and relay. On bridge reconnect, reconcile the process group by manifest and replay events from the last cursor instead of dispatching the command again. Extend the existing action receipt with exit code, signal, elapsed time, last output cursor, and an explicit 'cannot resume' reason for commands that died.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave a compile, export, sync, or test running and later hear the real result rather than a vague timeout or an accidental duplicate run. Failures become actionable (last output, exit signal, cwd, and whether the process is still alive), while unrestricted shell access remains intact.
changes.effort: Medium: a small local supervisor/event journal, relay replay endpoint, and adapters in executor.js plus dashboard/pendant consumers; tests for disconnect, process exit, timeout, and duplicate prevention.
changes.risk: A stale pid or reused process-group id could attach the wrong process; bind manifests to start time and verify command/cwd before reattachment. Log growth and secret leakage are risks; cap bytes, redact known secret patterns, and provide deletion. If reconciliation is uncertain, report 'unknown—no retry' rather than rerun.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model cost for lifecycle events; modest local disk and relay D1 writes per event. One background-tier summarization call only when the owner requests a human explanation of a failure.
changes.latency_impact: Launch remains near current latency. Heartbeats add negligible local work; reconnect status is available in seconds instead of waiting for an HTTP timeout.
changes.security_impact: No new authority and no confirmation gate. It makes existing arbitrary commands more observable; command text and output tails are sensitive and must use the existing authenticated Mac/relay paths with retention limits.
depends_on: A durable relay event stream with replay-from-sequence semantics
A local process supervisor that survives the request handler and records manifests
Wire shell lifecycle events into existing /journal, /jobs, and receipt APIs
Pendant notification consumer for completion/failure

changes.change: Add a cross-surface incident-correlation ledger, not another executor: on every Mac, browser, relay, or pendant failure, write a compact append-only event keyed by a shared correlationId and actionId; asynchronously join events by time window and parent job, attach the existing receipt/undo verdict, record disconnect/reconnect gaps, and expose one redacted incident bundle through the dashboard. Start with local-agent hooks around executor.js and browserBridge result handling, relay ingestion from pipeline events, and a pendant event envelope carrying boot/session sequence numbers. Deduplicate retries and reconnects by idempotency key; retain raw evidence locally and only upload redacted excerpts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a failure crosses devices, the owner sees one truthful timeline—what the pendant heard, what the relay dispatched, what the Mac/browser attempted, and where it stopped—instead of several incomplete job records. It directly enables the owner's requested self-filed pendant bug reports and makes support/debugging possible without asking them to reproduce the problem.
changes.effort: Medium: shared event schema and local hooks first, relay append/query and correlation worker second, dashboard incident panel and pendant envelope third. Add deterministic tests for dropped links, duplicate results, clock skew, and redaction.
changes.risk: Incorrect time correlation could merge two simultaneous jobs or split one across reconnects. Mitigate with parent IDs, monotonic device sequence numbers, confidence labels, and never deleting source receipts. If correlation fails, preserve separate events and show the uncertainty rather than inventing a story. UART/log volume must be capped and backpressured so audio and action latency are unaffected.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost for collection/correlation; optional background summarization costs about 1–2 cents per incident. Small D1/R2 growth from bounded redacted bundles; local ring buffers avoid shipping every raw log.
changes.latency_impact: No synchronous network dependency on action execution. Hook overhead should be under 5 ms; incident joining and summarization happen asynchronously, with a draft visible in roughly 1–3 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive stdout, environment variables, bearer tokens, cookies, authenticated page content, and secret UART fields are redacted before relay persistence. Preserve hashes and source locations for integrity. Raw logs stay on-device unless the owner explicitly exports them. This adds observability, not a gate or reduced access.
depends_on: A versioned event envelope shared by local-agent, relay, browser bridge, and pendant firmware
A pendant UART ring buffer and bounded event export
A relay incident storage/query route and retention policy
A local-agent failure-event hook for shell, typed actions, browser actions, timeouts, and planner errors

changes.change: Add a low-power wear/presence sensor and a hardware privacy state to the pendant: detect skin contact or lanyard removal, latch a local microphone/audio-capture mute and emit signed wear-state transitions over the existing radio link. Relay, Mac, and browser bridges consume that state as a shared session signal: when unworn, stop starting new capture or browser reads and mark in-flight work as paused; when worn again, resume only explicitly resumable work. Include a physical LED indication and a button override for false positives, with the state retained through brief link loss.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear the pendant all day without wondering whether it is listening or whether a private Mac/browser task will continue after they set it down. Removing it would be an immediate, visible privacy boundary that works even when the relay or Mac is unreachable, while putting it back on restores continuity instead of losing the session.
changes.effort: Hardware revision for a capacitive electrode or optical/proximity sensor, firmware debounce/calibration and signed event framing, relay session-state propagation, and Mac/browser hooks that pause only resumable work. Add tests for removal during speech, radio loss, false contact, charging, and rapid wear transitions.
changes.risk: A bad fit or clothing could cause false removal and interrupt a conversation; calibration, hysteresis, LED feedback, and an explicit button override mitigate this. A sensor failure must fail closed for capture but must not erase queued work. Do not infer identity or store biometric measurements—persist only boolean state, transition time, and confidence.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $0.20–$2 for a capacitive/proximity component and PCB/layout revision, with sub-milliamp average draw. Negligible API cost; only tiny state events cross the relay.
changes.latency_impact: Local mute/latch should take under 100 ms and must not depend on the network. Cross-surface pause notification should arrive within the normal link heartbeat, with reconnect reconciliation on return.
changes.security_impact: Strengthens privacy at the device boundary: local hardware mute is authoritative and signed wear events prevent an untrusted bridge from claiming the pendant is present. It introduces no new private data beyond presence transitions and should default to unworn on ambiguous sensor state.
depends_on: A pendant firmware event type for signed wear-state transitions
A local hardware mute path that survives dropped links
Relay session-state propagation to the Mac and browser bridge
Mac/browser job semantics that distinguish resumable from non-resumable work

changes.change: Add a non-blocking capability preflight and outcome verifier to every desktop action. Before UI actions, read the existing /observe reachability facts (Accessibility trusted/eventsPost, Screen Recording, secure input, foreground app, browser session); annotate the planned action with reachable/unreachable capabilities. After execution, run a typed postcondition probe appropriate to the action (frontmost app/window, volume, file hash, browser tab URL/title, or a bounded UI-state signal). If UI input is unreachable or the postcondition is false, mark the receipt as `not_verified` rather than success and automatically choose an equivalent available route (AppleScript/system API for app settings, shell for files/status, browser bridge for tabs), retaining the original attempt and fallback as one causal action group. Persist preflight, verification, fallback reason, and evidence IDs in /jobs/:id/receipts and expose aggregate unreachable-capability counts in /observe or /ops/snapshot. This is observability and recovery only: it must never block an action or add confirmation gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today the Mac reports clicks, typing, and key presses as successful even though the live host says Accessibility is not trusted and synthesized events are rejected. The owner can believe a task completed when nothing changed. This makes spoken completion reports honest and lets the system finish the same goal through a working path automatically, while showing exactly why a UI attempt was replaced.
