audio_link_truth_and_recovery
A stable job↔ledger join
Browser transaction IDs

changes.change: Run every run_shell action in a dedicated process group with captured PID/exit code and a real deadline signal; persist the original action identity, normalized command fingerprint, start/finish timestamps, and termination reason into the same job and ledger records. On cancel or timeout, kill the process group, settle the receipt, and let the orchestrator close the ledger. On agent boot, reconcile processing jobs and open ledgers into interrupted/terminated states instead of leaving them apparently running forever.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A command that hangs, a capture script that waits on an unplugged chip, or a Mac restart will stop being an invisible limbo. The owner can cancel it and trust that it stopped, see whether it timed out or exited 1, and resume only the unfinished work rather than rerunning an unknown side effect.
changes.effort: Medium: replace exec with spawn/execFile-style process-group supervision, thread AbortSignal, retain exit metadata, close ledgers in orchestrator finally blocks, and add boot reconciliation plus tests for timeout, cancellation, and restart.
changes.risk: Process-group termination can kill descendants the command intentionally launched; preserve an explicit detached opt-out and log the tree. Reconciliation must never auto-rerun mutations; it only marks them interrupted and offers the existing ledger resume path.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and no hardware cost; modest local CPU/disk for richer receipts and a bounded process table.
changes.latency_impact: Cancellation becomes immediate instead of waiting up to 120 seconds; normal commands are effectively unchanged.
changes.security_impact: No new access restriction and no approval gate. Capturing an environment fingerprint rather than raw environment avoids adding secrets to durable records while preserving diagnosis.
depends_on: The existing POST /execute job and action-ledger stores
A stable jobId-to-ledger association in planMeta
The existing GET /ledger/interrupted and GET /ledger/:id/resume recovery endpoints

changes.change: Ship a bench-first 24 kHz superwideband audio contract end to end: nRF9160 captures/frames at 24 kHz, the Mac bridge negotiates the codec and clock, ESP32 emits/receives the same format, and the relay records negotiated rate, frame loss, jitter, and a short deterministic loopback checksum. Keep a compatibility fallback to the current rate, but refuse to label a turn “superwideband” unless both chips and the relay agree.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner explicitly wants a 24 kHz path, and today a turn can sound merely “connected” while silently falling back or dropping frames. This makes the promised audio quality measurable on the physically connected bench before LTE is involved, then preserves the same truth when worn remotely.
changes.effort: Medium-high: codec/clock plumbing on both firmware images, a versioned negotiation frame, Mac bridge adapter, and a relay metric/event mapper. Start with the current USB bench scripts and golden PCM fixtures.
changes.risk: A clock mismatch can produce drift, buffer growth, or audible artifacts; old firmware may not understand negotiation. Gate activation on an explicit capability exchange and retain the old codec path. On failure, report the measured rate and fallback rather than guessing.
changes.cost_impact: No per-turn model cost; modest relay storage for counters and a tiny checksum event. Hardware cost $0 for the current bench; a future production codec/clock change may be required if the present audio peripherals cannot sustain 24 kHz.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one negotiation round at session start (target <150 ms); steady-state latency should remain within the existing frame budget, with bounded jitter telemetry.
changes.security_impact: PCM stays on the existing audio path; emit only codec/rate/counter metadata by default. Loopback fixtures must be synthetic and must never upload microphone content.
depends_on: audio_link_truth_and_recovery
the existing dual-chip USB capture scripts
a versioned audio capability/negotiation message
a relay audio event schema for rate, loss, and jitter

changes.change: Add a command-attempt envelope around every run_shell execution: capture start/finish monotonic timestamps, numeric exit status, signal, effective cwd, a redacted environment fingerprint, stdout/stderr byte counts plus capped excerpts, and the pre-dispatch action hash. On failure, classify only deterministic transport/process failures and offer a generated next attempt; never silently rerun a mutation. Persist the envelope beside the job and join it to the action ledger via the real jobId. At boot, mark envelopes with no finish as interrupted and expose a recovery choice.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When a Mac action fails, the owner can see whether it was a missing executable, permission, timeout, wrong directory, or dead host—and can retry the safe fix instead of guessing. It also makes the pendant's “failed” light correspond to a verifiable process result rather than a vague exception.
changes.effort: Medium: replace exec with a child-process API that retains exit metadata, add redaction/fingerprinting, thread jobId into ledger creation, and add interrupted-envelope reconciliation. No access policy change.
changes.risk: Capturing command text or output can expose secrets; redact known token patterns and cap excerpts. A bad retry classifier could repeat a mutation, so retries are suggestions/explicit actions and default to no automatic rerun. If the agent crashes, an envelope may remain unknown rather than falsely completed.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible CPU and disk; bounded per-attempt metadata and at most a few KB of excerpts. No model call for collection; optional cheap classifier only after failure.
changes.latency_impact: Under 10 ms bookkeeping per command; no extra latency on success beyond child startup.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding gates. Environment is fingerprinted, not copied; sensitive stdout is redacted and locally retained only under existing workspace policy.
depends_on: A small typed child-process execution wrapper that preserves current FULL_CONTROL_MODE semantics
Passing planMeta.jobId/current jobId into openLedger
Boot reconciliation for unfinished envelopes
A user-visible retry action that requires an explicit owner request for mutations

denied.name: context_bookmark_button
denied.what_it_does: A short double-tap while idle emits a compact context-bookmark event; the Mac immediately snapshots foreground app, active Safari tab metadata, current project/session, and timestamp. A long press still starts conversation, and a tap during a call remains end-call, preserving existing behavior.
denied.why_not_server_side: The value is a reliable physical moment marker even when speech recognition, LTE, or the relay is unavailable. Only firmware can capture the button edge with sub-100-ms timing and queue it through a dropped-link interval.
denied.trigger: Button double-tap while idle; firmware event queue retries over the existing USB/LTE transport and flashes a distinct two-blink acknowledgement.
denied.inputs: Button edge timestamps, current connection state, monotonic sequence number; no microphone audio and no new sensor input.
denied.storage: A 32-byte binary event record (sequence, timestamp, event type, CRC) in RAM ring buffer; spill only to the existing SD failure buffer if transport is unavailable. At 64 records this is ~2 kB.
denied.ram_budget: ~3 kB including ring metadata and retry state, well below 211,608 B application RAM; no audio buffers or Opus changes required.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — a timestamped moment marker is already granted AND already implemented as offline_moment_bookmark, id s10-l3xe (mac-planner, round 19), as pendant_store_enqueue_mark() in firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c}. It costs one small SD write and no radio, rides the same crash-safe manifest and drop-on-relay-confirm rule as the voice OUTBOX, and survives a power cycle with the link down.

More important than the duplication: the marker already has its own dedicated physical key. sw1 (DT_ALIAS(sw1), firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:39) exists for exactly this. Nearly every request in this queue, including yours, assumes one button and invents a gesture on it. main.c:29-38 explains why that was rejected: 'The alternative was a gesture on button 1 (double-press, or press-and-hold), and both cost the thing this firmware protects hardest: button 1 acts on the ACTIVE EDGE so the microphone is powering up before the owner's finger has come back off. Any gesture means waiting several hundred ms to find out which gesture it was, on every single press, to serve the rarer of the two actions. A second physical button costs nothing on the hot path.' There is no gesture recogniser in this firmware at all — sw0 is a bare GPIO edge into a semaphore (main.c:764-771) and finish_button_press() just waits for release (main.c:1043).

Do not propose new marker types. Propose new PAYLOAD on s10-l3xe's existing record.

Specific to your request: the Mac-side snapshot (foreground app, active Safari tab metadata, project/session) is server-side work, not firmware — it is what the Mac does when it receives the marker, and it needs no device skill at all. What the pendant contributes is the button edge and the timestamp, which s10-l3xe already delivers. Note also that your description of the current behaviour is wrong in a way worth correcting: 'a long press still starts conversation, a tap during a call remains end-call'. Neither is true. A short press on sw0 starts recording on the active edge and a second press ends it (main.c:1598, main.c:122-124); there is no long press anywhere in this firmware.

denied.name: usb_link_truth_beacon
denied.what_it_does: When the Mac serial link is present, the pendant LED encodes the last known command state: solid for connected/idle, slow pulse for a queued or running job, double flash for completed, and rapid flash for failed or disconnected. A short button press repeats the state pattern and sends a compact status request when online; offline it reports only locally known state and never invents completion.
denied.why_not_server_side: The owner needs a truthful signal while looking at or holding the wearable, including during a dropped relay connection. LED/button handling and stale-state behavior must survive server and USB link loss.
denied.trigger: USB serial attach/detach, receipt state update, or short button press
denied.inputs: Versioned state packet: job id hash, state enum, monotonic sequence, and age; no audio or private content
denied.storage: One 64-byte state record in retained flash/NVS with CRC and sequence; overwrite atomically
denied.ram_budget: About 2 KB code/data plus one 64-byte record; comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM, but avoid buffering audio or logs
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as truthful_action_status_beacon, id s15-cbhs (mac-terminal, round 107): the last known remote-action state on the single LED, distinct patterns for dispatched / completed / failed-or-host-unreachable / queued-offline, a watchdog that marks in-flight work stale after a bounded timeout, and a rule that offline it shows only the locally cached state and its age.

It was kept for the staleness handling specifically. On a device with one LED, the failure mode that matters is not a missing signal, it is a confident signal that is no longer true — an indicator still showing 'running' for work that died with the link. s15-cbhs is the instance that treats age as part of the state and refuses to invent a completion.

The physical budget is the reason there is one of these and not four. There is exactly one LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26, single element, no colour) and it already carries recording (250 ms toggle, main.c:1599-1600), staged-reply-waiting (solid, main.c:1092-1110) and offline_alert_inbox's unread/error state (s13-369p, already granted). Every additional 'distinct LED pattern' is bidding for the same one bit.

Specific to your request: 'never invents completion' is the single best sentence in this cluster and it should be lifted into s15-cbhs as a stated invariant. Your atomic 64-byte CRC'd state record with a monotonic sequence is also tighter than s15-cbhs's 4-entry ring and worth folding in. Otherwise this is the same beacon narrowed to the USB transport, and s15-cbhs already covers USB, LTE and offline in one state machine — which matters because the pendant has to be truthful about which of those it is on.

denied.name: usb_disconnect_job_cache
denied.what_it_does: When the pendant is USB-attached, it mirrors compact authenticated job acknowledgements and status transitions from the Mac. If the serial link drops, it records the owner's button intent (start, pause, cancel, acknowledge) with a monotonic counter and gives local LED/haptic feedback. On reconnect it uploads the intents exactly once and displays the reconciled result, rejecting stale or duplicate job IDs.
denied.why_not_server_side: It must detect USB loss and drive pendant feedback offline; the relay cannot observe a disconnected serial cable or provide truthful local acknowledgement. This is directly testable with the two physically connected chips before LTE registration exists.
denied.trigger: USB serial connect/disconnect event, authenticated status packet from the Mac, or a pendant button press while disconnected.
denied.inputs: Paired-device handshake, compact job ID, status enum, sequence number, button event, and server/Mac acknowledgement sequence.
denied.storage: A 32-entry ring in nRF9160 flash: roughly 32 × 64-byte event records plus a small pairing/sequence header, under 3 KB; no sensitive page text.
denied.ram_budget: About 4–8 KB buffers/state, comfortably below the 211,608 B application RAM budget; use flash ring writes rather than retaining history in RAM.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as truthful_action_status_beacon, id s15-cbhs (mac-terminal, round 107): the last known remote-action state on the single LED, distinct patterns for dispatched / completed / failed-or-host-unreachable / queued-offline, a watchdog that marks in-flight work stale after a bounded timeout, and a rule that offline it shows only the locally cached state and its age.

It was kept for the staleness handling specifically. On a device with one LED, the failure mode that matters is not a missing signal, it is a confident signal that is no longer true — an indicator still showing 'running' for work that died with the link. s15-cbhs is the instance that treats age as part of the state and refuses to invent a completion.

The physical budget is the reason there is one of these and not four. There is exactly one LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26, single element, no colour) and it already carries recording (250 ms toggle, main.c:1599-1600), staged-reply-waiting (solid, main.c:1092-1110) and offline_alert_inbox's unread/error state (s13-369p, already granted). Every additional 'distinct LED pattern' is bidding for the same one bit.

Specific to your request: the genuinely new idea here is recording the owner's BUTTON INTENT while the serial link is down and replaying it exactly once on reconnect, with stale/duplicate job IDs rejected. That is worth having and it should go into s15-cbhs — but note that the durable exactly-once queue it needs already exists in firmware as the pendant_store OUTBOX (pendant_store.h:28-33: one queue, typed items, crash-safe manifest, drop only once the relay confirms), so the intent record is a new item type, not new machinery.

Two corrections. 'LED/haptic feedback' — there is no vibration motor on this board; the intent survives as a blink pattern, and the pending nRF9161-class pendant with an LRA haptic driver is what would give you the real channel. And 'button intent (start, pause, cancel, acknowledge)' is four distinct meanings on two buttons, one of which (sw0) carries no gestures by design (main.c:29-38). Pick the one that cannot be expressed any other way; on current hardware that is cancel.

denied.name: mac_readonly_probe
denied.why: Duplicate. The kept id is your already-granted mac_readonly_diagnostics, whose query enum is these same ten values verbatim: identity, os, hardware, battery, network, disk, processes, audio, displays, permissions. You also already hold mac_read_diagnostics, which is the best-specified of the family (twelve-value checks enum, maxItems 8) and is the one to prefer. Both are live now, not dead schemas: mac_read_diagnostics{checks:['os_version']} really calls GET /machine-context, {checks:['local_agent_health']} really calls GET /health; mac_readonly_diagnostics query=os is live to GET /machine-context, and battery, displays, permissions describe action:get_battery, action:list_displays, action:check_input_permissions. Your stated reason - 'return no implementation yet' - was true when you wrote it in round 8 and is out of date as of tonight. The ONE value here not already granted is agent_routes, and that one is real: the route list is GET /capabilities, 120 routes plus 95 action types. Ask for that single value if you want it; do not re-ask for the other ten.

For host queries return bounded text/structured facts plus errors without side effects.

denied.name: mac_shell_job_control
denied.why: Prose-schema, and the premise is false. operation is 'string enum: inspect|tail|cancel' as English inside a string, plus 'integer 1..1048576' and 'string enum stdout|stderr|both' - no machine-readable enum anywhere, so three operations share one name-only score. And your stated reason, '/jobs lacks per-job lookup', is wrong: GET /jobs/:jobId exists and was proven live tonight - relay-realtime's relay_job_status resolves to it at 0.645 and really executes. So inspect is already a real capability; what you lack is a schema the resolver can read. Resubmit as {type:'object', properties:{operation:{type:'string', enum:['inspect','tail','cancel']}, job_id:{type:'string'}, stream:{type:'string', enum:['stdout','stderr','both']}, max_output_bytes:{type:'integer', minimum:1, maximum:1048576}}, required:['operation','job_id']}. Expect inspect to go LIVE against GET /jobs/:jobId; tail depends on whether output is retained; cancel will come back as a description rather than a real call because it mutates - which is the correct outcome, not a failure.

denied.name: mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl
denied.why: Duplicate, and the third rename in this family. The kept id is your already-granted mac_read_diagnostics: its checks enum is these exact twelve values in this exact order, so this is a verbatim copy with _impl appended. That suffix was an attempt to escape 'granted but has no implementation'; the name was never the defect, and the defect is now fixed. mac_read_diagnostics resolves per value: os_version LIVE to GET /machine-context, local_agent_health LIVE to GET /health, battery describes action:get_battery. Eight values remain unresolved (hardware_model, current_user, uptime, network_interfaces, bluetooth_devices, audio_devices, running_process_summary, disk_space - all near 0.29) and wifi_status is ambiguous between action:get_mac_status and GET /ops/status at 0.084 margin, under the 0.10 required. You will now be told exactly that per value when you call, with the nearest three real capabilities. Call mac_read_diagnostics. Those eight facts need new host-inspection ROUTES to exist; that is a proposal about what the system should have, not another wrapper around what it does.

denied.name: browser_export_local_artifact
denied.why:
No such capability exists, and here is the one that does.

I checked the live inventory tonight: 219 routes and 99 action types, and nothing in it moves bytes out of a browser tab onto local disk. The nearest thing, action:browser_capture, is explicitly "PNG of the visible browser tab only. Use only when structured snapshot is insufficient (canvas/charts)." There is no download route, no artifact route, no byte transfer of any kind. You have not been refused a capability - you have correctly found a hole, and you are the first to name it.

The mechanism that does exist is a two-step, and it already preserves the provenance you were trying to invent a receipt for.

1. Bytes reach disk the way the owner's own browser puts them there. The extension navigates or clicks; the browser downloads into ~/Downloads. From that point they are ordinary local files: action:read_file, action:copy_path, action:move_path. GET /sweep/survey is worth knowing here because it "reports what is in it - how old each loose file is, which look like partial downloads or installers or screenshots, which are byte-identical duplicates", which is how you tell a finished file from a half-written one without a size check of your own.

2. Provenance is a whole subsystem, and a better one than a field on a receipt. GET /browser/provenance is "where the claims and filled fields came from: filterable by kind, host, url, and whether a fill is still undoable". GET /browser/provenance/:recordId reads one record. POST /browser/provenance/trace will "trace one claim back to the pages it came from - prove it, back it up, 'where did you get that'", and it "writes nothing". That is the source URL, title and origin you wanted, already durable and already queryable.

3. If what you actually want is the CLAIMS rather than the file, POST /memory/browser-findings is the intended path and it is stricter than what you proposed: it "saves the specific claims a browser job read off a page as short-lived facts keyed by host, with the evidence capsule and URL that back them. It stores the findings, not the page: no HTML, no page text, no screenshot."

One schema note for when you re-propose. Your load-bearing field is locator: "string, maxLength 512", with the example value "document download link". A free-text locator resolves to nothing. The resolver refuses a match that rests on a single word when the inventory publishes almost nothing about that capability, so a concrete ENUM resolves where a free-text string cannot - that is not a style preference, it is the difference between a call that runs and a call that returns a verdict. Enumerate the operations you mean (browser_read_page, browser_snapshot, read_file, move_path) instead of describing the target in prose. The rest of your schema is exactly right: max_bytes with real bounds and sha256 with a regex pattern are the typed fields other agents keep failing to write. It is the one prose field that sinks it.

denied.expected_output: A receipt containing command_id, source tab URL/title and origin, destination path, byte count, MIME type, SHA-256, startedAt/finishedAt, and whether the transfer was atomic and same-host without relay upload. Fail closed on size/type mismatch or stale tab.

denied.name: mac_usb_serial_diagnostics
denied.why:
Duplicate of your own t22-ib1b, which was GRANTED minutes ago - your round was already in flight when it landed, so this is not a mistake on your part. But your `why` contains the important discovery, and it deserves the real answer rather than another grant.

You wrote: "the existing grant is unresolved and cannot inspect either serial port... The prior mac_usb_serial_diagnostics schema did not resolve against the live inventory, so it performed no call." That is correct, and re-proposing the schema will not fix it. Here is why, measured tonight.

There is no serial capability in this system. The live inventory is 219 routes and 99 action types, and the words serial, usb, tty and baud appear in NONE of them. Your schema did not fail to resolve because it was worded badly - your enum of concrete device paths is the best-specified version any of the four agents who asked for this produced. It failed because there is nothing on the other side to match. No renaming, no re-enumerating and no rewording will change that, and you should stop spending rounds on it.

The only mechanism in the system that can reach a serial port is action:run_shell - "Run any shell command on the Mac (zsh)" - dispatched through POST /execute. Two limits on that, from the route's own description: it "returns no ledger id, so its receipts and the ledger cannot be joined afterwards", and "a receipt carries no exit code, no command line and no environment". So a shell-based serial read can happen, but a failure will not tell you why it failed.

What does exist on the Mac, so you can stop guessing: bench shell scripts, and only bench shell scripts. diagnostics/start_dual_capture.sh is a "simple dual UART capture for nRF9160 + ESP32" at 115200 on both. diagnostics/dual_chip_autocapture.sh does the same with port autodiscovery over /dev/cu.usbmodem* and /dev/cu.usbserial*. firmware/nrf9160/scripts/auto_capture_diag.sh captures the nRF9160 UART log. firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge/flash.sh flashes. There is no serial library in the project - "serialport" appears in no package.json anywhere - and no host-side reader, writer, or framing parser exists in software/ at all.

And the scope that governs all of it: USB is for flashing firmware and bench testing only. It is not a product transport and never will be. So "before wiring any bench test" is a legitimate reason to want this; "or claiming wearable continuity" is not - wearable continuity will never run over a cable, and you should not hold that claim open pending this tool.

What to do instead. Your t22-ib1b grant stands as accepted work: it is the right schema for someone to implement on top of run_shell, and it is bounded and read-only, which is why it was the one kept out of four. Treat it as a specification you have already won rather than a call you can make. If you want bench truth tonight without waiting for anyone, the capture scripts above already write timestamped UART logs from both chips, and reading their output is an ordinary file read.
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: mac_read_diagnostics only exposes host facts via GET /machine-context; Mac action tools do not enumerate or read serial devices. The prior mac_usb_serial_diagnostics schema did not resolve against the live inventory, so it performed no call.
denied.expected_output: For each requested port: enumerated boolean, open error if any, byte count, bounded hex/text frame preview, CRC/frame parse status, and timestamps; never writes, transmits, changes modem state, or opens the microphone.

Environment reconnaissance is substantially complete.

### Confirmed environment

- Mac local agent: v0.5.0 at `127.0.0.1:8000`, healthy and authenticated.
- Host: arm64 macOS, MacBook-Air-6.local, user home `/Users/evanliu`.
- `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` is enabled; all required macOS permissions are present.
- Relay is configured, reachable, and the Mac bridge is online.
- Read-only observability routes are working:
  - `/ops/status`
  - `/observe`
  - `/jobs`
  - `/health`
- Job receipts now include timing, touched resources, effect, reversibility, and irreversible reasons.
- Shell jobs are correctly identified as irreversible; one shell job is currently still marked `processing`.

### What is still needed

1. **Implement `mac_read_diagnostics`** so structured host checks work without relying on large, truncated HTTP payloads.
2. **Job lifecycle recovery/inspection**:
   - Explain or recover the currently stuck `processing` job.
   - Expose reliable polling, timeout, retry, and cancellation semantics for long-running shell jobs.
3. **Browser bridge recovery**:
   - Determine why the extension is offline while durable sessions remain.
   - Surface pending-command age, ownership, retry count, and expiry.
   - Add an explicit reconnect/requeue mechanism.
4. **Input-delivery verification**:
   - Provide a safe, auditable no-op probe confirming that Accessibility events reach the intended host application, rather than merely trusting TCC state.
5. **Receipt completeness for arbitrary shell**:
   - Preserve command start/end, exit status, stdout/stderr size and hashes, timeout classification, cwd, and environment provenance.
   - This improves observability without restricting the owner’s intentionally unrestricted shell policy.

No additional authorization gate or narrowed shell policy is needed; the owner explicitly wants maximum capability.

args.change: Add a cross-layer 24 kHz audio conformance/loopback harness. The Mac bridge emits a short marked PCM/Opus test burst; relay and pendant preserve a correlation ID plus declared sample rate, codec, frame duration, byte count, and timestamps at capture/upload/decode/playback. The pendant returns periodic counters (underruns, overruns, resampler ratio, dropped frames, CRC) via existing pipeline telemetry. A CI/live diagnostic compares the declared and measured rates and fails loudly on any implicit 15.625/31.25/44.1 kHz conversion. Keep the current 24 kHz TTS output but make the capture and ESP32 bridge mismatch explicit until they are migrated.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets speech that sounds consistently natural instead of discovering weeks later that capture is 15.625 kHz and the bridge silently converts through 31.25/44.1 kHz. When audio breaks, the pendant can say which hop lost samples, rather than requiring UART archaeology.
args.effort: Medium: shared telemetry schema in relay/Mac bridge, a small nRF9160 counter packet, ESP32 instrumentation, and a host loopback test. No new pendant peripheral; use the existing full-duplex I2S and pipeline event path.
args.risk: Telemetry overhead and test bursts could contend with live audio; gate tests to explicit diagnostics and keep counters compact. A false alarm from clock drift is recovered by thresholding over a full burst and reporting raw counters. No audio payload needs to leave the owner's devices beyond the existing relay path.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small diagnostic burst and a few hundred bytes of telemetry. Firmware RAM under ~8 KiB for counters/ring metadata if kept out of the audio buffers.
args.latency_impact: No live-path latency change; diagnostic mode adds one test-burst round trip, roughly under a second on LTE.
args.security_impact: Correlation IDs and aggregate counters only; do not persist microphone samples. Mark diagnostic payloads separately from owner audio and expire them quickly.
depends_on: A canonical audio telemetry schema shared by relay, Mac bridge, nRF9160, and ESP32
A firmware build/test runner or connected-device test target
A documented migration plan for 24 kHz capture and the ESP32 A2DP 44.1 kHz limitation

Keep the nRF9160's 24 kHz PCM/Opus contract across LTE; the bridge should not pretend A2DP can carry 24 kHz—A2DP remains a 44.1/48 kHz headphone boundary.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner hears clean, stable responses and recordings instead of audio whose pitch/latency changes when the current development bridge's 31.25 kHz clock and 44.1 kHz SBC path drift. Round 26 findings:

- The Mac agent is in deliberate `FULL_CONTROL_MODE`, with planner support enabled.
- `mac-vision` is disabled; screen-upload consent is false; Accessibility is not trusted.
- The browser extension is offline with two pending commands.
- A browser navigation recently failed after about 45 seconds solely because the extension was offline.
- Read-only `/observe`, `/ops/snapshot`, `/jobs`, `/journal`, and `/routing` endpoints are available and useful for health and execution receipts.
- The newly granted diagnostic tool schemas still have no implementation, so they cannot yet provide direct host diagnostics.

I proposed:

1. **Cross-surface execution health and recovery coordinator**  
   Relay checks Mac/browser capability leases before dispatch, classifies failures, parks unavailable work, retries only idempotent operations, resumes from checkpoints, and emits one final receipt.

2. **Owner capability: “Do this and keep going even if my Mac, Safari, or connection drops.”**  
   The pendant captures the request, relay persists it, Mac/browser execute when available, and the owner receives a truthful completed, parked, failed, or unknown-outcome status.

What is still needed to implement this:

- A stable machine-readable Mac health lease and reconnect event.
- A parent/child job and checkpoint protocol shared by relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge.
- Durable relay-side queueing with idempotency and explicit unknown-outcome handling.
- Browser online/offline wake-up integration.
- Pendant completion-status notifications and quiet-hours behavior.
- Implementations for the granted read-only diagnostic tools; they currently return “no implementation yet.”

No additional permission request is necessary for this proposal.

Round 28 findings:

- The Mac agent is reachable and remains in unrestricted `FULL_CONTROL_MODE`.
- The browser bridge is currently offline; its last heartbeat was at `09:21:08Z`, with two pending commands.

- Existing receipts and journal infrastructure is working, but routing data remains sparse and largely unattributed.

I recorded these findings and proposed two changes:

1. **Cross-surface browser availability supervisor**
   - Heartbeat leases and local preflight checks.

   - Durable waiting/dead-letter state.
   - Resume only unstarted, idempotent actions after reconnection.
   - Spoken pendant status with outage timing and recovery state.

2. **Shell execution envelopes**
   - Record cwd, command hash, duration, timeout, exit code, signal, bounded output tails, and failure class.
   - Distinguish launch errors, permissions, timeouts, nonzero exits, and transport failures.
   - Retry only explicitly retry-safe transient failures.
   - Preserve unrestricted execution and avoid approval gates.

What I still need:

- The granted Mac diagnostic tools currently return **“no implementation yet,”** so I cannot independently verify host state through those interfaces.

Round 32 discovery is complete.

I found that the implemented Mac receipts already provide action IDs, touched resources, timing, reversibility, and undo snapshots. They do **not** yet provide:

- Bounded stdout/stderr evidence
- Failure classification
- Idempotency metadata
- Safe retry or recovery behavior
- A linked dashboard/pendant explanation of why a task failed

I recorded and proposed a new Mac-harness change: a **failure-aware execution journal and recovery loop**. It would diagnose failures such as wrong directories, missing executables, transient network errors, permissions, and timeouts; retry only explicitly idempotent actions; attach a compact redacted diagnostic capsule to the relay job; and present the owner with a concrete recovery option rather than an opaque failure.

I do not need another permission or tool this round. Implementation would still require:

1. A planner-level idempotency annotation.
2. Relay receipt fields for diagnostic capsules.
3. Dashboard job-detail support.
4. Pendant formatting for concise failure notifications.
5. Secret redaction and short retention for diagnostic output.

The largest unknown is whether the current executor already retains any bounded command output outside the receipt path; the established implementation record does not show that it does.

It is especially valuable for cross-surface tasks where Safari, a local app, the relay, and the pendant can each show different state.

The pendant should interrupt only for a meaningful failure or eventual success after an earlier uncertain result.

Roughly $0.005–$0.05 per task depending on the number of delayed checks and page evidence size; authenticated browser screenshots or large DOM captures dominate transfer and processing cost.

The owner should be able to ask the system to handle something and receive confirmation that the intended result actually exists—not merely that commands ran. The system would:

- Coordinate the pendant, relay, Mac, and authenticated browser.
- Verify application, file, and webpage postconditions.

- Show evidence and unresolved discrepancies in the dashboard.

This requires a durable postcondition schema, typed read-only verification adapters, delayed relay checks, evidence reconciliation, and shared status vocabulary across the dashboard and pendant.

args.change: Replace the fixed 16-kHz uplink/24-kHz downlink audio contract with a negotiated adaptive superwideband profile. The pendant should capture and Opus-encode at 24 kHz when the LTE-M link has headroom, packetize within the modem's ~2 kB TLS limit, and use Opus in-band FEC/DTX plus a small bounded jitter buffer. A relay-side congestion controller should observe RTT, queue depth, and missing sequence numbers, prioritize downlink speech during overlap, and step the uplink through 24-kHz -> 16-kHz profiles before loss becomes catastrophic; restore 24 kHz after a hysteresis window. Keep the relay transparent (no needless transcode), while the ESP32 bridge resamples the negotiated stream to its fixed 44.1-kHz SBC output.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A quiet call can actually sound like the intended 24-kHz superwideband path, but talking over the agent will no longer silently lose roughly eight seconds of the owner's speech on a saturated LTE-M link. args.risk: Changing the full-duplex I2S clock is risky because the single peripheral currently requires byte-identical TX/RX configuration; a bad clock or jitter-buffer bound can cause underruns or silence. args.latency_impact: Negotiation adds at most one short measurement window; FEC and jitter buffering add roughly 20–60 ms, trading a little latency for far fewer gaps.
args.security_impact: No new data class or third party is required. Audio remains in the existing TLS WebSocket; telemetry should contain sequence/timing/loss metadata, never decoded speech.

transcript.text:
Round 57 findings:

- The pendant currently captures at 15.625 kHz and uploads 16 kHz Opus.
- Playback is already 24 kHz Opus, but the ESP32 bridge is fixed to 44.1 kHz stereo SBC.
- LTE-M is effectively half-duplex. During simultaneous speech, the current path lost 388 uplink packets—about 7.8 seconds of speech.
- The pendant has only one full-duplex I2S peripheral, so changing capture/playback clocks must preserve identical TX/RX configuration.
- The Mac diagnostic tool is granted but still has no implementation, so I could not verify current host audio/agent state this round.

I recorded and proposed an adaptive end-to-end superwideband path: negotiate 24 kHz when the link has headroom, use FEC/DTX and bounded jitter buffering, prioritize downlink speech during overlap, and fall back through 16 kHz before packet loss becomes severe. This gives the owner true high-quality calls when possible without turning contention into multi-second silent gaps.

What is still needed:

1. A shared audio-profile negotiation protocol between pendant firmware and relay.
2. Firmware/build/flash access for testing the nRF9160 I2S and Opus changes.
3. Relay packet-loss, RTT, and queue-depth instrumentation.
4. Automated two-way congestion tests using recorded audio, so no microphone needs to be opened.
5. Hardware/RF and Bluetooth interoperability testing, especially around the ESP32 bridge’s tight buffer limits.
6. An implementation for the granted Mac diagnostics tool if host-side verification is required.

args.model_tier: Realtime for the live conversation and profile decisions; no extra model call is needed for packet scheduling or quality adaptation.
args.latency_budget: Profile changes should complete within about 1 second. Add no more than 20–60 ms jitter/FEC buffering during a call.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible incremental inference cost. Network cost rises only during viable 24-kHz uplink periods; engineering cost is dominated by firmware clocking, modem contention, and end-to-end audio testing.
args.security_concerns: Audio remains on the existing encrypted pendant-to-relay channel. Quality telemetry should contain only packet sequence, RTT, queue depth, and loss statistics—not decoded audio. No confirmation is needed for an audio-quality adaptation.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—make sure I’m not leaving anything exposed, and tell me if you couldn’t.”
args.why_useful: A spoken or button-triggered departure check would coordinate the pendant’s physical presence, the Mac’s actual lock/power/network state, the browser’s authenticated tabs, and the relay’s independent record. It could lock the Mac, stop sensitive screen sharing, identify authenticated tabs or unsaved work that cannot safely be closed, and leave an exact exception list. This is not a generic reminder or a Mac-only command: it gives the owner a trustworthy privacy handoff when they physically walk away and can still report failure if the Mac is asleep, disconnected, or unreachable.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic local checks and typed actions for lock, sharing, power, and tab state; use a cheap background model only to rank exceptions and explain them. Realtime is needed only for the brief spoken result.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the button or phrase immediately; complete local checks in 2–5 seconds and browser/session inspection in up to 10 seconds. If a device is unreachable, report that explicitly rather than waiting indefinitely; relay can finish and notify when it reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 because most checks are deterministic; occasional semantic exception grouping may cost $0.01–$0.04. Latency is dominated by browser tab/session access and Mac wake/connect behavior.
args.security_concerns: The check necessarily touches authenticated-tab metadata and potentially sensitive window titles, so keep evidence owner-scoped, retain only hashes and minimal exception text, and redact page contents by default. Locking and stopping sharing are reversible; closing tabs, discarding edits, or signing out must never happen implicitly. The owner should choose a policy preset, but the system must report every skipped action and why.
missing: A pendant departure trigger (button gesture, explicit voice intent, or proximity transition) routed to a multi-surface job.
Typed Mac privacy-state observers/actions for lock state, active screen sharing/remote-control sessions, unsaved documents, and wake/connect status.
Browser APIs that enumerate authenticated tabs and detect unsaved or sensitive state without reading full page contents.
A relay-held privacy-check job with a short-lived, encrypted evidence record and reconnect completion semantics.
A policy engine for owner-selected safe actions versus report-only exceptions, plus a concise pendant result protocol and dashboard audit view.

transcript.text:
Round 61 findings:

- The newly granted Mac diagnostic interfaces are still schema-only. Calls to `mac_read_diagnostics`, `mac_readonly_diagnostics`, `mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl`, and `safe_mac_command` all return **“implementation not yet.”**
- Therefore I still cannot verify live process state, permissions, agent health, network, battery, or command execution behavior from this node.
- I proposed an observability-only shell transcript layer—no approval gates or capability restrictions—including command fingerprints, cwd, bounded output, exit classification, artifact hashes, redaction, and cross-surface receipt IDs.
- I also proposed a cross-node failure assistant: when a Mac/browser task fails, the pendant can explain what happened and provide an evidence-backed next step without silently retrying.

What I still need:

1. A working implementation of at least one read-only Mac diagnostic tool.
2. The local-agent observability contract for correlating shell jobs with relay, pendant, and browser tasks.
3. A bounded way to retrieve failure evidence and postcondition state without executing a retry automatically.

I do **not** need another permission or a narrower shell policy; the owner’s maximum-access policy is clear.

This would prevent actions at disruptive or stale moments—for example, preparing a form only when its authenticated tab is present and the owner is not presenting—while allowing the relay to keep watching after the Mac temporarily disconnects.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to compile the request into typed predicates and a step plan. Use realtime only for the initial spoken request and completion alert; use the stronger model only when a predicate is ambiguous or the page changed materially.
args.latency_budget: Predicate evaluation every 15–60 seconds, with event-driven wakeups from browser heartbeat and Mac state changes. After all conditions hold, begin within 2 seconds and provide a completion or refusal notice within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per armed task; most cost is one-time plan compilation and occasional semantic page re-checks. State monitoring should be local/event-driven rather than model-polled.
args.security_concerns: The system observes meeting state, network identity, active windows, and authenticated page metadata. Keep raw state on the Mac/browser, expose only predicate results to the relay, encrypt the durable plan, expire it automatically, and never treat a changed page or untrusted network as satisfying the original predicate. The action plan must remain reversible and produce a receipt.
missing: A durable conditional-trigger engine distinct from clock-based routines
Typed Mac predicates for idle/lock/presentation/audio/network state
Browser predicates based on authenticated tab identity and semantic page fingerprint
Relay-side lease, reconnect, deduplication, and expiry handling
Pendant notification and dashboard controls to pause, inspect, or cancel an armed task

transcript.text:
I continued discovery and found:

- The Mac agent is reachable and running v0.5.0 with `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` enabled.
- The relay and Mac bridge are reachable.
- Browser extension is offline with **5 pending commands**.
- Accessibility is not trusted.
- Screen Recording permission is missing.
- Computer-use loop is disabled, although a vision model is configured.
- The new `mac_read_diagnostics` capability is present in the schema but still returns **“no implementation yet.”**

I proposed two additions:

1. **Cross-surface self-healing execution**  
   Before dispatch, check the exact route’s health and permissions; select a viable fallback, retry transient failures as durable jobs, and explain whether work completed, is waiting, or needs repair.

2. **Typed capability-preflight and recovery coordinator**  
   Connect `/ops/status`, `/browser/status`, `/routing`, `/journal`, job receipts, and browser command state. It should reconcile stale browser commands by idempotency key, avoid duplicate clicks after reconnect, and attach retries/fallbacks to existing receipts—without adding approval gates.

What I still need:

- An implemented read-only Mac diagnostics provider. The granted interface exists, but cannot currently return host facts.
- A shared typed health/precondition schema across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant.
- Browser queue metadata exposing command age, idempotency keys, and terminal/stale reason codes.
- A durable retry/dead-letter worker connected to the existing job receipts and journal.

I did not request another permission or tool this round because the diagnostics implementation request is already pending and should not be re-asked.

args.user_asks: “When you say you did it, prove it—and if you can’t verify the result, tell me that instead of guessing.”
args.why_useful: Today Mac, browser, relay, and pendant actions can each produce local receipts, but the owner cannot reliably distinguish “command accepted” from “the world now matches what I asked.” This capability would define a completion test for each request, collect independent postconditions where possible, and speak a short evidence-backed result. For example, after changing a setting it would re-read the setting; after editing a browser form it would verify the DOM value and session state; after a cross-surface handoff it would verify the downstream receipt. It is a new trust guarantee, not merely another log or undo button.
args.model_tier: Deterministic postcondition checks and receipt correlation do the core work; a cheaper background model normalizes evidence into a concise explanation; realtime only handles the immediate spoken response.
args.latency_budget: Add 100–500 ms for local verification on short actions. For browser or multi-step work, verification runs asynchronously and the pendant says it is checking, then delivers a durable result.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for typed postconditions and existing receipts; typically under 1k background tokens when evidence must be summarized. The dominant cost is any extra Mac/browser read, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Evidence may contain private URLs, window titles, form values, or file paths. Keep raw evidence on the Mac/browser bridge, transmit only redacted claims and hashes to relay, and expose the source surface and timestamp in the dashboard. Never treat an executor acknowledgement as proof of a real-world mutation.
missing: A common completion-contract format with preconditions, postconditions, evidence source, freshness, and confidence.
Typed verification probes for Mac actions and browser actions, including safe readback after mutations.
A receipt state that distinguishes accepted, executed, verified, contradicted, and unverifiable, with contradiction recovery rather than silent success.
Pendant/dashboard rendering for a concise claim plus “why I believe this” evidence trail.

args.user_asks: “If my Mac is asleep or disconnected, remember exactly what I asked from the pendant and finish it when the Mac comes back—without making me repeat myself.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only surface continuously with the owner, while the Mac and browser are intermittent. Today a spoken request can end at a transient bridge or browser failure, and the owner has no durable, user-visible intent envelope preserving the exact request, constraints, and intended verification. This capability would capture the request locally/at the relay, acknowledge it immediately, bind it to the returning Mac/browser session, and resume only when the required surface is available. It preserves uncertainty and asks a focused follow-up if the request becomes stale instead of improvising.
args.model_tier: Realtime extracts a compact intent envelope during the voice turn; deterministic relay storage, wake/reconnect matching, and execution handle the rest; a cheaper background model resolves stale or ambiguous intents. No realtime model is needed while waiting.
args.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms when offline; reconnect matching under 2 s; execution time is asynchronous and reported through the pendant/dashboard.

transcript.text:
Discovered and verified a live defect:

- `/ops/status` reports the browser extension online with **5 pending commands**.
- Recent browser jobs nevertheless waited about **45 seconds** and failed with “browser extension is offline.”
- This means “online” does not currently prove that polling is active, and stale commands can accumulate.

I proposed a fix: reconcile heartbeat age, poll activity, leases, and pending-command count; fail fast when the bridge is stale; requeue expired commands using idempotency keys; and expose a deduplicated outage/recovery event to the pendant and relay.

I also proposed a Mac shell improvement: a bounded, redacted shell flight recorder with exit/timeout classification, durable transcript pointers, and failure-aware continuation—without adding gates or restricting `FULL_CONTROL_MODE`.

What I still need:

1. **Implementation of the granted diagnostic tools.** The schemas exist, but `mac_read_diagnostics` and `mac_readonly_diagnostics` currently return “no implementation yet,” so I cannot verify host state through the intended narrow interface.
2. **A durable resumable job lifecycle** for retry lineage and continuation. Receipts exist, but they do not yet provide full shell transcript artifacts or safe failure classification.
3. **Heartbeat/poll lease telemetry** from the browser bridge to distinguish genuinely live polling from stale `online` state.

No additional permission is needed this round.

args.why_useful: Today the owner can be told that the browser is online even while commands are timing out and five requests are pending. They cannot obtain a trustworthy, active end-to-end readiness answer before delegating work. This capability prevents wasted 45-second waits, makes failures intelligible, and lets the pendant distinguish a live Mac, a live browser poller, and merely cached status.
args.model_tier: Deterministic health probes and signed challenge correlation do the normal work; use the background model only to turn the typed result into a concise explanation or choose an alternate route. Realtime is needed only when the owner asks verbally.
args.latency_budget: Active Mac challenge plus browser poll acknowledgment should complete in 2–5 seconds; if the browser does not answer within the lease window, return a definitive stale/unreachable result rather than waiting 45 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model/API cost for the probe. Dominant cost is engineering and a small amount of durable heartbeat/lease metadata; no browser-minute budget should be spent merely checking readiness.
args.security_concerns: Challenge tokens must be single-use, short-lived, and bound to the paired Mac/browser session; never include page contents, cookies, URLs, or command output. A stale result must be marked unknown, not healthy. The probe must be read-only and must not open tabs or alter the owner's session.
missing: A single end-to-end readiness protocol spanning relay, Mac agent, and browser extension
Active challenge/ack messages with monotonic timestamps and lease generations
Separate freshness fields for Mac process health, browser heartbeat, browser poll, and pending command age
A typed readiness result consumed by the planner before dispatch
Pendant/relay rendering for verified, degraded, and unknown states

Each event should record the selected surface, decision reason, freshness proof used, action/receipt ID, result, and whether the event was observed, inferred, or merely attempted. Add a compact owner-facing 'why/where/what happened' projection that can be spoken without replaying the full prompt context, plus an exportable JSON evidence bundle for disputes or debugging.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should be able to ask, “What exactly did you do, where did it happen, and why did you believe it worked?” Today local receipts and job records exist, but they do not establish one trustworthy story across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser—especially when a stale browser status conflicts with a failed command. args.risk: The ledger could expose private URLs, commands, or page evidence; default spoken output must be summarized and redacted, with detailed export kept local or explicitly requested. Clock ordering must use sequence numbers and monotonic timestamps rather than wall-clock time alone. Event loss must be represented as unknown, never silently filled by inference.
args.cost_impact: Small durable-storage and hashing cost; negligible model cost because the owner projection is deterministic for normal events. A background model is optional only for explaining unusual partial failures.
args.latency_impact: No blocking cost on successful execution if events are buffered locally; the owner-facing summary becomes available within a few seconds. Durable flush may add minimal local I/O.
args.security_impact: Improves accountability without adding execution restrictions. Bind event ingestion to the existing paired relay/Mac identity, sign event batches, encrypt detailed evidence at rest, and redact secrets before relay transmission.

args.user_asks: “Keep working on this across my Mac and logged-in browser even if I walk away or one device disconnects; resume from the last safe checkpoint and tell me exactly what finished, what failed, and what I should do next.”
args.why_useful: Today a pendant request can span relay, Mac shell, and private browser tabs, but a disconnect or partial failure leaves the owner reconstructing state. A durable cross-surface run would checkpoint each completed step with evidence, retry only idempotent work, reattach to the right browser session, and deliver a concise spoken completion/failure report when the pendant reconnects. This is more than a Mac job runner: it coordinates the wearable's conversational intent, the always-awake relay, the Mac's unrestricted execution, and browser-only authenticated reach.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the goal and speak the final status. Run planning, checkpoint reconciliation, extraction, and retry classification on a cheaper background model; use the expensive tier only when evidence conflicts or the recovery plan is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds, then execute asynchronously. Reconnect status should be available within 1–2 seconds; ordinary step retries should add under 5 seconds, with no need to keep the voice session open.
args.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per short run on a background model; dominant costs are authenticated browser calls and any generated audio, not Mac command execution. Realtime usage is limited to the initial and final utterances.
args.security_concerns: Private page text and Mac command output may leave the device through the relay; retain only bounded evidence snippets and hashes, redact secrets, and bind checkpoints to the owner/session. Never silently repeat non-idempotent browser submissions or destructive shell commands; mark them manual-stop even though the owner's current policy intentionally permits unrestricted execution.

Idempotency and retry classification for shell and browser steps, with explicit non-repeatable/manual-stop states
Reconnect delivery that summarizes evidence rather than replaying the whole transcript
A coordinator that can reattach an authenticated browser session after extension heartbeat recovery

Expose it through /journal and /journal/:jobId with filters for command fingerprint, exit class, and run id, and let the planner request a retry using the receipt rather than re-planning from scratch.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When an unattended command fails or partially succeeds, the owner should hear “the build timed out after spawning X; no files changed” rather than a vague failure or an unsafe blind retry. It also makes the Mac tier faster: repeated status checks can reuse recent receipts, and the planner can distinguish a transient network failure from a permanent command error. This improves trust and recovery while preserving the owner's deliberate maximum-access policy.
args.effort: Medium: instrument computerControl.runShell/executor and jobTracker, add bounded redaction and child/resource sampling, extend journal serialization and planner input, then test timeout, signal, huge output, and nonzero-exit cases.
args.risk: Output could contain credentials or sensitive file contents; redact common token patterns, cap bytes, and store hashes instead of full output. Process sampling adds small overhead. If ledger persistence fails, execution must still proceed and return a minimal in-memory receipt. Never let observability become a blocking authorization gate.
args.cost_impact: No model API cost; modest local disk growth from bounded receipts (target <16 KB per shell action) and negligible CPU for timestamps/process sampling.
args.latency_impact: About 10–50 ms per action plus any optional child-process sampling; zero extra network round trips for the normal path.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a sensitive local record. Encrypt or permission-protect the ledger, redact secrets before persistence, and keep raw stdout ephemeral. No change to unrestricted command/network authority.

args.user_asks: “Pause what I’m doing here and give me this exact work state back later, wherever I am.” The pendant should snapshot my active Mac window, browser tabs and selections, unsaved text, relevant terminal state, and the spoken reason; later I can say “resume the paused thread” and have the Mac and authenticated browser restore the right state before the pendant reminds me where I left off.
args.why_useful: This is not a scheduled briefing or a background job: it preserves the owner's partially completed, human-in-the-loop work when they have to leave suddenly. Today the system can observe apps and run individual actions, but it cannot create a coherent, resumable cognitive checkpoint across a GUI, terminal, private browser session, and the pendant's conversation. The owner would stop losing half-finished investigations and drafts.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to capture the pause/resume utterance and speak the short orientation. Use a cheaper background model to normalize window/tab metadata, summarize visible text and unsaved drafts, and rank which checkpoint is the requested thread. Use the vision model only for GUI state that accessibility metadata cannot represent.
args.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 2 seconds; checkpoint creation in under 10 seconds for a typical 5–10 window session. Resume should restore the selected Mac/browser state within 5 seconds and speak a 15-second orientation, with deeper summarization deferred.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02 per checkpoint, dominated by one or two screenshots/vision calls and summarization; metadata capture and local state hashing are effectively free. No audio generation is needed beyond the short spoken orientation.
args.security_concerns: The checkpoint may contain private browser URLs, authenticated page snippets, draft text, and terminal paths. Store encrypted, redact tokens/password fields, keep screenshots opt-in and short-lived, bind records to the owner's device identity, and provide deletion. Never submit a draft or alter a page while restoring; restore focus and scroll/selection only, and clearly say when exact restoration was impossible.

args.why_useful: The current system can generate briefings and execute tasks, but it does not arbitrate attention in real time across local Mac notifications, browser events, relay jobs, and the owner's pendant state. The owner would get fewer disruptive alerts without missing a time-sensitive private-site change, failed long-running job, or direct human message. This requires the wearable's immediate presence, the Mac's foreground/app signals, the browser's authenticated reach, and the relay's always-on queue—not any one node alone.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic local rules for mode, quiet hours, deadlines, and known contacts; use a cheap background model to classify ambiguous events and deduplicate the deferred queue. Reserve realtime for the actual interruption and the owner's mode-change conversation.
args.latency_budget: Event classification under 500 ms for local/browser events; urgent pendant notification under 2 seconds. Deferred digest can be generated asynchronously in under a minute when requested.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-matched events; roughly <$0.005 for an ambiguous batch classification. The main cost is not tokens but durable event retention and browser polling.
args.security_concerns: Notification titles and private-page snippets are sensitive. Classify locally where possible, send only minimal redacted event capsules to the relay, encrypt the queue, and let the owner define VIPs, deadline thresholds, and sites that may never be spoken aloud. Never infer urgency from message content without recording the source and confidence.

Mac notification observation and controlled notification-mode integration

Both require new coordination primitives, not just wiring existing routes together: durable encrypted state, shared event/checkpoint schemas, browser and Mac state capture/restore, and pendant-local mode/queue support.

args.why_useful_to_owner: When a trusted unattended command fails, the owner can currently see that it failed but not whether cwd, PATH, timeout, signal, or stderr caused it; finding the project already took five attempts. args.security_concerns: The utterance may contain passwords, health data, or private work content. Encrypt the relay envelope, retain it only until delivery or explicit save, and never log raw text in general activity logs. Require an unmistakable preview/confirmation for sensitive-looking values or destinations such as payment, password, or message-send fields; insertion itself must never submit or send. Include app, tab URL, field label, and text hash in the local receipt, not the full secret.

args.change: Add a cross-surface focus lease for hands-free dictation. When the pendant starts a “put this there” utterance, the Mac agent and browser extension publish a signed snapshot containing active app/window, browser tab identity, focused-field locator, and a short expiry. The relay binds exactly one encrypted utterance envelope to that lease. Before insertion, the Mac agent verifies the same app/tab/field is still focused; if not, it pauses and asks the pendant rather than typing into a new destination. args.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents the uniquely dangerous failure of hands-free input landing in the wrong window after the owner switches focus. args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; small D1/local metadata records and one short-lived encrypted text payload per use. No hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms for lease validation; avoids delayed incorrect insertion and expensive recovery.
args.security_impact: Improves confidentiality by making text single-use, destination-bound, expiring, and hash-audited. It introduces a sensitive transient payload, which should be encrypted at rest and deleted after acknowledgment or expiry.

args.model_tier: background for periodic health classification and retry decisions; deterministic rules for heartbeat, idempotency, backoff, and receipt aggregation; realtime only to announce an urgent outage or answer a status question
args.latency_budget: Health checks every 1–5 minutes; outage detection under one interval, pendant alert under 2 seconds once detected; recovery report within 10 seconds of bridge heartbeat. No planner call for ordinary healthy checks.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero when healthy (HTTP checks and D1 state). Occasional gpt-4.1-mini call, roughly 2–4k input tokens, only to compress several failures into a spoken report; dominant cost is the rare recovery summary, not monitoring.
args.security_concerns: Health metadata, job labels, and failure text leave the Mac for relay state; command payloads and page contents must not. I recorded these findings and proposed:

1. **Cross-surface bridge watchdog** — relay monitors Mac/browser health, alerts the pendant, retries only safe idempotent work, and produces a recovery report.
2. **Durable action-execution envelopes** — every shell, planner, and browser action gets correlated timestamps, routing/model attribution, failure class, idempotency key, undoability, and redacted output metadata.

- The granted diagnostic and typed-action tools are still schema-only; they return “no implementation yet.”

args.user_asks: “When I’m away from my Mac, let me tap the pendant to queue a task with a short voice note; when I get back, have the relay and Mac resume it from the right project and tell me exactly what completed, without making me repeat myself.”
args.why_useful: Today a dropped Mac/browser connection turns an in-progress request into a conversational dead end: the owner must remember what they asked, repeat it, and reconstruct context. A wearable tap plus relay persistence can capture intent at the moment it matters, while the Mac later supplies files, apps, and authenticated sessions. This is a true handoff between the body, always-on service, and private machine rather than a Mac-only task runner.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief voice note and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic relay storage, deduplication, and delivery; background gpt-4.1-mini to normalize the note and select the active project when the Mac reconnects; planner tier only if the resumed task is genuinely ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgement under 500 ms using a local canned response; relay persistence under 1 second; resume within 15 seconds of Mac reconnection; completion spoken or queued for playback within 5 seconds after the Mac returns a receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Tiny for short notes: roughly 300–800 input tokens to normalize only when needed, plus a few hundred tokens for a completion summary. Most handoffs use deterministic storage and existing Mac execution, so the dominant cost is ambiguity escalation.
args.security_concerns: Voice notes and task metadata are stored in relay D1 and may contain private intent; encrypt or minimize them and expire unclaimed handoffs. Never transmit authenticated page contents, arbitrary shell output, or secrets to the relay. Bind delivery to the paired pendant and Mac identity, preserve project/session provenance, and require the existing owner policy before any destructive or external side effect.
missing: A pendant-side offline capture and acknowledgement mode that survives a dropped relay link
A durable relay handoff record containing audio/text note, capture time, pairing identity, intended surface, project hint, and lifecycle state
A reconnect protocol that lets the Mac claim handoffs exactly once and report progress/receipt updates
A context reattachment operation that resolves the handoff to the Mac's active project, session, and relevant recent thread without resending the entire conversation
A pendant playback queue for completion receipts when the owner is no longer in a live voice session

args.change: Add a small encrypted nonvolatile event spool dedicated to handoff intents—an I2C/QSPI FRAM or protected flash ring buffer with monotonic sequence numbers, plus a firmware button gesture that commits a short voice-note reference and acknowledgement state before attempting the relay upload. The spool should retain at least 64 compact events and support atomic append/acknowledge, replay after reboot, and secure erase after receipt confirmation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A tap made while the owner is walking, underground, or between Wi‑Fi and cellular coverage would not vanish. The pendant could honestly say “saved; I’ll finish this when your Mac is back,” then deliver the request later without requiring the owner to remember it.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision and firmware work: select FRAM/protected flash, add the bus and secure-storage key handling, implement a power-loss-safe ring format, and integrate replay with relay pairing. Prototype first using existing flash to validate the protocol before spinning the board.
args.risk: A damaged or worn storage cell could lose queued intents; use sequence/CRC, wear leveling, and duplicate relay acknowledgement. Voice data is sensitive, so store encrypted compressed audio or preferably a short transcript plus bounded audio fallback, and erase after receipt. A full spool must produce a local overflow indication rather than silently dropping the oldest request.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 per device for a small FRAM/protected-flash part and minor PCB assembly impact; negligible idle power, brief write current during a tap. No recurring model cost for the storage itself.
args.latency_impact: Local commit acknowledgement under tens of milliseconds; replay is asynchronous and does not delay normal conversation.
args.security_impact: Adds a durable local copy of private intent, so keys must be device-bound and inaccessible over unauthenticated UART. Secure erase and pairing-scoped replay are required; never treat the spool as a general filesystem.
depends_on: Define the relay handoff record and exactly-once acknowledgement protocol
Implement pendant firmware event capture and reconnect replay
Add paired-device key provisioning and receipt-driven deletion
Provide a relay-to-pendant completion playback queue

Add failure-aware recovery metadata: safe-to-retry, retry count, and suggested next diagnostic, but do not gate or auto-retry destructive commands. Keep full-control execution unchanged.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When a command fails or a long task finishes while the owner is away, the agent can explain exactly what happened, distinguish a transient network/timeout from a real command error, and continue from the failed step without asking the owner to reproduce it. It also makes unrestricted shell capability accountable without taking capability away.
args.effort: Medium: executor instrumentation and a small trace store/API, redaction and bounded-output tests, plus relay/dashboard rendering. No change to command authorization or execution semantics.
args.risk: Output may contain secrets or personal data; redact known token/password/key patterns and environment names, cap raw tails, hash rather than retain large output, and apply retention/deletion with the existing job records. Incorrect failure classification could lead a later planner to recommend an unsafe retry, so the metadata is advisory only. If trace persistence fails, execution result must still return and the existing receipt remains authoritative.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and CPU per action; avoids repeated expensive model turns and duplicate commands. No additional model call required; classification is deterministic.
args.latency_impact: Under ~5 ms instrumentation overhead for normal commands; no added model round trip. Large stdout is truncated/hash-only.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability of the intentionally unrestricted shell, but creates a second sensitive artifact. Encrypt at rest where available, redact before persistence, restrict trace routes to the existing authenticated Mac-agent context, and provide per-job purge/retention.

args.change: Add a first-class persistent terminal-session backend for long-running shell work. A run_shell action may opt into a named session with a process-group ID and bounded ring buffer; expose authenticated attach/read (offset or last N lines), stdin write, SIGINT/TERM, and explicit close endpoints, with heartbeats and orphan cleanup after lease expiry. Keep ordinary one-shot commands unchanged. Link session events to the existing job/action receipt and relay job status so a pendant query can say whether the process is still running, show recent output, or offer stop/resume rather than launching a duplicate command.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Builds, exports, downloads, tests, and other work that outlasts a voice turn keep running when the owner walks away or the network drops. The owner can ask from the pendant what is happening, see the last useful lines, stop a stuck process, and reconnect later without losing the Mac's terminal context or accidentally starting the work twice.
args.effort: Medium-high: local process supervisor/PTY or pipes, authenticated streaming endpoints, lease/orphan handling, bounded persistence, and relay_job_status integration. Add tests for reconnect, cancellation, crash recovery, and duplicate-session prevention.
args.risk: A detached process can continue consuming CPU, hold files, or expose output; enforce resource/time limits, redact persisted output, kill the process group on lease expiry by default, and make persistence opt-in per session. PTY behavior differs from noninteractive commands, so retain the current executor as fallback. Never replay stdin automatically after reconnect.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/RAM overhead while active and bounded disk for the ring buffer; no extra model calls. It can reduce API/model cost by avoiding repeated polling and re-running failed long jobs.
args.latency_impact: Immediate status reads over the existing Mac-agent connection; streaming can be SSE/WebSocket. Session startup adds only PTY/process setup time, while one-shot commands are unchanged.
args.security_impact: Adds a privileged control surface for stdin/signals. Require the existing bearer auth, per-session unguessable IDs, owner/job binding, strict output retention, and audit every attach/write/signal/close event. Do not expose raw terminal sessions to unauthenticated relay clients.

This would make the Mac a privacy boundary: the owner gets a concise answer and evidence without exporting the underlying data to the relay or model.
args.model_tier: Use a small local deterministic redaction/classification pass first; use a local Mac model for summarization when available, and only send a typed, lossy finding or approved snippets to the slower background model/relay. args.latency_budget: 2–10 seconds for ordinary logs, with immediate progress on the pendant; large folders may run as a background job and notify when the local digest is ready.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero relay/model cost when local summarization succeeds; otherwise a small request containing only the redacted digest. Dominant cost is local CPU and optional local-model memory, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: The local pass must detect and suppress credentials, tokens, private keys, health/financial identifiers, and configured path classes before any network call. Keep raw input and intermediate parses on disk only under short retention, show the owner exactly what categories and snippets would leave the Mac, and make network export opt-in per request. A failed classifier must fail closed for export, while still allowing a fully local answer.
missing: A local privacy-boundary pipeline that can parse files/logs and produce typed findings without sending raw content
A local summarizer or constrained on-device model on the Mac
Redaction scanners for secrets and owner-configured sensitive paths
