args.change: Create a Mac-local privacy boundary between terminal execution and model/relay context. Every file/log read is first converted into a typed local finding (category, severity, line/span hash, local citation, confidence, and redaction reason); raw bytes never enter the normal job result or fleet context. Add an explicit export manifest containing only the finding fields/snippets approved by a local policy, and make /plan, /execute, job receipts, and relay status consume that manifest rather than arbitrary stdout. Keep a local-only answer path for requests whose manifest is empty.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for analysis of genuinely private Mac material and receive a useful answer without trusting that raw terminal output will be forwarded. They get citations back to local files and a clear statement of what stayed on the Mac, instead of having to choose between no help and data export.
args.effort: High: local parser/redactor and secret detectors, typed result schemas, context-routing changes, local citation storage, export preview, and tests against source code, credentials, and personal documents. Requires a local summarizer or a deterministic extractive fallback.
args.risk: False negatives could leak sensitive data; default to no export when classification is uncertain and let the owner explicitly inspect/override the manifest. False positives reduce usefulness but preserve privacy. Local citations must not expose contents in logs or receipts. Add deletion/retention controls for raw local intermediates.
args.cost_impact: Adds local CPU, disk, and possibly a one-time local-model download; normally reduces remote token and relay costs because only compact findings travel. No additional remote call for a local-only answer.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–3 seconds for scanning typical logs and potentially longer for folders; remote summarization starts only after the manifest is produced. Existing non-private actions can bypass this path.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces exfiltration risk by making raw stdout ineligible for context propagation, but introduces a sensitive local index. Encrypt or permission-lock the index, bind manifests to job IDs, and audit every export decision without storing the blocked content.

args.why_useful: Today the relay is reachable but the Mac reports ready=false (Accessibility and Screen Recording missing), the computer-use loop is disabled, and the browser extension is offline with five queued commands. A pendant request can therefore look accepted while silently having no executor. This capability turns outages and permission loss into an explicit, recoverable handoff: the relay records a goal and an execution lease, the Mac/browser advertise health, and the system either reroutes a safe read to another surface or resumes exactly once when the missing surface returns. surfaces: pendant: button starts/ends the request and plays a terse state update; LED distinguishes queued, executing, waiting-for-Mac, and failed
relay-realtime: persists the intent, leases steps, applies expiry and idempotency, and emits a spoken update without keeping the expensive realtime model busy

browser-extension: heartbeats and claims only commands for its bound tab/session; reconnect replays pending work without duplicating a completed step

args.model_tier: Use realtime only for the initial conversational acknowledgment and urgent spoken status. Use a cheaper background model for step decomposition, capability-health matching, fallback selection, and final reconciliation; deterministic code handles leases, idempotency, retries, and receipts.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge from the pendant in under 1 second. Health/routing decision in under 2 seconds when a node is online. A disconnected node may wait until its next heartbeat; surface a 30-second stale warning and an owner-configurable expiry rather than polling expensively.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.01 per request beyond the normal voice turn, dominated by one small background planning/reconciliation call; heartbeat, lease, retry, and receipt work is database/Worker compute. Avoid sending full page or Mac context on every status update.
args.security_concerns: Health metadata must not include page contents, credentials, or shell output. Bind browser work to an extension/session/tab identity and Mac work to the paired host. Persist only the goal, step hashes, surface, timestamps, and typed result summaries. Never retry a non-idempotent browser submission or shell mutation automatically; preserve the existing before/after receipt and checkpoint semantics. Tell the owner when a fallback changes what was actually done.

Expose it through the existing job receipt and /journal/:jobId, and let the planner ask for a retry with the same idempotency key or a corrected command. A crash between command completion and journal write could still create ambiguity, so mark attempts as unknown and require a fresh status probe rather than blindly retrying. Never infer success solely from a truncated output tail.

args.why_useful: A useful fact often exists only in a private Safari tab or a local Mac file, then disappears when the tab closes. This would create a small, provenance-preserving capsule rather than dumping an entire page into long-term memory: the browser supplies the authenticated URL/tab and selected text or DOM citation, the Mac supplies local-file provenance when relevant, the relay stores an encrypted, expiring snapshot plus a compact semantic index, and the pendant can retrieve it by voice. surfaces: pendant: voice command “remember this” and later spoken retrieval; button controls capture timing so no microphone is left open
browser-extension: captures only the user-selected text/region, URL, title, tab/session identity, and a DOM locator/source hash; does not scrape unrelated tabs
mac-planner/mac-terminal: captures a selected local artifact or command result with path, modification time, content hash, and a redacted excerpt when the source is on the Mac
relay: encrypts and stores the capsule with owner-defined TTL, sensitivity label, and source provenance; retrieves only matching capsules for a later question
dashboard/iOS: shows capsule list, source link, expiry, evidence excerpt, and delete/export controls
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short capture acknowledgment or spoken lookup. A cheaper background model generates a compact title, entities, and retrieval keywords; deterministic code preserves the exact excerpt/hash and enforces TTL. Use no model for a direct exact-quote lookup.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second; persist the capsule in under 3 seconds. Exact retrieval under 1 second; semantic retrieval under 3 seconds. Never block the owner on summarizing a large source—store first and summarize asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per capture for optional compacting, plus small D1/R2 storage; exact lookup costs no model call. The dominant cost is embedding/semantic indexing if enabled, so cap excerpt size and index only owner-selected content.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and local files are highly sensitive. 1. **Health-aware cross-surface execution** — keep a pendant request alive, report exactly which surface is unavailable, reroute safe work where possible, and resume idempotently when the Mac/browser returns.
2. **Provenance-preserving memory capsules** — let the owner explicitly save selected browser text or Mac artifacts with source, timestamp, citation, expiry, and later pendant retrieval.

args.user_asks: “Only show private Mac and logged-in-browser results when I’m actually wearing the pendant; if I take it off, pause the sensitive work and continue when I put it back on.”
args.why_useful: Today the Mac, browser, and relay can continue acting while the owner is away, but none of them has reliable proof that the intended person is physically present. This would let the owner walk away from a shared room without leaving private notifications, authenticated-page excerpts, or draft contents exposed, while preserving useful continuity: non-sensitive background work may finish, sensitive results remain sealed, and the pendant announces the exact point at which work resumes.
surfaces: pendant: periodic authenticated presence beacon, local wear/presence sensor, and a short button gesture to re-authorize; LED indicates present, paused-sensitive, or expired authorization

args.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for presence enforcement. Deterministic firmware/relay cryptography handles leases and state; a cheap background model classifies a job's output sensitivity at planning time, with owner-configurable overrides. Realtime is used only if the owner asks for a spoken explanation while present.
args.latency_budget: Presence loss recognized within 2–5 seconds, with no model round trip. Re-authorization and release of sealed results under 1 second after a valid button gesture. Background jobs continue without waiting for model responses.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per-event API cost; cryptographic lease checks and D1 writes dominate. Optional sensitivity classification costs roughly $0.001–$0.01 per job, cached for the job lifetime.
args.security_concerns: Presence must be cryptographically bound to the paired pendant, not inferred from an easily spoofed MAC-visible Bluetooth name. Do not transmit raw audio, page content, or credentials in the beacon. Use short-lived rotating tokens, replay protection, and a fail-closed policy for sensitive presentation. The owner must be able to revoke a lost pendant from the dashboard. Clearly distinguish ‘paused because absent’ from ‘failed’; never delete sealed results automatically without the configured retention policy.
missing: A real pendant presence/wear signal or secure proximity channel; the current single-button/LED prototype has no presence sensor
Firmware support for rotating signed presence leases and replay counters within the device's constrained RAM/flash budget
A relay-side encrypted sealed-result store and presence-epoch API
A Mac/browser presentation broker that classifies and withholds sensitive output without terminating resumable work
An owner-facing sensitivity policy and lost-pendant revocation flow

args.change: Add a low-power capacitive skin-contact/proximity sensor and a hardware-backed identity element to the pendant, while retaining the existing single button and LED. Firmware should derive a signed, rotating presence epoch from contact plus an authenticated nearby-host handshake; it should never expose a raw sensor stream. Put the sensor on an always-on low-power GPIO/I2C path and reserve the secure element for lease signing/revocation keys.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could leave a shared room without private Mac/browser results remaining audible or visible, then resume them immediately on return. It also gives the system a trustworthy way to tell the owner ‘you are present’ rather than guessing from an online Mac or an easily spoofed Bluetooth name.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision and firmware integration: choose a skin-contact electrode/sensor, add secure-element support, define signed epoch packets, validate false-positive/false-negative behavior across clothing and charging, and add a lost-device revocation path in the relay.
args.risk: A contact sensor can misclassify pockets, loose wear, or another person holding the pendant. Use conservative expiry and require the existing button for sensitive reauthorization when confidence is low. Secure-element provisioning and board changes add manufacturing complexity; retain a development bypass only in lab firmware, never production.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 per unit for a basic capacitive/proximity component plus $1–$3 for a secure element, with milliwatt-or-less idle draw if duty-cycled. No per-request API cost beyond lease state writes.
args.latency_impact: Presence transitions can be detected locally in roughly 1–3 seconds; no model latency. Signed lease verification is sub-millisecond on the Mac/relay.
args.security_impact: Meaningfully improves physical-presence assurance, but it is not biometric authentication. Never treat it as sufficient for irreversible financial or account actions; combine it with the existing action-specific controls. Protect private results by failing closed when the lease is stale or revoked.

Pendant firmware support for rotating signed epochs within the existing constrained RAM/flash budget
Relay and Mac/browser presentation layers that consume presence epochs

Its read-only journal covers 120 retained jobs, 147 actions, 14 failures, 76 writes, but reports 0 undoable and 112 routing requests unattributed to a tier. transcript.text:
Discovered the current state and found one gap beyond the existing shell-journal work.

### Live findings
- Mac agent v0.5.0 is online with `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` and planner enabled.
- Journal currently retains 120 jobs:
  - 147 actions
  - 14 failures
  - 76 writes
  - 0 currently marked undoable
- Routing telemetry has 112 unattributed requests.
- The Chrome extension is offline with 5 pending browser commands.
- mac-vision is disabled, vision upload consent is absent, and Accessibility permission is not trusted.

### New proposal recorded
I proposed a **cross-surface causality and cost trace**: one lineage ID should follow a request from pendant/relay → model routing → Mac job → shell subprocess → browser commands → receipts and spoken completion.

That would let the owner hear whether a delay or failure came from:
- model planning,
- Mac execution,
- a dropped browser connection,
- queued browser work, or
- an ambiguous retry.

It also addresses the current 112 unattributed routing records and reduces duplicate work caused by confusing “queued” with “failed.”

### What is still needed
1. A shared lineage envelope propagated through relay, planner, Mac jobs, and browser commands.
2. A non-blocking, bounded trace sink with redaction and short retention.
3. Browser reconnect reconciliation so the five pending commands are clearly distinguished from failed work.
4. An implemented diagnostic executor: the granted `mac_read_diagnostics` and typed-action tools are schemas only and currently do not execute. I did not rely on them.

No microphone was opened, and I did not execute any Mac mutation.

args.user_asks: “For that request I made earlier, show me the complete chain of what happened, what is still queued, what failed, which device did each step, and roughly how much model time it cost.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner gets separate Mac jobs, routing receipts, and browser queue state, but no single trustworthy, human-readable explanation joining them. This would make cross-device behavior understandable after delays, dropped connections, partial completion, or duplicate attempts—without requiring the owner to inspect technical logs.
args.model_tier: background for assembling and summarizing existing structured records; deterministic joins and totals first, with a small model only for concise spoken wording. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks during a live conversation.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a recent request from retained records; under 5 seconds if browser reconnect reconciliation is needed. The pendant can say 'I am checking the Mac and browser trace' while the background job assembles it.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost when records are structured; roughly 1–3k input tokens and a short completion only when summarization is needed. Dominant cost is not inference but retaining and joining bounded trace metadata.
args.security_concerns: The report may reveal private URLs, shell commands, file paths, account names, and model prompts. Store raw spans locally with short retention, redact secrets and sensitive arguments, expose opaque IDs and summaries by default, and require owner-authenticated access for detailed views. Never include bearer tokens or full private page contents in relay speech.
missing: A shared request-lineage ID propagated from relay routing into Mac jobs, shell actions, and browser commands
A bounded redacted trace store that survives the current 120-job eviction window through aggregate summaries
Browser reconnect reconciliation that records whether pending commands eventually completed, failed, or remain indeterminate
A join endpoint or dashboard view combining routing, journal, job receipts, and browser queue state

args.user_asks: “After anything gets interrupted, tell me what is definitely complete, what is only partly done, and what cannot be verified—and offer the next safest way to reconcile it without blindly repeating the action.”
args.why_useful: A dropped Mac connection, browser disconnect, timeout, or process crash currently leaves the owner to guess whether a command ran before the failure. This capability distinguishes completed, failed, and indeterminate effects, then proposes inspection or continuation rather than silently replaying potentially permanent work.
args.model_tier: Background/deterministic for effect-state calculation from receipts, exit codes, checkpoints, browser acknowledgements, and reconnect state; use the planner tier only to explain ambiguous cases or formulate a recovery plan. Realtime is only needed to read the short result aloud.
args.latency_budget: Initial interruption classification under 2 seconds from local records; reconciliation under 10 seconds when it needs a live Mac or browser check. The owner should get an immediate compact uncertainty report, followed by an update if a device reconnects.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic classification; roughly 1–3k model input tokens only for an ambiguous multi-step recovery explanation. Most cost is local state tracking, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Recovery inspection can expose private files, authenticated pages, and command arguments. Keep evidence local by default, redact secrets, require explicit owner choice before any compensating mutation, and make the spoken summary disclose uncertainty rather than claiming success.
missing: Per-step effect checkpoints with an explicit unknown/indeterminate state rather than only job success or failure
Command- and browser-operation effect probes that can verify postconditions without replaying the original action
A recovery-plan record that separates read-only reconciliation from compensating mutations and records the chosen outcome
Cross-device acknowledgement and reconnect handling so a late browser result or Mac receipt can close an uncertain step

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **Cross-device request trace** — the owner can ask what happened across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, including queued work, failures, device ownership, and model cost.

2. **Interruption reconciliation** — after a timeout or disconnect, the owner can learn what definitely completed, what is indeterminate, and what read-only checks or compensating actions are appropriate without blindly replaying mutations.

Both require missing connective infrastructure: propagated lineage IDs, explicit indeterminate step states, postcondition checks, reconnect acknowledgements, and recovery records.

Round 78 findings:

- `/ops/snapshot` confirms the Mac agent and relay are reachable.
- The browser extension is offline with **5 pending commands**.
- macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions are missing, so mac-vision cannot currently operate.
- The newly granted `mac_read_diagnostics` and `mac_readonly_diagnostics` tools still have no implementation; I recorded this blocker. Current host facts must come from authenticated HTTP snapshots or existing Mac actions.
- Current job telemetry shows **14 failed actions**, **0 undoable actions**, and **112 unattributed routing records**, indicating observability remains incomplete.

I proposed and recorded a new Mac-harness change: **reconnectable long-running shell process leases**. Explicitly marked long-running jobs would survive relay/request disconnects, retain bounded output with cursors, report status through `/jobs/:jobId` and `relay_job_status`, and support explicit process-group cancellation—without adding approval gates or automatic retries.

I also told `mac-planner` that its on-demand Calendar/Mail/authenticated-tab/workspace handoff packet is not exactly covered by the backlog.

The owner cannot reliably leave a build, export, backup, or research command running, return later through the pendant, inspect only the unseen output, and resume after a Mac or agent restart. This would make the pendant a dependable remote terminal companion rather than a one-shot command launcher.

args.security_concerns: A detached process can continue using CPU, files, credentials, or network after the owner leaves. Require explicit long-running intent, a maximum lifetime and disk quota, visible lease status, and pendant cancellation; do not auto-retry. Keep raw output on the Mac with TTL deletion and send only redacted tails/summaries to relay. Restrict status access to the paired owner.

args.security_concerns: Private authenticated content must never fall back to public web search or leave the Mac. Each task must declare public/private data class, permitted surfaces, and idempotency. Keep existing owner policy of no approval gates; instead attach receipts showing why a fallback or defer occurred and require explicit confirmation only where an existing action already requires it.

transcript.text:
I found one concrete defect: Mac job traces are carrying unrelated long-term facts, including a “bike lock code,” into planner context and potentially `/jobs`, `/thinking`, relay telemetry, or spoken output.

I proposed a **sensitivity firewall** that:

- Classifies stored facts and page/shell outputs by sensitivity.
- Excludes secrets from planner prompts and receipts by default.
- Uses scoped references when an executor genuinely needs private data.
- Redacts at serialization time across Mac, relay, dashboard, and pendant surfaces.
- Preserves provenance and a non-secret explanation for each redaction.
- Adds retention and cleanup hooks for already-stored traces.

I also proposed fail-fast, health-aware degraded routing, though it overlaps somewhat with the browser lease-reconciliation work already underway.

Round 96 findings:

  - Accessibility: **not trusted**

2. **Cross-surface request lineage**  
   One request ID would follow work through relay, model routing, Mac jobs, browser commands, and pendant audio, making failures, costs, and resumptions explainable without resending the entire context.

What I still need:

- The granted diagnostic tools still return **“schema but no implementation yet.”** HTTP observability is usable, but a real narrow Mac diagnostic implementation would remove that gap.

args.risk: A stale or incorrect lease could delay work or resume at the wrong time. Use short TTLs, monotonic attempt IDs, explicit blocker categories, and a manual “resume now” endpoint; expiry must park rather than discard jobs.

args.latency_impact: No impact on normal actions; failed jobs become parked immediately, and resume starts within one heartbeat interval (target 5–15 seconds).

transcript.text:
Round 97 findings:

- Mac agent is online with unrestricted full-control planning enabled.
- Agent readiness is **false**: Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions are missing.
- Browser bridge is offline with **9 pending commands**.
- Relay and Mac bridge are reachable.
- `/journal` reports 120 retained jobs, 146 actions, 18 failures, zero undoable actions, and 112 actions without model-tier attribution.
- `browser_navigate` has retried 8 times and failed all 8 times, including 45-second timeouts.

I recorded these findings and proposed:

1. A **cross-surface readiness lease/resume protocol** so jobs park on a verified blocker instead of repeatedly retrying an offline browser, then resume exactly once when the bridge returns.
2. A **causal execution ledger** linking Mac shell, browser, relay, retries, receipts, and failure details under one trace ID.

What is still needed to implement them:

- Machine-readable capability leases and reason codes from `/ops/status` and `/browser/status`.
- Parked/blocked job states with dependency and retry-lineage fields.
- Shared trace IDs through Mac, browser bridge, and relay completion events.
- A relay-to-pendant status event for concise blocker/resume announcements.
- Bounded, redacted execution metadata for shell commands and stderr.
- Retention/compaction so causal histories survive the current 120-job limit.

No further discovery permission is needed from me this round. The immediate operational fix for the owner is enabling Accessibility, Screen Recording, and the browser bridge; the architectural fix is preventing work from being attempted while those capabilities are unavailable.

args.user_asks: When I ask “what did you do for that?”, show me one trustworthy, chronological answer covering the pendant, relay, Mac shell, and browser: what was attempted, what actually changed, what failed, and the evidence—without rerunning anything.
args.why_useful: Today status is fragmented: relay job status, Mac jobs, browser receipts, and journal entries can disagree or omit tier attribution. The owner cannot obtain a single verifiable postmortem for a task, especially after a browser timeout or unrestricted shell command. A trace-backed answer would make the system accountable without adding approval gates or reducing capability.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic aggregation and a small background summarizer; use the realtime tier only to speak the already-computed concise answer.
args.latency_budget: Return the structured trace in under 1 second from local/relay stores; generate the spoken summary in under 2 seconds. Never wait for a new Mac or browser round trip.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for aggregation; typically under $0.01 for optional summarization. Storage and redaction are the dominant costs, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The trace may contain private URLs, shell commands, file paths, and snippets. Keep raw evidence on the paired Mac, expose redacted hashes and bounded excerpts by default, require explicit owner request for sensitive detail, and never rerun a command merely to gather evidence. Preserve the owner's deliberate full-control policy; this is observability, not a gate.
missing: A durable cross-surface trace ID propagated from the original pendant request through relay, Mac jobs, browser commands, and receipts.
An immutable event schema distinguishing planned, dispatched, started, completed, failed, retried, and actually-mutated effects.
A join/normalization service that correlates local job IDs, browser command IDs, receipt IDs, and relay IDs, including gaps and stale/offline periods.
A read-only owner-facing trace endpoint and dashboard/pendant renderer with evidence links, redaction, and retention/export controls.

args.user_asks: When I say “stop that” to the pendant, cancel every still-running part of that request across the relay, Mac, and browser, leave completed changes untouched, and tell me exactly what was stopped and what could not be stopped.
args.why_useful: The system exposes cancellation for individual Mac jobs, but the owner cannot reliably revoke one conversational request across multiple surfaces. Without a causal cancellation group, a queued browser command or relay continuation may still run after the owner has changed their mind. This gives the wearable a real emergency brake while preserving an honest boundary around already-completed effects.
args.model_tier: Deterministic cancellation propagation and state reconciliation; no expensive model call is needed except a short realtime spoken response when the owner says the phrase.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge locally in under 300 ms, propagate cancellation within 1 second, and reconcile receipts within 3 seconds. Do not wait for an unavailable Mac to acknowledge; report it as unconfirmed.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API/model cost; state fan-out and durable event writes dominate.
args.security_concerns: Cancellation must be scoped to the authenticated request trace, not a broad global kill switch. It must never pretend to undo completed shell, browser, or external mutations. Use signed cancellation tokens, monotonic sequence numbers, idempotent delivery, and an explicit distinction between cancelled, completed, and cancellation-unconfirmed.
missing: A request-level cancellation group and signed cancellation token created at pendant/relay ingress.
Cancellation propagation and acknowledgement handlers in the Mac executor and browser command queue, including removal or tombstoning of pending commands.
A reconciliation state machine that merges late completions with cancellation, preserving receipts and never reversing completed effects automatically.
A pendant phrase/gesture handler and dashboard timeline showing stopped, completed, and unconfirmed branches.

Keep credentials and sensitive page contents in the browser session, send the relay only redacted hashes and confirmation evidence. Require a new approval if any field or target changes. Ambiguous network outcomes must be treated as unknown and reconciled by reading the service's history/status page before any retry.

A remote-service idempotency/reconciliation strategy that distinguishes timeout-after-commit from never-submitted

Each invariant stores a typed desired state, evidence predicate, check cadence, expiry, quiet hours, last independently verified value, and a recovery recipe. args.user_asks: When I ask the pendant to do something on my Mac or in my browser, make sure the intended real-world result happened—not merely that a command returned—and tell me the evidence or the exact point where verification failed.
args.why_useful: Today a UI action can report success while macOS ignores it, and browser commands can fail repeatedly while remaining queued. The owner needs outcome-level certainty: for example, confirmation that a reminder exists, a document was actually saved, or a browser form produced the expected post-submit state. This is more useful than a transport receipt and prevents silent no-ops.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic semantic verifiers and cheap background reasoning for expected-state extraction and evidence comparison; reserve realtime for the owner's spoken request and concise result. Use the Mac planner only for ambiguous recovery, not every verification.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge intent immediately; verify simple outcomes within 1–3 seconds and multi-step outcomes within 10 seconds. If verification cannot complete, report `unverified` rather than claiming success and continue asynchronously when appropriate.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no additional model call: local app/API readback and browser DOM/session inspection dominate. Cheap-model use for ambiguous expected-state matching should remain below $0.01 per invocation; realtime is not used for background verification.
args.security_concerns: Verification must inspect only the target app/session and redact secrets from evidence. Never treat a matching screenshot alone as proof for destructive or externally visible actions; require a semantic readback such as an object ID, saved-file stat, sent-message record, or post-submit confirmation. Keep evidence hashes and short summaries rather than raw page content. Retries must be idempotency- and precondition-aware to avoid duplicate sends or purchases.

A deterministic failure taxonomy and retryability table
A receipt-aware executor retry path that skips completed stable action IDs
Dashboard and relay projections for redacted failure summaries

args.change: Add an execution-aware router that recognizes high-frequency Mac/browser intents and failure-recovery requests from typed action plans and recent receipts, then chooses deterministic or background handling before constructing the planner prompt. Cache compact intent signatures and successful recovery recipes keyed by action type plus normalized error, not by sensitive URLs or raw commands; escalate only when confidence is low or the plan spans surfaces.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Routine status checks and repeated recovery attempts would answer faster and stop spending the expensive planner tier on work the system already understands. The live router already saves 44% of requests, but still spends about 47k planner prompt tokens across nine requests; this makes those savings persist for the common failures the owner actually encounters.
args.effort: Medium: define intent/error signatures, add a bounded local cache with expiry, connect routing receipts to executor outcomes, and test that cached recipes never cross user/session boundaries.
args.risk: A stale recipe could produce an irrelevant retry, especially after browser tabs change. Recovery: short TTLs, require matching action schema and surface/session, verify current browser status and receipt preconditions, and fall back to the planner on mismatch. Unknown commands remain unchanged.
args.cost_impact: Potentially substantial reduction in planner tokens and latency for repeated intents; cache metadata is tiny and deterministic lookup is effectively free. No additional model cost except occasional recipe synthesis.
args.latency_impact: Milliseconds for cache lookup; removes 1–3 seconds of planner latency for recognized requests. Recovery itself still pays bridge or shell execution time.
args.security_impact: Never cache raw authenticated page contents, shell output, or secrets. Use salted hashes and normalized action/error labels; keep the detailed evidence in local receipts.
depends_on: Cross-surface correlation IDs and failure taxonomy
GET /routing receipts linked to GET /jobs and GET /journal
A local, TTL-bounded recipe cache with session isolation

args.user_asks: “Pause this exactly where it is, remember what I was looking at and what remains, and resume it when I’m back at my Mac—without losing the browser context.”
args.why_useful: The owner can start a task by voice or in Safari, then walk away, but cannot currently preserve a coherent, resumable checkpoint across the pendant, relay, Mac job, and authenticated browser. Today a job receipt records actions after the fact; it does not capture the live task state, open-tab evidence, pending decisions, or the exact next safe step. This would make interruption normal rather than forcing the owner to reconstruct context.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic checkpoint capture and a small background model to compress the task state; use the realtime model only for the short pendant acknowledgement and a planner-tier call when resuming requires reconciling changed tabs or a new goal.
args.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement and local checkpoint in under 2 seconds; resume inspection in under 10 seconds, with longer work continuing durably and a concise pendant notification when ready.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per pause/resume: local browser snapshots, receipts, and structured state need no model; background summarization is the dominant routine cost. Planner escalation is reserved for changed or ambiguous authenticated pages.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoints may contain authenticated URLs, page text, drafts, shell paths, and voice-derived private context. Store raw snapshots only on the Mac, encrypt or expire them, send the relay only a redacted task summary, and never resume a submit/send/delete step automatically. On resume, show changed evidence and require the owner's existing confirmation convention before irreversible actions.
missing: A first-class resumable checkpoint schema containing goal, completed stable action IDs, next step, open browser tab/session IDs, evidence capsule references, pending decisions, and expiry
An atomic pause endpoint that snapshots Mac job state and authenticated browser state without executing a new command
Browser tab/session reattachment and stale-state detection on resume
A relay notification and dashboard review surface for paused, expired, and resumed checkpoints
A resume planner that compares checkpoint evidence with current tabs and produces a diff before continuing

args.user_asks: “If something truly urgent happens, reach me on the pendant; otherwise wait until I’m free and put it on the Mac. Escalate only if I haven’t acknowledged it.”
args.why_useful: The system can produce jobs, browser findings, and briefings, but cannot yet decide how to interrupt the owner based on live availability across the wearable and Mac. This would prevent nonurgent browser/account changes from interrupting the owner while making a genuinely time-sensitive item harder to miss, with an explicit acknowledgement trail rather than repeated alerts.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy for urgency, quiet hours, acknowledgement, and escalation; background model only to classify an unfamiliar finding's urgency. Realtime is used solely to speak an urgent alert and capture acknowledgement.
args.latency_budget: Urgent event delivered within 5 seconds of a confirmed finding; normal events batched at the next availability transition; escalation after a configurable deadline.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for routing and acknowledgement state. Background classification is occasional and dominates model cost; realtime audio is only used for escalated alerts.
args.security_concerns: Availability signals (active app, audio activity, pendant presence) are sensitive. Keep raw presence telemetry local or coarse-grained, transmit only urgency and delivery state, expire unacknowledged content, and do not speak sensitive page/email text aloud until the owner requests details.
missing: A cross-surface availability state machine (pendant connected/away, Mac active/idle/locked, quiet hours, current call or focus mode)
A normalized urgency contract for browser findings, Mac jobs, and relay routines
Durable notification delivery, acknowledgement, deduplication, and escalation records
A pendant-side alert/acknowledge event and a Mac presence adapter
Owner-configurable urgency rules and a dashboard showing why an alert was routed or deferred

transcript.text:
Recorded two new proposals:

1. **Interrupt-aware urgent delivery** — route alerts to the pendant, Mac, or dashboard based on live availability, urgency, quiet hours, and acknowledgement state, with escalation only when necessary.
2. **Cross-surface resumable checkpoints** — pause a task with browser state, evidence, completed actions, and pending decisions, then resume it later with a diff showing what changed.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this page” through the pendant, remember the exact Safari page and the part I’m looking at, then let me ask for it back later.
args.why_useful: It turns fleeting browsing into searchable memory without copy/paste: the pendant supplies intent, Safari supplies authenticated title/URL/selection, the Mac persists a compact citation, and the relay makes it retrievable from any surface. Unlike a generic voice note, the saved item is anchored to what was actually on screen.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to detect the short save command; use a cheaper background model to normalize page text and generate a one-line label; use the relay's normal text retrieval for later questions.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 500 ms; capture the page in 2 s; later retrieval under 3 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per save depending on extracted text length; most cost is one background summarization, not realtime audio.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and any selection leave Safari only to the local Mac and the owner's relay account. Default to storing URL, title, selection, and a short hash/snippet rather than the whole page; require an explicit “save the whole page” phrase for more data.
missing: A browser command that atomically returns active tab URL/title/selection plus a stable content fingerprint
A capture record type linking a saved item to browser tab provenance and searchable embeddings
A retrieval intent that searches these page captures and returns citations

args.user_asks: During a meeting, let me tap the pendant once to bookmark what is happening; afterward give me a timeline of my bookmarks with the active meeting, the Safari page on screen, and a short note for each.
args.why_useful: The owner can mark decisions or follow-ups without interrupting the conversation. The pendant provides a physical, low-friction timestamp; the Mac adds the foreground app and browser evidence; the relay turns sparse bookmarks into a useful post-meeting timeline instead of requiring continuous recording.
args.model_tier: Do not run a large realtime model for each tap. Store an event locally, use a cheap batch model after the meeting to label nearby transcript/page snippets, and reserve realtime for the spoken follow-up request.
args.latency_budget: LED/haptic acknowledgement within 150 ms; event persisted within 1 s; post-meeting timeline within 60 s of the meeting ending.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.10 per meeting, dominated by optional transcript summarization; bookmark-only mode is nearly free.
args.security_concerns: Default mode stores timestamps, foreground app, URL/title, and short local excerpts—not continuous audio. Authenticated page text stays scoped to the owner's Mac/relay and is deleted with the meeting record. Make recording mode visibly distinct via the pendant LED.
missing: A firmware tap event distinct from start/end conversation
A local event journal that snapshots foreground app and active Safari tab at tap time
A meeting-session correlator using Calendar/meeting window identity
A post-meeting endpoint returning cited bookmark evidence

args.user_asks: If the pendant stops responding, let me ask “what’s wrong?” and have the Mac inspect both USB devices, the relay pipeline, and the last audio/job receipts, then tell me the cause and recover what can be recovered.
args.why_useful: Today a dropped call, dead bridge, stale browser, and failed relay job look identical to the wearer. This gives one truthful diagnosis spanning the physically attached nRF9160 and ESP32, the Mac agent, and cloud state, with concrete recovery instead of a vague error LED.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic health probes and receipt correlation first; call a cheap text model only to explain the evidence. Use realtime only if the owner asks while a live call is active.
args.latency_budget: Initial diagnosis in 3 s; safe recovery attempts (reconnect serial, restart bridge process, replay unsent SD chunks) within 15 s; never claim recovery until a new heartbeat/audio packet is observed.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for probes; under $0.01 for an optional explanation. Engineering cost is serial protocol and relay correlation, not model inference.
args.security_concerns: USB logs can contain speech metadata and tokens; redact payload bytes and secrets before cloud upload. Recovery must be limited to the known pendant/bridge processes and produce an immutable local receipt. Never replay audio without telling the owner what interval is being replayed.
missing: A Mac serial health probe for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
A relay endpoint that correlates pipeline audio/events with Mac and device heartbeats
Typed recovery operations for reconnect, bridge restart, and SD failure-buffer replay
A truthful diagnosis contract with observed-at timestamps and a final verification probe

args.name: context_bookmark_button
args.what_it_does: A short double-tap while idle emits a compact context-bookmark event; the Mac immediately snapshots foreground app, active Safari tab metadata, current project/session, and timestamp. A long press still starts conversation, and a tap during a call remains end-call, preserving existing behavior.
args.why_not_server_side: The value is a reliable physical moment marker even when speech recognition, LTE, or the relay is unavailable. Only firmware can capture the button edge with sub-100-ms timing and queue it through a dropped-link interval.
args.trigger: Button double-tap while idle; firmware event queue retries over the existing USB/LTE transport and flashes a distinct two-blink acknowledgement.
args.inputs: Button edge timestamps, current connection state, monotonic sequence number; no microphone audio and no new sensor input.
args.storage: A 32-byte binary event record (sequence, timestamp, event type, CRC) in RAM ring buffer; spill only to the existing SD failure buffer if transport is unavailable. At 64 records this is ~2 kB.
args.ram_budget: ~3 kB including ring metadata and retry state, well below 211,608 B application RAM; no audio buffers or Opus changes required.

args.change: Add a duplex-aware audio scheduler for the nRF9160/relay pair: reserve a minimum uplink slice for mic packets whenever downlink TTS is active, adapt Opus uplink from 16 kbps toward 8 kbps under contention, and mark every dropped packet with a sequence gap. The relay should shorten or pause TTS on detected barge-in rather than allowing both streams to saturate LTE-M.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can interrupt the agent and be heard instead of losing roughly eight seconds of speech during simultaneous talk. Conversations feel responsive on the real pendant, not merely healthy in telemetry.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware packet scheduler and bitrate control, relay congestion feedback, and an integration test over the USB-connected modem/bridge with induced contention.
args.risk: Poor bitrate transitions could create artifacts or starve playback; recover by falling back to the current fixed 16/24 kbps mode when feedback is absent. Sequence numbers make loss visible rather than silently corrupting turns.
args.cost_impact: No API cost and no new hardware; slightly higher CPU during bitrate changes, within the existing ~87% single-core audio load only if transitions avoid extra transcoding.
args.latency_impact: Barge-in acknowledgement improves from multi-second loss to one or two packet intervals; TTS may sound briefly clipped when preempted.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves the device; congestion metadata is non-content telemetry.
depends_on: A framed packet sequence/priority field shared by pendant and relay
Relay-side barge-in detection that can stop queued TTS packets
An integration test harness for the live /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA pair

args.finding: The Mac bridge and Safari extension are online, but the local agent reports ready=false because Accessibility and Screen Recording are not granted; the browser's active tab is currently a failed example.com page. The physical pendant and ESP32 are USB-attached but no serial health endpoint exists yet.

transcript.text:
Round 127 findings:

- Mac bridge and Safari extension are online.
- The active Safari tab is currently a failed `example.com` page.
- The local agent is not fully ready: Accessibility and Screen Recording are still ungranted.
- The nRF9160 pendant and ESP32 bridge are physically USB-connected, but there is still no serial health/recovery endpoint.

I recorded four new proposals:

1. **“Save this page” physical context bookmark** — a pendant command that captures the active Safari page, selection, URL, and provenance for later retrieval.
2. **Meeting bookmark timeline** — a pendant tap marks moments during a meeting; the Mac adds foreground-app and browser evidence, and the relay produces a sourced timeline afterward.
3. **Cross-device pendant diagnosis and recovery** — inspect both USB devices, relay pipeline, jobs, and receipts, then safely recover dropped audio or bridge failures with truthful verification.
4. **Duplex-aware audio scheduler** — reserve uplink capacity during TTS, adapt Opus bitrate, and preempt TTS on barge-in to address the measured ~7.8-second speech loss during simultaneous talking.

I also queued a firmware skill for a **double-tap context bookmark event**, requiring only about 3 KB RAM and no new sensor hardware.

What I still need:

- Implementation of the queued serial diagnostic/recovery capability for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- A device-to-relay heartbeat and packet-sequence contract so failures and replayed audio can be verified rather than guessed.
- The actual Accessibility and Screen Recording grants for the AI Pendant Agent if GUI automation or screenshots are expected.
- Firmware support for distinguishing idle double-tap context bookmarks from the existing conversation button behavior.

args.user_asks: When I walk away from my Mac, quietly checkpoint whatever I was doing, and when I return with the pendant, restore the right Safari tabs, window layout, and unfinished draft without sending or submitting anything.
args.why_useful: The owner can move between rooms or lose connection without reconstructing their working state. The pendant supplies physical presence, the Mac captures the real UI state, and the browser preserves authenticated tabs and drafts; no single surface can provide that continuity alone.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic presence and state capture; use a cheap background model only to name the checkpoint and identify the active task. No realtime reasoning is needed unless the owner asks for restoration by voice.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint within 5 seconds of departure; restore within 10 seconds of return; never restore by submitting, sending, or navigating past an approval boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for state capture; under $0.02 for optional task labeling. Main cost is implementation of presence and browser/window snapshots.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated tabs and drafts remain encrypted/local where possible. A checkpoint must expire, be bound to the owner's pendant identity, and never expose page contents in notifications. Restoration must preserve tab/session affinity and avoid replaying destructive actions.
missing: A presence signal between pendant and Mac that survives relay loss
A versioned Mac window/layout checkpoint format
Browser APIs to save and restore tab groups plus draft-safe DOM state
A conflict resolver when the owner changes the same tab while away

args.user_asks: Let the pendant act as my interruption filter: during a focus block, collect notifications from my Mac and authenticated browser, interrupt me only for things that meet my urgency rule, and give me a one-button way to defer the rest until I am free.
args.why_useful: The owner gets fewer context switches without losing genuinely urgent work. The relay can remain awake, the Mac and browser can see events, and the pendant provides the only interruption channel that follows the owner away from the screen.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a small classifier for urgency; reserve realtime for a concise spoken alert. Batch deferred items with a cheaper model into a digest.
args.latency_budget: Urgent alerts within 10 seconds; defer/dismiss acknowledgement under 1 second; digest generation under 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Typically below $0.01 per event; background summarization dominates, while rule matches are free.
args.security_concerns: Notification text can contain sensitive work or personal data. Keep full content on the Mac/relay account, send only a redacted title and urgency rationale to the pendant, and expose a visible focus-state indicator in the dashboard. Never auto-reply or change notification settings without an explicit request.
missing: A unified event intake for Mac notifications, calendar changes, and authenticated browser alerts
A durable per-owner urgency policy with quiet hours and focus sessions
Pendant alert/defer acknowledgements that work while the Mac is disconnected
A deduplicating event ledger so the same alert is not spoken twice

args.user_asks: When I say “hand this off,” package the exact current browser or Mac state into a private, expiring handoff that another device or a later session can reopen at the same point, with my unsent draft and source citations intact.
args.why_useful: The owner can start research on the Mac, continue from the pendant or phone, and return later without losing the exact context. This is a stateful handoff of work—not a generic briefing or a browser watch—and it preserves what was drafted without accidentally sending it.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic state serialization and citation collection; a cheap model can produce a short handoff label. Realtime is only needed to interpret the short voice command.
args.latency_budget: Create a handoff in under 5 seconds; reopen in under 8 seconds; expired handoffs disappear immediately from all surfaces.
args.cost_estimate: A few cents at most for optional labeling and citation compression; storage is small JSON plus selected snippets.
args.security_concerns: Handoffs may contain authenticated URLs, drafts, and private text. Encrypt at rest, bind access to the owner's paired clients, expire by default, and redact secrets such as passwords or tokens. Reopening must never execute a draft or submit a form.
missing: A cross-client handoff object with encrypted payload, expiry, and capability-scoped access
Browser serialization of tab/session/selection/form-draft state with provenance
Mac restoration of app/window/document context
A pendant and iOS command to enumerate, resume, or discard handoffs

args.change: Replace the prototype's single-button/LED interaction with a production pendant interaction module: add BLE presence beacons (or UWB if reliable room-level presence is required), a low-power vibration motor, and a capacitive double-tap surface while retaining the existing physical button for conversation. Expose signed presence epochs and alert acknowledgements to the nRF9160 firmware and Mac over USB/LTE.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can know when the owner has left or returned, deliver a private interruption without opening a speaker, and distinguish a context bookmark or defer gesture from starting/ending a call. That enables seamless work handoffs and attention protection rather than making the owner repeat commands.
args.effort: High: enclosure and power redesign, BLE/UWB coexistence testing with LTE-M, firmware input state machine, and Mac pairing/reconnection UX.
args.risk: False presence near the Mac or accidental taps could checkpoint or defer the wrong thing. Recover with explicit state LEDs/vibration patterns, debounce and a dashboard history; keep the existing button path as a fallback. UWB increases BOM and power, so BLE can ship first if room-level precision is unnecessary.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$25 BOM increase depending on UWB versus BLE and a $1–$3 haptic motor; intermittent beaconing should add modest battery draw, while UWB ranging can materially increase it.
args.latency_impact: Presence changes in roughly 1–3 seconds with BLE, sub-second with UWB; local vibration acknowledgement is under 100 ms.
args.security_impact: Pairing keys and signed presence epochs must be device-bound; do not broadcast an owner-identifying static address. Presence data should remain local unless needed for a queued handoff.
depends_on: A new firmware event protocol for presence, haptic acknowledgement, and capacitive gestures
Mac and relay support for paired-device identity and presence epochs
A durable handoff/interruption state machine

args.user_asks: Keep my pendant conversational when it is plugged into my Mac, even if LTE or the relay is unavailable: I press the button, speak, hear the response through the audio bridge, and sync the transcript and pending work when connectivity returns.
args.why_useful: This is the first genuinely local/offline use of the hardware that is physically attached today. It makes the pendant useful on a plane, in a basement, or during an outage instead of becoming dead weight whenever the cloud link drops.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap local Mac model for speech/intent triage and deterministic device protocol; use realtime only when the relay is reachable, and sync summaries in background with a cheaper model.
args.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 150 ms; local response under 3 s; cloud handoff and reconciliation can take seconds after reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost offline; occasional background sync uses a small model. Engineering cost is the serial protocol, local audio path, queue reconciliation, and a Mac launch agent.
args.security_concerns: Raw audio and private browser text can remain on the Mac in offline mode. Persist encrypted queue records, expose a clear local/cloud indicator, and require confirmation before replaying queued mutations after reconnect.
missing: nRF9160 USB-serial framing and button/audio control protocol
ESP32 bridge serial/audio playback service
Mac launch agent that discovers /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
offline speech recognition and TTS or a local fallback
idempotent cloud-sync/reconciliation protocol

args.user_asks: Give me a private-mode answer: inspect my currently open authenticated Safari tabs and local Mac state, but keep the page contents and audio on my Mac; send the relay only a redacted request and a short answer, with a switch to reveal the evidence if I ask.
args.why_useful: The wearable can reach the owner anywhere, while the browser holds secrets. This makes that combination usable for banking, health, and work pages without blindly shipping authenticated page contents to the cloud.
args.model_tier: Local Mac model performs extraction, redaction, and evidence selection; realtime handles only the spoken request/response envelope. Use a cheaper background model for redaction QA and caching.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge mode in 200 ms and answer in 5 s for already-open tabs; evidence reveal is an explicit second turn.
args.cost_estimate: Small realtime token usage for redacted text; most extraction stays local. Main cost is a local redaction/evidence broker and browser bridge changes.
args.security_concerns: Treat DOM, screenshots, cookies, and audio as Mac-confidential. Redaction must fail closed on uncertain fields, log hashes rather than contents, and never let a cloud prompt request raw tab data implicitly.
missing: Mac-local redaction service with field/secret detectors
browser result schema separating private evidence from shareable summary
relay metadata flag enforcing no-raw-context mode
pendant indication of private mode and reveal action
auditable local evidence store

args.user_asks: When I say 'continue that later' on the pendant, save the exact state of the conversation and the open Mac/browser work, then let me resume from the pendant or Mac with a one-sentence spoken checkpoint and no repeated explanation.
args.why_useful: Long tasks currently lose the owner's place when attention or connectivity changes. A physical button and spoken checkpoint can suspend work safely and resume it across the wearable, Mac, browser session, and relay.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic state capture and a cheap summarizer; reserve realtime for the resume conversation, not for indexing every event.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint confirmation under 1 s; resume context ready under 2 s from local state, with cloud sync eventually.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost because only compact deltas and a short summary are stored. Engineering cost is cross-surface checkpoint schema and browser/tab attachment persistence.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoint may contain private tab state. Encrypt sensitive fields, store capability-scoped references rather than cookies, expire stale browser attachments, and make spoken summaries avoid secrets by default.
missing: Cross-surface checkpoint schema with versioning
pendant double-press or spoken checkpoint event
Mac job/session and browser-tab snapshot adapter
resume conflict detection when tabs or files changed
sync queue for relay reconnect

args.user_asks: If the Mac or browser agent starts doing something I no longer want, let me long-press the pendant to stop all in-flight work immediately, hear what was cancelled, and later resume only the safe unfinished parts.
args.why_useful: A wearable is the only control surface still in the owner's hand while the Mac is busy or a browser workflow has gone wrong. A physical stop is faster and more reliable than finding a window or speaking over an active response.
args.model_tier: Deterministic device event fan-out and job cancellation; realtime only speaks the concise cancellation receipt, with no model call needed for the stop itself.
args.latency_budget: Hardware acknowledgement under 100 ms; cancel requests dispatched under 300 ms; spoken receipt under 2 s.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost. Requires serial button-event firmware, relay cancellation fan-out, Mac/browser abort handlers, and a compact receipt.
args.security_concerns: Long-press must be hard to trigger accidentally and never erase data. Cancel is safer than undo; report which operations could not be stopped and preserve receipts.
missing: Pendant long-press event and debounce policy
authenticated emergency-cancel endpoint keyed to owner session
fan-out cancellation for Mac jobs, browser commands, vision loops, and relay streams
device haptic/LED acknowledgement
partial-cancel receipt schema

args.change: Add a command execution ledger at the shell boundary that records argv after safe tokenization, cwd, selected environment fingerprints (never raw secrets), start/finish/timeout, stdout/stderr hashes plus a bounded tail, process tree, exit code, and whether the command is reversible. Expose a structured failure bundle and retry recipe through the existing job journal; do not gate or block anything.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the agent says something failed, the owner gets a truthful explanation and a one-tap retry or handoff instead of a vague error. It also makes unattended work auditable without reducing the maximum-access policy.
args.effort: Medium: shell wrapper, redaction, D1 schema, journal API, and UI/voice formatter.
args.risk: Secrets can leak through output or environment; redact known secret patterns and store only hashes by default. Process-tree capture may be incomplete; mark unknown rather than claiming success. Recovery is to retain the existing raw job record.

transcript.text:
Round 128 findings:

- `/ops/status` is healthy: full-control mode is enabled, relay is reachable, and the Safari extension is online with three tabs.
- Mac computer-use is **not ready**: Accessibility is untrusted, Screen Recording is missing, and the vision loop is disabled.
- The physically attached pendant and ESP32 bridge still lack a defined serial control/audio protocol, so USB-local conversation is not yet runnable.

New proposals recorded:

1. **USB-local offline conversation** — button, nRF9160, ESP32 audio bridge, Mac-local processing, and eventual relay reconciliation. This is the strongest capability: it makes the wearable useful today even without LTE or cloud access.
2. **Private-mode browser answers** — authenticated Safari content stays on the Mac; only a redacted request and answer reach the relay.
3. **Cross-surface “continue later” checkpoints** — preserve Mac jobs, browser tabs, evidence, and spoken context for safe resume.
4. **Pendant emergency stop** — long-press cancels in-flight Mac, browser, vision, and relay work and speaks a cancellation receipt.
5. **Shell execution ledger** — recorded as a Mac-harness change, but flagged as close to an existing shell-observability proposal rather than treated as wholly new.

What I still need is implementation work, not another permission request:

- A serial protocol and daemon for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- Local speech recognition/TTS fallback for USB offline mode.
- Relay-level cancellation fan-out and pendant long-press firmware event.
- A Mac-local browser redaction/evidence broker.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions if vision/UI automation is intended.

args.user_asks: Make my Mac and browser automatically enter a private state when my pendant leaves me: pause spoken output, hide sensitive Safari tabs, stop sharing, and restore everything when the pendant returns—without me touching the keyboard.
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one object that travels with the owner. Presence-based privacy protects authenticated work, banking, and health sessions during interruptions or when the owner walks away, something a Mac alone cannot reliably infer.
args.model_tier: Deterministic presence and policy engine; no expensive model call for lock/unlock. Use realtime only to announce state changes when appropriate.
args.latency_budget: Detect departure within 2 seconds and apply browser/audio protections within 1 second; restore within 2 seconds after return.
args.cost_estimate: No per-use model cost. Requires a low-power proximity signal, Mac presence daemon, Safari tab masking, and relay session coordination.
args.security_concerns: False departures must not destroy work; suspend and restore exact tab state. Never treat presence alone as authentication for financial actions. Keep presence history local and expire it quickly.
missing: Low-power pendant-to-Mac proximity transport
Pendant presence heartbeat firmware
Mac privacy-state daemon
Safari tab redaction/restore API
Relay stream pause/resume tied to presence state

args.user_asks: When a sensitive value is visible in my authenticated browser—such as a one-time code, delivery address, or account number—let me ask from the pendant for just that value and whisper it locally through the audio bridge, without sending the page or value through the relay.
args.why_useful: The browser has private sessions and the pendant has the owner's attention, but today there is no safe local handoff between them. This would make the wearable useful for quick lookups while sharply reducing exposure of secrets.
args.model_tier: Mac-local deterministic extraction first, with a small local model only for semantic field identification; realtime is limited to the spoken request envelope and should not receive the secret.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds for an already-open tab; no cloud round trip for the extracted value.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost per lookup. Engineering cost is local browser extraction, secret-type validation, and ESP32 audio playback.
args.security_concerns: Do not persist the value, include it in logs, or expose it to relay telemetry. Require a deliberate button gesture for playback, redact browser evidence, and refuse ambiguous matches.
missing: Mac-local browser extraction endpoint
Secret-value classification and non-persistence rules
USB audio-bridge playback protocol

Local-only request routing

The beacon should expose only an ephemeral identifier and support a signed return-to-presence handshake; it must not become a general-purpose tracking device.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's wearable can become a reliable privacy boundary: walking away can protect browser sessions and audio automatically, while returning restores the exact working state. The current button and USB connection cannot detect daily physical presence once unplugged.
args.effort: Medium-high hardware revision plus firmware, macOS daemon, Safari integration, and relay session-state support.
args.risk: Radio loss can cause nuisance privacy transitions; use hysteresis and suspend/restore rather than destructive actions. Battery life and pairing bugs are the main recovery concerns.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–8 in added BLE-capable beacon/sensor hardware depending on board revision, with low average power draw; negligible model cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second local detection after radio tuning; no network latency required.
args.security_impact: Use rotating identifiers, authenticated pairing, no location history, and local-only presence logs. A stolen beacon must not unlock accounts or authorize transactions.

Browser tab masking/restoration integration
Relay pause/resume state model
