args.user_asks: “Where was that thing I looked at earlier—the page, file, or message I was just reading—and put me back there.”
args.why_useful: People lose work across Safari tabs, desktop windows, and project folders constantly. A wearable should recover the owner's recent visual context by meaning, not require them to remember a title or manually search history. This is a genuinely cross-surface ability: the Mac observes local context, the browser supplies private tab/session metadata, the relay resolves the spoken reference, and the pendant returns the result while away from the keyboard.
args.model_tier: Cheap background indexing of redacted foreground-app/tab/file metadata; realtime model only resolves the owner's vague spoken reference and, if necessary, compares a few candidate screenshots or text snippets.
args.latency_budget: Return the top three candidates in under 2 seconds and open the selected one in under 1 second. Indexing runs opportunistically and should never slow foreground work.
args.cost_estimate: Low when using titles, URLs, paths, and timestamps; screenshot/text comparison is the expensive fallback. Most indexing is local and incurs no cloud token cost.
args.security_concerns: Keep a local encrypted index with per-application privacy exclusions and retention limits. Never upload full browser history, private messages, or screenshots by default. Require an explicit spoken confirmation before opening a sensitive page or file on a shared display.
missing: A local, time-decayed context index spanning foreground apps, Safari tabs, files, and browser sessions
A semantic resolver that can search that index without sending its raw contents to the relay
A stable Mac deep-link/open-context action that restores the exact tab, window, scroll position, or file selection
A pendant response format for disambiguation candidates and an offline-safe ‘last known context’ cache

args.user_asks: “While I’m walking, read me the important parts of the page or document I left on my Mac, let me say ‘save that’ or ‘skip it’, and have the exact place stay queued until I’m back.”
args.why_useful: This makes the wearable a continuity surface rather than a remote control. The browser keeps the authenticated session and the Mac keeps the file; the pendant provides a private, eyes-free review and durable intent when the owner is away. The owner can turn a research or work session into a short spoken triage without exposing credentials or manually copying links.
args.model_tier: Background model extracts a short local summary and candidate highlights; realtime model handles the owner's spoken save/skip/follow-up commands. Use deterministic local extraction for ordinary text and vision only for layout-heavy pages.
args.latency_budget: First spoken excerpt within 3 seconds, next excerpt under 1 second, and each save/skip acknowledged within 300 ms. Queue intents offline and reconcile on reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: One small summarization call per changed document, with browser text extraction keeping most turns cheap. Vision and long PDFs are the dominant cost; cache summaries by content hash.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page text and local documents remain on the Mac by default. Redact passwords, forms, cookies, and unrelated tabs before any model call. Saving must store a pointer/content hash, not duplicate private content into relay memory; deletions and retention need owner control.
missing: A Mac-side read-aloud cursor that can extract and chunk a private tab/document without changing the user's page
A durable spoken annotation/save queue tied to URL or file identity plus content hash and selection offsets
A relay/pendant protocol for streaming short excerpts and accepting save/skip intents with exactly-once delivery
A local destination integration (notes, project context, or task list) that records the saved excerpt and provenance

args.user_asks: “Before you act on my behalf, tell me in one sentence what the other agents are about to do, and after they finish give me one combined answer—not three competing updates.”
args.why_useful: The hive currently has multiple surfaces that can observe, plan, and act. The owner should experience one accountable assistant, not duplicated browser clicks, contradictory voice messages, or a Mac job that the pendant reports differently from the dashboard. A cross-agent intent lease and final synthesis would make delegation trustworthy at the moment it matters.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic coordinator for leases, deduplication, and state aggregation; realtime model only compresses the final status into a spoken sentence. Use no expensive model for identical observations or already-known receipts.
args.latency_budget: Pre-action spoken plan under 500 ms for known actions; concurrent observations coalesce within 1 s; one final result within 2 s of the last receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below one realtime turn because coordination is deterministic. Savings come from suppressing duplicate model calls and repeated screenshots, not from adding inference.
args.security_concerns: Every side effect needs an owner-visible intent ID, acting surface, target, and expiry. A lease must prevent two agents from executing the same mutation while still allowing independent read-only observations. Receipts should redact shell environments, page secrets, and private content; stale leases must expire safely rather than silently replay.
missing: A shared intent/lease registry across relay, Mac, and browser agents
Canonical action IDs and causal parent IDs propagated into /execute, browser commands, pipeline events, and pendant acknowledgements
A reducer that turns heterogeneous receipts into one success/partial/failure/unknown outcome
A single owner-facing notification policy with deduplication, urgency, and replay protection

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Recover and reopen lost context** — ask “Where was that thing I was just reading?” and restore the exact browser tab, file, window, or scroll position. This requires a private, time-decayed Mac/browser context index and deep-link restoration.

2. **Walk-away document triage** — have the pendant read important excerpts from a Mac document or authenticated page, then say “save that” or “skip it.” This requires streamed local extraction, durable spoken annotations, content-hash provenance, and offline intent queuing.

3. **One accountable hive mind** — receive one concise pre-action explanation and one combined final result rather than conflicting updates from relay, Mac, browser, and vision agents. This requires shared intent leases, canonical causal IDs, receipt reduction, deduplication, and unified notification policy.

args.user_asks: “Finish the thing I started on my Mac, even if the link drops: when I reconnect the pendant, continue the browser or shell workflow from its last safe checkpoint and tell me exactly what happened.”
args.why_useful: Today a long Mac job can be left processing, cancellation is cooperative, and interrupted ledgers are never resumed automatically. This would turn the worn device into a true remote control for unfinished work rather than a second, stateless microphone. The relay queues the intent, the Mac persists step checkpoints, and the browser preserves authenticated session affinity; reconnecting the pendant yields a truthful resume or a precise stop reason.
args.model_tier: background for checkpoint reconciliation and retry planning; realtime only for the short spoken status on reconnect
args.latency_budget: A reconnect status in under 2 seconds; resume begins within 5 seconds. Checkpoint reconciliation can take 10–30 seconds in the background.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one short realtime response plus occasional background planner calls; dominant cost is only when a failed step needs replanning, not on every heartbeat.
args.security_concerns: The Mac must retain opaque browser session/tab IDs and command receipts, never send cookies or shell environment to the relay. Resume only the exact idempotent checkpoint; require explicit owner confirmation for a step whose prior receipt is ambiguous. The pendant should say 'stopped, not verified' rather than invent success.
missing: A durable step checkpoint protocol joining jobId, ledgerId, browser commandId, and pendant turn ID
Boot-time reconciliation that closes or marks open ledgers and offers resumable steps
Abortable run_shell execution and an idempotency-aware retry executor
A relay-to-pendant queued-resume message type with authenticated nonce and monotonic sequence

args.user_asks: “From the pendant, carry out this authenticated browser action and prove the result: send the message, submit the form, or place the order, then read back the exact account/page confirmation and leave me a receipt I can inspect later.”
args.why_useful: A voice agent that merely clicks is dangerous because a success-looking UI can hide a failed submission, wrong tab, or stale session. This makes the unique combination of pendant intent, browser-held credentials, Mac execution, and relay receipt into a dependable action: the owner gets a spoken result grounded in post-action evidence, not an optimistic model sentence.
args.model_tier: realtime for intent disambiguation and a one-sentence spoken result; deterministic browser actions and evidence extraction first, background model only when the page needs interpretation
args.latency_budget: Simple actions 3–8 seconds; evidence verification up to 15 seconds. Do not speak completion until a postcondition is observed or timeout is explicitly reported.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: deterministic browser calls dominate latency; use the expensive model only for ambiguous page semantics or conflicting evidence.
args.security_concerns: Credentials and page contents remain in the browser bridge. Bind every action to tab/session ID, origin, and a nonce from the pendant; redact secrets from receipts. For irreversible purchases, deletion, or external messages, the pendant must get a concise confirmation before dispatch; completion still requires independent postcondition evidence.
missing: A typed postcondition/evidence contract for browser actions (expected URL, DOM text, receipt number, or changed state)
Cross-surface transaction ID carried from pendant audio turn through relay, Mac job, browser command, and durable receipt
A browser result verifier that rejects stale-tab or wrong-origin evidence
A dashboard receipt view with before/after evidence and spoken/visual distinction between dispatched and verified

args.user_asks: “Stop the Mac task that is running right now.” (spoken to the pendant, with “the task” resolved from the latest spoken request or currently active job)
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one surface available while walking away from the Mac, but today cancellation only sends a cooperative signal and cannot interrupt a running shell child. A real remote stop would prevent runaway commands, browser loops, or an accidentally expensive workflow from continuing, then report whether it was actually terminated.
args.model_tier: realtime for resolving the current job and speaking the result; deterministic relay routing and host process control, with no planner call unless the reference is ambiguous
args.latency_budget: A stop request should reach the Mac in under 1 second and produce a truthful terminated/not-terminated response within 3 seconds. Long-running process cleanup may be bounded at 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: a short realtime utterance and deterministic control calls; no background LLM needed for an unambiguous current-job stop.
args.security_concerns: Bind cancellation to the authenticated pendant session and a concrete job/process identity, never 'kill all'. The Mac must distinguish graceful cancellation from SIGTERM/SIGKILL and record the escalation. If the host is offline, the relay queues a stop intent with expiry and the pendant says it has not yet stopped anything; on reconnect, stale intents must not kill a new job.
missing: A live-job registry that exposes jobId, action, child PID/process group, and owner-facing label to the relay
Abortable run_shell using a process group and signal escalation rather than exec without signal
A typed remote-cancel route carrying jobId, nonce, expiry, and expected session ID
Pendant voice-to-intent routing for cancel plus a completion receipt that truthful_action_status_beacon can display

args.subject: Round 170 cross-node gaps
args.body: Three proposals recorded: resumable cross-node workflow, postcondition-verified browser transaction, and true pendant remote cancel. Key missing connective contract is one transaction ID/nonce across pendant turn -> relay -> Mac job/ledger -> browser command -> receipt, plus process-group cancellation and postcondition evidence.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.change: Make every run_shell action execute through a tracked process group with a stable child PID, explicit start/finish/exit metadata, and a cancellation escalation: send SIGTERM to the group, wait a bounded interval, then SIGKILL descendants. Persist the group identity and a monotonic execution sequence in the receipt, and make the relay's cancel intent target that exact sequence.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says stop from the pendant, the command actually stops instead of continuing invisibly for up to two minutes. They can also trust the later answer: terminated, exited itself, or could not be reached — rather than a generic cooperative-cancel message.
args.effort: Medium: replace exec with a spawn/execFile-style wrapper, create process-group bookkeeping, persist exit metadata, and add crash cleanup/reconciliation tests.
args.risk: Some commands depend on shell semantics, so preserve an explicit shell mode and test pipes/redirection. Killing a process group can terminate legitimate descendants; target only the recorded group and expose the command label. On agent crash, reconcile orphan groups conservatively instead of killing by stale PID alone.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small CPU and disk overhead for process metadata.
args.latency_impact: Normal commands are effectively unchanged; cancellation becomes seconds instead of waiting for the command timeout.
args.security_impact: No new authority beyond the already deliberate unrestricted shell. Stable process-group identity improves auditability and prevents an ambiguous remote cancel from affecting another job.
depends_on: A relay-visible current-job identity and authenticated cancel intent
Boot-time handling for orphaned process groups
The accepted truthful_action_status_beacon state mapping

args.user_asks: “What am I looking at right now, and is it safe to trust?” — asked while away from the Mac, with the answer grounded in the active window, browser origin, visible page, and the last action receipt.
args.why_useful: The owner can currently get a screenshot or browser text, but not a compact, cross-checked answer about whether the visible UI is the expected authenticated page or a stale/error/phishing-looking state. This would use the pendant as an always-available question surface, the Mac for foreground/window facts, the browser extension for origin and DOM evidence, and the relay for a short spoken explanation.
args.model_tier: realtime for the final spoken answer; deterministic collection first, with a small background classifier for page-state comparison and only escalate to the expensive model when evidence conflicts
args.latency_budget: Collect evidence in 1–3 seconds and speak within 5 seconds; if the screenshot and DOM disagree, say that explicitly rather than delaying indefinitely.
args.cost_estimate: Low for ordinary checks; browser and host probes dominate. Expensive model calls occur only on conflicting or novel UI states.
args.security_concerns: Never transmit cookies, passwords, or full page contents by default. Bind evidence to active window, tab ID, origin, and capture timestamp; redact sensitive fields in the dashboard receipt. The answer must distinguish observed facts from model interpretation.
missing: A single evidence capsule joining active-window capture, browser tab metadata, DOM text, origin, and recent action receipt
A Mac-vision route that can return a bounded redacted view while preserving provenance
A relay intent that requests a read-only trust check rather than an action
A compact pendant speech/result format for confidence and conflicting evidence

args.user_asks: “Only interrupt me when this is genuinely urgent.” Then let the system arbitrate browser-watch changes, Mac job failures, and scheduled results against whether I am recording, speaking, presenting, or idle, and deliver the least disruptive alert that still meets the deadline.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has independent jobs, watches, routines, and pendant alerts, but no hive-wide interruption decision. A relay that knows the wearable's conversation state, the Mac's foreground activity, browser urgency, and job deadlines can stop routine completions from talking over the owner while still surfacing a failed payment, expiring form, or blocked task in time.
args.model_tier: Background/deterministic scoring for every event; realtime only when an urgent alert must be phrased for speech. Do not spend the expensive tier on ordinary event arbitration.
args.latency_budget: Classify events under 250 ms; urgent escalation under 2 seconds; defer nonurgent events until the next natural conversational boundary or idle window.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: event scoring and scheduling dominate, with occasional short realtime speech generation.
args.security_concerns: Urgency rules and quiet hours remain local and inspectable. Browser page text should be minimized and redacted before relay scoring. Never suppress a deadline-critical event solely because the owner is busy; expose the reason and age of every deferred alert.
missing: A shared event envelope with source, deadline, urgency evidence, sensitivity, and deduplication key
A pendant conversation/recording-state feed available to the relay in real time
A Mac foreground/presentation/idle signal and browser-watch change severity classifier
One durable alert queue with coalescing, quiet-window delivery, expiry, and truthful LED/audio state

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /watches. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: “Work on this until it is done, but stop at $X, 20 minutes, or any irreversible step, and bring me the best next decision.” The pendant should let me set that budget, while the Mac, browser, and relay execute and checkpoint the work without needing me to micromanage every click.
args.why_useful: Today the owner can ask for an action or a plan, but cannot give the hive a bounded objective with an explicit time/cost/risk budget and receive a decision-ready checkpoint. This is the difference between a remote command and a dependable personal operator: the relay remains awake, the Mac can act, the browser retains authenticated context, and the pendant is the escalation channel.
args.model_tier: Background planner for multi-step execution and checkpoint summaries; realtime only for initial budget capture and escalation questions. Deterministic tiers should enforce elapsed-time, step-count, and spend budgets.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the budget in under 2 seconds; ordinary steps proceed asynchronously; escalate at the first boundary or within 5 seconds of a blocked decision.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate and controllable: background planner calls only at checkpoints, with a hard token/request budget. Browser and Mac execution are the dominant wall-clock costs, not conversation.
args.security_concerns: Budgets must be signed to the specific task and expire. No irreversible or external side effect may be silently inferred as allowed just because time remains. Persist every consumed budget unit and evidence; if the relay is offline, the Mac must fail closed at the last checkpoint and the pendant must report that it cannot supervise.
missing: A first-class task lease containing owner intent, deadline, token/API budget, allowed effect classes, and escalation policy
Budget accounting across planner calls, browser commands, shell runtime, and network/API spend
Checkpoint summaries that cite receipts and expose the exact next decision
A pendant control/result protocol for pause, resume, amend-budget, and abandon

transcript.summary: Recorded three capabilities the owner cannot have today: a cross-checked “what am I looking at, and is it trustworthy?” spoken inspection; hive-wide interruption arbitration that respects recording/presentation state and deadlines; and bounded autonomous work leases with explicit time, cost, and irreversible-step budgets. Each requires new connective contracts across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser rather than another standalone Mac feature.
transcript.biggest_unknown: The exact live pendant transport framing and firmware event surface remain unavailable, so the proposed real-time state, budget, and evidence messages need protocol work before implementation.

args.subject: Cross-surface proposal check
args.body: I’m proposing a wearable->browser/Mac recovery workflow and browser urgent-item digest. What live relay event/job hooks should I cite, and any duplicate backlog IDs to avoid?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: “Continue the task I started on my Mac, even if the agent or browser crashed.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets real continuity instead of a dead 'failed' notification: the pendant identifies the unfinished job, the relay finds its durable journal/ledger, the Mac restores the exact project and browser checkpoint, and the browser extension verifies what is still on screen before the next action. It can safely resume a half-completed research, filing, or web workflow rather than repeating side effects blindly.
args.model_tier: Background model reconstructs the checkpoint and proposes the next step; realtime is used only for the short spoken status and any interruption.
args.latency_budget: 5–15 seconds to reconstruct and inspect; then actions stream as ordinary Mac/browser work.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per resume, dominated by vision/browser inspection context; no model call if the durable checkpoint proves the next deterministic step.
args.security_concerns: The checkpoint can contain authenticated page titles, file paths, and task text. Keep raw screenshots and command output on the Mac; send the relay only a redacted summary and opaque job ID. Do not replay a side effect whose postcondition is unknown; mark it 'needs recovery' and ask the owner verbally before continuing that one step.
missing: Boot-time reconciliation of processing jobs and open ledgers
A job↔ledger join and an explicit per-step postcondition/checkpoint record
Process-group cancellation and idempotent retry for run_shell
A browser checkpoint endpoint that records inspected tab/frame identity and last verified DOM state

args.user_asks: “Check my authenticated work sites and tell me only what changed that actually needs me today.”
args.why_useful: This turns the previously denied portal briefing into the correct browser-owned workflow. The browser extension can see sessions that the relay and Mac cannot, compare the current page against a private per-site baseline, and the pendant can deliver a short interruption-free spoken list. The owner does not have to expose passwords or manually copy portal pages into chat.
args.model_tier: Background model performs site-by-site diffing and priority ranking; realtime only speaks the final two or three actionable items.
args.latency_budget: Under 30 seconds after the owner asks; site inspection is parallelized and bounded to 5 seconds per tab.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.02–$0.10 per request, mostly DOM/text extraction and ranking; screenshots are used only when a page is visual or ambiguous.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated content stays in the extension until it has been reduced to an owner-approved summary. Never send cookies, tokens, hidden form values, or full page HTML to the relay. Site allowlists and a local encrypted baseline are required; any suggested reply or mutation is returned as a draft, not silently submitted.
missing: Per-site authenticated-session allowlist and encrypted local baselines
A browser diff/priority endpoint that can inspect several existing tabs without copying secrets
A scheduler that runs only when the browser session is present and reports stale/unavailable sites truthfully
Relay payload redaction for browser-derived summaries

args.user_asks: “Run this long Mac job and keep me informed; if it fails, recover it without me staring at the screen.”
args.why_useful: The pendant becomes a remote operator, not a one-shot command button. The Mac starts the work, emits milestone receipts, and on failure captures the failing step and a bounded diagnostic; the relay speaks only meaningful transitions. The owner can say 'retry the safe step' or 'stop' while away from the laptop, and a dead Mac process cannot be mistaken for completion.
args.model_tier: Cheap background worker watches receipts and classifies recoverable failures; realtime is reserved for a concise alert or the owner's spoken intervention.
args.latency_budget: Immediate dispatch acknowledgement under 1 second; milestone alerts within 2 seconds of receipt; recovery begins within 5 seconds of a retry instruction.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.03 per job when deterministic receipt rules handle progress; model cost appears only on an ambiguous failure.
args.security_concerns: Command text, paths, and output may contain secrets. Store full logs locally and send the relay a redacted error plus job ID. Recovery must use action idempotency/postconditions, never blind whole-job replay; destructive or externally visible steps remain explicitly described to the owner even though the Mac policy permits maximum access.
missing: A real-time per-step event stream including exit code, pid/process-group, effective command after rewrites, and bounded stdout/stderr
Cancellation wired to the child process group rather than only the between-step abort signal
Retry/idempotency engine connected to /execute
Boot reconciliation that marks orphaned processing jobs and closes ledgers
Pendant command correlation for spoken retry/stop intents

args.change: Replace the shell execution internals with a durable command envelope: preserve original and effective (rewrite-resolved) command, use execFile/argv where possible while retaining an explicit raw-shell escape hatch, record redacted environment fingerprints, capture exit code/signal/pid/process-group and bounded stdout/stderr, pass AbortSignal to the child process group, close the ledger with the jobId, and reconcile processing/open records at boot. Expose one append-only per-step event stream consumed by pendant and relay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks the pendant to do something while away from the Mac, they will know what actually ran, whether it finished, and can stop or resume a stuck task. A crash will no longer leave a job falsely marked 'running' forever or cause an unsafe blind replay.
args.effort: Medium-high: executor/computerControl, jobTracker, actionLedger, orchestrator, and bridge event plumbing; add migration for existing records and integration tests around rewrites, SIGTERM, restart, and retry.
args.risk: Changing exec semantics can break shell-dependent commands; preserve raw-shell mode and compare old/new envelopes in shadow logging first. A process-group kill may terminate grandchildren intentionally; record the tree and offer recovery from the last settled step. Reconciliation must distinguish an orphan from a still-running external process.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; modest local disk for capped event/receipt records (roughly <1 MB per rolling history).
args.latency_impact: Tiny dispatch overhead (<100 ms); event emission is local and asynchronous. Restart recovery becomes faster because stale jobs are identified at boot.
args.security_impact: Better than today: current run_shell inherits AGENT_TOKEN and model keys and records none of that. Record only a hash/name allowlist of environment keys, never values; keep full stdout local and redact relay events.
depends_on: Define the job↔ledger correlation field and close-ledger lifecycle
Choose a stable child-process runner with AbortSignal/process-group support
Add relay/pipeline subscription for per-step events

args.finding: The live inventory now shows Safari on MacIntel with 9 tabs online and home-macbook-bridge online; cloudflare-contract-test mobile remains offline. Browser inspections are currently empty.
args.evidence: discover:devices returned Safari on MacIntel browser online (9 tabs), home-macbook-bridge online, cloudflare-contract-test offline; GET /browser/inspections returned {ok:true, inspections:[]}.

transcript.summary: This round produced three owner-facing capabilities: resume a crashed Mac/browser task from a verified checkpoint; browser-owned authenticated work-site change triage (the correct re-file of the previously denied portal briefing); and a wearable long-job operator with truthful milestones, recovery, and spoken retry/stop. I also proposed the underlying Mac execution-envelope change, but the recorder flagged it as close to an existing observability idea, so it should be treated as a refinement rather than a separate feature. Live discovery confirms Safari (9 tabs) and the Mac bridge are online; browser inspections are empty, and the test mobile device is offline. I still need implementation—not another wrapper—of the missing joins: job↔ledger correlation and boot reconciliation, per-step event streaming, child-process cancellation/retry, browser authenticated diff baselines, and pendant intent correlation. The previously queued mac USB-serial diagnostics request remains the only access request; I will not re-ask for it.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the browser extension can expose stable authenticated tab/frame identity and a redacted DOM-diff baseline without leaking session content; that determines whether the portal-triage capability can be built safely rather than merely planned.

args.summary: This round produced three owner-facing capabilities: resume a crashed Mac/browser task from a verified checkpoint; browser-owned authenticated work-site change triage (the correct re-file of the previously denied portal briefing); and a wearable long-job operator with truthful milestones, recovery, and spoken retry/stop. I also proposed the underlying Mac execution-envelope change, but the recorder flagged it as close to an existing observability idea, so it should be treated as a refinement rather than a separate feature. Live discovery confirms Safari (9 tabs) and the Mac bridge are online; browser inspections are empty, and the test mobile device is offline. I still need implementation—not another wrapper—of the missing joins: job↔ledger correlation and boot reconciliation, per-step event streaming, child-process cancellation/retry, browser authenticated diff baselines, and pendant intent correlation. The previously queued mac USB-serial diagnostics request remains the only access request; I will not re-ask for it.
args.biggest_unknown: Whether the browser extension can expose stable authenticated tab/frame identity and a redacted DOM-diff baseline without leaking session content; that determines whether the portal-triage capability can be built safely rather than merely planned.

args.user_asks: “Undo the last thing you did, even if it happened in Safari or through a Mac app.”
args.why_useful: Today undo only covers a small set of local actions. The owner should get a semantic reversal: identify the last externally visible action, explain its evidence and reversibility, then perform the compensating action—restore a moved file, revert an edit, withdraw a queued browser change, or draft a correction—across the browser and Mac. The pendant gives one concise spoken result instead of forcing the owner to remember which surface acted.
args.model_tier: Background model builds and checks a compensation plan from receipts; realtime only handles the owner's short undo request and result.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds to identify the candidate and describe the reversal; under 20 seconds for a reversible local/browser compensation.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.06 per invocation; dominated by reconstructing the action and checking the current browser/app state.
args.security_concerns: A reversal can itself have consequences. Never claim success without a postcondition check; preserve the original receipt and compensation receipt locally. Do not automatically send external corrections or cancel financial/legal actions—speak the proposed compensation and require an explicit owner instruction for those exceptional classes.
missing: A typed compensation registry for Mac and browser actions, including postconditions
Cross-surface receipt ordering with stable action IDs and effect scope
Browser extension support for reversing its supported mutations rather than only reporting them
A pendant utterance/intention route that addresses a specific receipt

args.user_asks: “Explain what I’m looking at on my screen, privately, and point me to the exact source.”
args.why_useful: The owner can ask through the pendant while a sensitive page is open and receive a grounded spoken explanation without sending a raw screenshot or authenticated page to the relay. Mac vision reads the pixels, the browser extension supplies the accessible text and URL/title, and the answer cites the exact visible region or DOM element. If asked, it can then open the cited source or copy only the selected fact.
args.model_tier: A local/cheap vision-text pass fuses DOM and pixels; realtime is used only for the short spoken answer.
args.latency_budget: 2–4 seconds for ordinary pages; up to 8 seconds for dense visual documents.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.04 per request, with local extraction avoiding repeated cloud image tokens.
args.security_concerns: Raw screen pixels and authenticated DOM remain on the Mac. Send the relay only a redacted question, answer, and source locator; source locators must not include query-string tokens. Blur password/payment fields before any model sees them, and refuse to read hidden or off-screen content.
missing: A local multimodal fusion service joining a screenshot region to browser DOM coordinates
A redaction/secret-field detector that runs before model invocation
A source-locator protocol understood by the pendant response renderer

args.user_asks: “Hand this unfinished task to my future self tomorrow, with exactly what I saw and what remains.”
args.why_useful: Instead of a reminder with no context, the owner gets a sealed, resumable handoff capsule: the pendant records the intent, the Mac captures the relevant project and app state, the browser extension records only the permitted tab identity and evidence, and the relay delivers a compact brief at the chosen time. Opening it restores the task without reconstructing the whole conversation.
args.model_tier: Background model compresses and redacts the capsule; scheduled delivery uses a cheap model, with realtime only for the spoken capture and reminder.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 2 seconds; capsule generation under 10 seconds; restore under 15 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per handoff, mostly state compression; scheduled delivery costs pennies or less.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private page titles, paths, and snippets. Encrypt them locally, store an expiry and allowed surfaces, and exclude passwords, cookies, and full screenshots by default. The spoken reminder should reveal only the capsule title until the owner asks to open it.
missing: A first-class encrypted handoff-capsule store with expiry and surface permissions
A Mac snapshot adapter for foreground app, project, and relevant window state
A browser evidence adapter that stores stable locators plus a redacted excerpt
A restore planner that validates state before reopening or editing anything

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface semantic undo** — reverse the last Mac or browser action with verified compensation and truthful postconditions.
2. **Private screen explanation** — fuse local vision with browser DOM, redact secrets, and explain the visible page through the pendant with exact source locators.
3. **Resumable future-self handoffs** — capture an encrypted, expiring capsule containing relevant Mac/browser state, then restore it later without reconstructing the task.

Each requires new connective primitives rather than another wrapper around existing routes: compensation registries, local multimodal fusion and redaction, and encrypted state capsules with validated restoration.

args.user_asks: When a Mac command fails, fix it for me: show me the exact failure, make one safe corrective attempt, and tell me what changed.
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell job loses the exit code and cannot be retried intelligently; the owner has to diagnose and reissue it manually. This turns the pendant into a practical operator rather than a one-shot command launcher.
args.model_tier: background for diagnosis and repair planning; realtime only for the short spoken result
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds to report the failure; up to 30 seconds for one corrective attempt
args.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap background inference; dominant cost is command execution, not tokens
args.security_concerns: The repair can mutate files or processes under the owner's deliberately unrestricted Mac policy. Return command, cwd, exit code, stderr, diff/receipt, and never claim success without a post-check; require explicit confirmation only for destructive repairs if owner policy changes.
missing: Capture real exit code, signal, pid, argv/env provenance, and rewritten-vs-submitted command in the shell receipt
A bounded repair loop with one retry and idempotency key; current cancellation cannot interrupt exec and no job retry is wired
Join job record to action ledger and close/reconcile ledgers so a repair can resume after restart

args.user_asks: Save this page as evidence.
args.why_useful: A spoken request from the pendant should preserve the exact authenticated page the owner is looking at, not just a URL: snapshot the visible state, relevant text, timestamp, and provenance so it can be revisited even after the session changes.
args.model_tier: background model extracts a concise title and evidence summary; realtime only acknowledges capture
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; persist the bundle within 5 seconds
args.cost_estimate: Low: one small extraction call; storage and screenshot dominate, with no web-search call
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents leave the browser and are sensitive. Default to local Mac storage, encrypt the bundle, redact passwords/tokens/forms, show domain/title before persistence, and make sharing/export a separate explicit request.
missing: Browser command that atomically captures sanitized DOM/text, screenshot, URL, tab identity, and page timestamp
Mac-side encrypted evidence-bundle store with content hash and retention policy
Relay index and pendant lookup by spoken title/date, including offline queued capture receipt

args.user_asks: Watch this long-running task and interrupt me only if it needs me.
args.why_useful: The owner can hand off a build, sync, export, or research job and stop babysitting it. The Mac observes output and process health while the always-awake relay filters routine progress; the pendant speaks only a failure, permission prompt, completion, or a decision it cannot make.
args.model_tier: Cheap background classifier over incremental output; realtime model only when escalation is actually spoken
args.latency_budget: Detect an actionable event within 5 seconds; no periodic spoken chatter
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: polling and local parsing dominate; model calls only on novel output or escalation candidates
args.security_concerns: Output may contain source code, URLs, or secrets. Parse locally first, redact tokens, retain bounded excerpts, and never auto-answer a prompt that can grant permissions or send data. The pendant must label stale monitoring after Mac disconnect.
missing: A supervisor job type that attaches to a PID/process group and streams bounded stdout/stderr incrementally
Event classifier with deduplication, quiet hours, escalation severity, and owner acknowledgement state
True process cancellation/reattachment and restart reconciliation; current /jobs cancel is cooperative between steps and exec has no signal

args.change: Add a local Mac failure-and-progress parser before any LLM call. It classifies exit status, common compiler/test/package-manager errors, permission prompts, and completion markers; only ambiguous excerpts go to the background model, and only owner-facing escalations reach realtime.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Long commands become quieter, faster, and cheaper: routine success is silent, familiar failures get an immediate precise explanation, and the expensive voice model is reserved for decisions that genuinely need conversation.
args.effort: Medium: local parser, bounded stream reader, redaction, confidence thresholds, and routing hooks in the job supervisor.
args.risk: A parser can misclassify a failure as success or suppress an important prompt. Use conservative completion rules, retain raw receipts locally, and escalate low-confidence events rather than dropping them.
args.cost_impact: Reduces inference spend substantially for builds and scripts; negligible CPU cost on the Mac.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second classification for known patterns; ambiguous cases add one background call.
args.security_impact: Less command output leaves the Mac; redaction happens before relay/model upload.
depends_on: A shell receipt carrying exit code and process identity
Incremental stdout/stderr streaming or bounded tail capture
Supervisor/monitor job type

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
This round I established:

- The Mac bridge is online, and Safari has 9 open tabs.
- The pendant and ESP32 bridge are physically usable over USB, but the relay still has no registered LTE device.
- The current Mac surface still lacks reliable shell observability: exit codes, process identity, incremental output, job/ledger joins, true cancellation, retry, and restart reconciliation.

I proposed four additions:

1. **Failure-aware command recovery** — report the real failure, make one bounded corrective attempt, verify the result, and tell the owner exactly what changed.
2. **“Save this page as evidence”** — browser capture of sanitized authenticated-page content, screenshot, URL, timestamp, and hash into an encrypted local evidence bundle.
3. **Long-running task supervision** — watch builds, exports, syncs, or research jobs and interrupt the owner only for actionable failures, permission prompts, completion, or decisions.
4. **Local output triage** — classify familiar shell failures and completion locally, sending only ambiguous cases to a cheaper background model and reserving realtime voice for actual interaction.

What I still need:

- The pending **USB serial diagnostics capability** to inspect the live nRF9160 and ESP32 links directly.
- A real process-supervisor/streaming interface on the Mac: PID/process-group tracking, incremental stdout/stderr, exit code, signal-aware cancellation, and reattachment after restart.
- A durable job-to-ledger identity join and boot-time reconciliation.
- Browser-side atomic evidence capture with sanitization and encrypted local storage.
- A bounded local classifier for shell output before sending anything to the relay or model.

args.user_asks: While I’m away, keep this task moving until morning, but stop at the first ambiguity and leave me a concise handoff.
args.why_useful: The owner can delegate a multi-hour workflow—such as a build, export, download, or research collection—without leaving the Mac unattended blindly. The system makes measurable progress, pauses when judgment is required, and gives the owner a ready-to-resume state instead of a vague failure.
args.model_tier: Background model for planning and checkpoint summaries; realtime only for an actual urgent escalation
args.latency_budget: Start within 2 seconds; checkpoint every 10 minutes or meaningful milestone; morning handoff under 10 seconds
args.cost_estimate: Moderate background inference for milestones; local process observation and storage dominate
args.security_concerns: A delegated task may access authenticated browser sessions and local files. Require a bounded lease, explicit allowed applications/projects, no silent privilege grants, encrypted checkpoints, and automatic expiry at the requested time.
missing: A lease-based autonomous-work supervisor with deadline, scope, pause, and escalation state
Checkpoint format containing completed steps, pending decision, inputs, outputs, and exact resume action
Scheduler integration that survives Mac-agent restart and hands the checkpoint to the relay

args.user_asks: Compare these two authenticated pages and tell me what changed, without exposing either page to the internet.
args.why_useful: The owner can compare two private dashboards, invoices, project views, or account pages using the browser session they already have. The system extracts only the relevant differences locally and speaks a short answer, instead of requiring screenshots, copy-paste, or an external web service.
args.model_tier: Local deterministic DOM/table diff first; background model summarizes ambiguous differences; realtime speaks only the final result
args.latency_budget: First diff within 5 seconds; summary within 10 seconds for ordinary pages
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: local parsing is cheap; one background summary call for irregular layouts
args.security_concerns: Both pages may contain financial or work data. Keep raw DOM and screenshots on the Mac, redact credentials and hidden fields, send only a minimal diff to the model, and bind comparison to the current tab/session identities.
missing: A browser capture API for two selected tabs or snapshots with stable semantic fields and timestamps
Local structured diff engine for tables, amounts, statuses, and changed text, including page-state validation
A relay request schema that carries tab references rather than URLs or page contents

args.user_asks: Pick up the workflow where it stopped, even if the Mac restarted, and show me the one step you will repeat before doing it.
args.why_useful: A crash, sleep, update, or lost USB link should not erase a half-completed multi-app workflow. The owner gets a truthful resume point and can avoid duplicate uploads, messages, purchases, or file mutations while still recovering useful work.
args.model_tier: Background model reconstructs intent from a deterministic action checkpoint; realtime model explains the proposed next step
args.latency_budget: Reconstruct state within 3 seconds after Mac reconnect; resume after the owner’s spoken acknowledgement
args.cost_estimate: Low: checkpoint validation is local; model is used only when the next action is ambiguous
args.security_concerns: A stale browser session or changed page can invalidate a checkpoint. Revalidate tab identity, URL origin, file hashes, and preconditions; refuse to replay a side effect when state differs, and keep secrets out of checkpoints.
missing: Crash-safe per-step checkpoint records shared by /execute, browser commands, and relay jobs
Idempotency keys and postcondition validators for browser and shell side effects
Startup reconciliation that distinguishes completed, interrupted, and unsafe-to-replay steps, then exposes a single resume plan

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

- Overnight bounded delegation with lease, checkpoints, ambiguity pauses, and a morning handoff.
- Private authenticated-page comparison performed locally, with only a minimal diff sent for summarization.
- Crash-safe workflow resume across Mac restarts and USB/browser interruptions, with precondition validation before replaying side effects.

Each includes the missing changes required to make it real.

args.subject: avoid duplicates
args.body: What recent Mac capability proposals should I avoid? I plan USB-first pendant local mode and closed-loop verified action.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: "Do that, and don't tell me it worked until you have checked the result." Then carry out a voice-requested task across my Mac and browser, verify the post-condition independently, and tell me exactly what changed (or what did not).
args.why_useful: Today the system can dispatch actions and report execution, but a successful process is not the same as the owner's goal. This is the single most useful missing behavior: a spoken request becomes a closed loop of intent, execution, independent observation, and honest completion. It can use the authenticated browser session when the Mac alone cannot, and the pendant gets a truthful result rather than a confident guess.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short voice turn and final answer; a cheaper background model performs plan decomposition and evidence comparison. mac-vision/faculty-perception use deterministic checks or a small model before escalating.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 500 ms; execute within the task's natural duration; post-condition verification within 2 s after the last action, with a spoken progress update if longer than 8 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01-$0.08 per ordinary task, dominated by screenshots/browser evidence and any escalation to the expensive model; trivial deterministic checks cost essentially zero.
args.security_concerns: Evidence may include private browser pages and screen pixels, so keep raw captures on the Mac and send only a redacted claim/diff to relay. Never claim success when verification is unavailable; say 'executed but not verified.' Destructive actions still follow the owner's existing maximum-access policy, but the system must report their actual post-state and preserve a recovery hint.
missing: A post-condition DSL that can express checks such as file exists with hash, app state, browser text/URL, or visible UI state
A correlation envelope connecting voice turn, /execute job, browser command, and evidence snapshot
A Mac-side verifier that runs after actions and returns evidence without asking the expensive model to reread the whole screen
A failure response that distinguishes action failure, verification failure, and ambiguous evidence

args.user_asks: "Use the pendant over USB right now, even though it has no LTE, and read me the result."
args.why_useful: The nRF9160 and ESP32 are physically attached to this Mac today, while LTE registration is absent. A USB-first local mode would make the worn device genuinely useful now: button/audio requests can reach the Mac with low latency, and Mac/browser work can return to the pendant without pretending the relay is reachable. It also becomes the field diagnostic path before trusting cellular transport.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic local serial broker and a cheap parser for framing; reserve realtime model inference for the actual spoken request. No cloud model is needed for link negotiation, buffering, or acknowledgements.
args.latency_budget: USB discovery and handshake under 1 s; button-to-Mac dispatch under 300 ms; audio control/status acknowledgement under 500 ms. On disconnect, switch to offline behavior within 1 s and resume queued work after a verified reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost after setup; approximately 1-2 engineering days for serial framing/bridge integration. Existing hardware and USB cables incur no additional cost.
args.security_concerns: Only accept serial devices matching the known VID/PID/serial patterns and bind the bridge to the local authenticated agent. Keep audio and command payloads local unless the owner explicitly invokes cloud inference. Use per-connection nonce and monotonically increasing sequence numbers to reject stale or replayed frames.
missing: A real serial transport implementation for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
A local Mac bridge session that maps pendant frames to /pipeline/audio and /pipeline/events and returns acknowledgements
A framed protocol with CRC, sequence, turn/job IDs, reconnect replay, and capability negotiation
A Mac-side device health/status route exposing USB link, firmware identity, and queue depth

args.user_asks: "Pause this; when I come back, continue from exactly where you stopped and remind me what is still unfinished."
args.why_useful: Long Mac/browser tasks currently have no owner-visible, durable notion of a safe pause point. A resumable handoff would let the owner stop speaking, close the laptop, or lose USB without restarting or duplicating side effects. The pendant can capture the interruption, the relay can retain the task envelope, and the Mac/browser can resume only from a verified checkpoint.
args.model_tier: A cheap background model summarizes checkpoint state and unfinished intent; deterministic code owns checkpointing, idempotency, and resume. Realtime is used only to acknowledge pause/resume and answer the owner's short follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 500 ms when connected; checkpoint durable within 2 s. Resume should begin within 3 s of reconnect, after a quick state comparison; if state diverged, ask one concise clarification instead of replaying blindly.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005-$0.03 per checkpointed task, mostly summary/evidence tokens; local state comparison and persistence are free.
args.security_concerns: Checkpoint records may contain private URLs, filenames, and snippets. Store raw state locally, encrypt or redact relay summaries, and expire abandoned checkpoints. Resume must reject stale job/ledger IDs and require explicit confirmation only where the owner's existing policy says the action itself warrants it—not as a new global gate.
missing: A durable task envelope linking pendant turn ID, Mac job ID, browser command IDs, and ledger step keys
Checkpoint snapshots containing completed side effects, observed post-state, and the next action, written before interruption
A resume endpoint that compares current Mac/browser state to the checkpoint and emits only uncompleted, idempotent steps
Pendant UI/audio wording for paused, resumable, diverged, and expired states

args.change: Add a provenance-preserving shell execution record: before dispatch, store the planner-authored action and the exact rewritten action side by side; execute via a child-process API that records pid, start/finish monotonic timestamps, exit code/signal, cwd, timeout actually used, and a redacted environment fingerprint. On failure, retain bounded raw stderr/stdout plus a machine-readable failure class, and attach the receipt to the parent job and ledger step. Do not gate or restrict commands; this is evidence and recovery only.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the Mac says a task failed, the owner can know whether the command never started, timed out, was killed, or ran and returned an error—and whether a planner rewrite changed what was executed. That makes spoken follow-up ('retry the same thing' or 'undo what changed') reliable instead of guesswork.
args.effort: Medium: replace exec with an argv-capable spawn path where possible while retaining arbitrary shell compatibility, add receipt fields, redaction, and tests for rewrite/timeout/exit-signal cases; then join receipt IDs to job and ledger records.
args.risk: Changing process invocation can alter shell quoting and working-directory behavior. Preserve a compatibility mode and compare command output in tests. Redaction could hide useful diagnostics, so retain hashes/variable names and local-only raw data with bounded size.
args.cost_impact: No model/API cost; modest local disk growth, capped per receipt. Engineering effort several days.
args.latency_impact: Negligible (<10 ms bookkeeping); spawn startup may differ slightly from exec.

args.user_asks: "What changed on my computer and in my browser while I was away, and which of those changes were caused by you?"
args.why_useful: Today activity is fragmented across Mac jobs, browser commands, relay turns, and physical pendant events. The owner cannot obtain a trustworthy, causal after-the-fact account: a log may show that something ran, but not what the screen/account state was before and after, whether the owner or an agent caused it, or which events belong to the same request. A cross-surface change ledger would turn unexplained drift into a concise, evidence-backed answer.
args.model_tier: Collect and correlate events deterministically; use a cheaper background model to summarize the causal timeline. Escalate to realtime only for the owner's spoken question and final concise explanation.
args.latency_budget: Recording is asynchronous and should add under 20 ms to an action. A normal 'while I was away' answer should arrive in 2-5 seconds; large histories can be summarized in the background with a progress indication.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002-$0.03 per query, dominated by summarizing selected diffs rather than replaying raw screenshots. Local event capture and hashing have no API cost.
args.security_concerns: The ledger could expose sensitive URLs, document names, and screen content. Keep raw snapshots on the Mac, encrypt retention, redact secrets and page bodies by default, and return only the minimum evidence needed. The owner must be able to erase a time range. Clearly distinguish owner-originated, agent-originated, browser-extension-originated, and unknown changes.
missing: A durable cross-surface event schema with actor, causal parent, monotonic sequence, wall time, surface, before-state digest, after-state digest, and evidence pointers
Mac filesystem/app/window observers and browser DOM/URL/storage change observers that produce bounded diffs rather than unrestricted screenshots
A relay/pendant turn correlation mechanism that stamps physical button events and spoken requests onto the same causal chain
A query service that reconstructs a causal timeline, detects unexplained changes, and cites local evidence without uploading raw private state

args.user_asks: "Look in the sites I am already signed into, compare the relevant information, and tell me the answer without sending my page or credentials to the cloud."
args.why_useful: The browser is the only node that physically holds authenticated sessions, but the voice agent cannot safely turn those sessions into a private, cited answer. This would let the owner ask about current account-specific information while keeping page contents and credentials on the Mac. It is more useful than a generic browser action because it returns a comparison with source locations and explicitly reports when the local session cannot answer.
args.model_tier: Run DOM extraction, redaction, comparison, and citation generation locally with a small model; use realtime only to interpret the short question and speak the result. Cloud receives intent and a minimal redacted answer, never raw authenticated page content.
args.latency_budget: Answer within 5 seconds for already-open pages; up to 15 seconds when several tabs need inspection. Tell the owner immediately which sites are being checked without exposing their contents.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero cloud cost for local extraction; roughly $0.001-$0.02 for intent parsing and speech-turn handling. Engineering cost is the dominant expense.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated content remains local and is never included in relay prompts. Apply field-level redaction for tokens, payment data, and personal identifiers; cite a local tab title/URL and timestamp rather than uploading excerpts. The owner can require a spoken confirmation before any navigation that changes state, while read-only queries remain hands-free.
missing: A browser-extension command for local structured extraction and field-level redaction, distinct from screenshot inspection
A local comparison worker that can join results from multiple authenticated tabs and attach citations
A privacy contract in the relay protocol carrying only intent, redacted answer, and citation metadata
A policy that marks navigation, downloads, and form submission as mutations so a question cannot silently change the session

args.change: Introduce signed, content-addressed evidence capsules at every surface boundary. A Mac or browser observer emits a small local capsule containing the claim, relevant diff, source locator, timestamp, confidence, and hash of retained raw evidence; relay and models exchange capsule IDs and summaries instead of resending full screenshots, logs, or page text. On request, the Mac materializes the raw evidence locally for inspection. Capsules expire and can be revoked independently.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets quicker, cheaper, more consistent answers about what the system saw and did, without repeatedly shipping private screen contents or making the model reread entire histories. When an answer is disputed, it can point to concrete local evidence rather than an opaque assertion.
args.effort: Medium-to-large protocol and harness change across Mac, browser extension, relay, and faculty perception; requires canonical schemas, signing, local retention, and adapters for existing jobs and inspections.
args.risk: A bad summarizer could omit the one detail that matters, and hashes do not prove semantic correctness. Preserve raw evidence locally, include confidence and coverage, and fall back to a fresh inspection when a capsule is stale, incomplete, or challenged.
args.cost_impact: Reduces repeated context-token spend substantially; small local storage overhead for hashes and bounded diffs. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Usually lowers response latency by avoiding large uploads; first capture may add tens of milliseconds.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves data minimization, but signing keys and local evidence stores become sensitive. Rotate keys, scope access per session, and make expiration/erasure enforceable.
depends_on: A cross-surface actor and causal-parent identity so capsules cannot be confused across jobs or browser sessions.
Local browser structured extraction and Mac post-state observation.
A relay protocol that accepts capsule metadata and fetches raw evidence only through an authenticated local request.

This round produced three new capabilities and one hardware recommendation:

1. **End-to-end 24 kHz audio acceptance test**  
   A spoken “make the audio path pass” command would exercise the physically connected nRF9160, ESP32 bridge, relay codec path, and playback, then report latency, underruns, packet loss, and the exact failing stage.

2. **Pendant-generated bug reports**  
   A failure marker on the pendant would cause the Mac to collect bounded UART traces from both USB devices, redact secrets, join them with pipeline/job receipts, and produce a reproducible issue draft. External filing would still require confirmation.

3. **Cross-node engineering timeline**  
   Pendant turn IDs, bridge events, Mac jobs, receipts, and relay pipeline events would be joined into one causal timeline, so “what happened before the audio stalled?” has an answer rather than requiring manual log archaeology.

4. **Hardware change: separate audio compute from modem/control work**  
   The current prototype spends roughly 87% of one core on simultaneous Opus encode/decode. A product pendant should use a second application core or dedicated audio DSP so the requested 24 kHz path remains reliable while radio, storage, diagnostics, and recovery continue.

What is still missing:

- A bounded Mac serial collector for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- Firmware test mode and counters for deterministic audio stimuli, decode deadlines, underruns, and acknowledgements.
- A relay endpoint to correlate pendant turn IDs, codec events, bridge acknowledgements, and Mac receipts.
- A shared monotonic event envelope so USB, relay, and Mac timestamps can be joined reliably.
- The previously requested `mac_usb_serial_diagnostics` capability remains pending; I did not re-request it.

args.model_tier: background model for test/review orchestration and evidence synthesis; realtime only for short status replies
args.latency_budget: Minutes for tests and browser review; immediate acknowledgement and resumable progress after every stage
args.cost_estimate: $0.05–$0.30 per delivery depending on model review and browser interaction; compute/test time dominates

Relay job status that can resume a delivery after Mac, browser, or LTE interruption

args.user_asks: "Show me where my wearable connection is unreliable, and tell me what to change so conversations stop dropping."

args.latency_budget: Milliseconds for counters; a daily report in under 10 seconds; immediate warning after a repeated failure pattern
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per daily report; local aggregation and retention dominate, not inference

args.user_asks: "When I say 'do this later', hold the whole task until the right machine, browser session, network, and power state are available, then finish it without losing what I meant."

This capability makes deferred intent dependable across the wearable, sleeping relay, Mac, and browser instead of forcing the owner to restate it.
args.model_tier: background model evaluates conditions and plans resumptions; realtime model only captures the intent and reports state
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to persist the intent; execution begins within one polling interval after all predicates become true
args.cost_estimate: <$0.03 per deferred task; most invocations are deterministic predicate checks
args.security_concerns: Conditions and task payloads may contain private URLs, files, or credentials. Encrypt the payload at rest, keep browser secrets inside the extension, expire stale intents, and require confirmation immediately before irreversible actions.
missing: A durable conditional-intent schema with expiry, dependencies, and exactly-once completion semantics
Pendant storage for the owner’s original intent and a concise local queued state

args.user_asks: When I tell you to do something on my Mac, make it finish even if the local agent or laptop restarts; if it cannot safely resume, tell me exactly where it stopped on the pendant.
args.why_useful: Today a long shell or browser job can remain falsely 'processing' after a restart, and the durable ledger is never automatically reconciled or resumed. This gives the owner one reliable mental model: a request is either completed, explicitly paused at a named step, or failed with evidence—not silently lost.
args.model_tier: background for reconciliation and resume planning; realtime only for the short spoken status and the owner's follow-up
args.latency_budget: Immediate dispatch acknowledgement under 1 s; restart recovery within 5 s of the Mac agent boot; spoken final status under 2 s after each resumed step
args.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap planner call only when a step failed or needs re-planning; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per recovery, dominated by model reasoning rather than storage or polling
args.security_concerns: The agent retains the owner's deliberate FULL_CONTROL_MODE and does not add approval gates. Resume must require an idempotency key and replaySafety check, never blindly repeat non-reversible shell/file/browser mutations. The relay receives command labels, step state, and bounded error text; redact stdout/stderr secrets before sending to the pendant.
missing: boot-time reconciliation that marks processing jobs interrupted
closing the orchestrator ledger on every terminal path
a durable jobId-to-ledgerId link in planMeta
step-level idempotency/replay decisions wired into /execute
a resume worker that submits only safe runnable steps
pendant delivery of paused/resumed state over the existing status beacon

args.user_asks: What changed because of that last request? Give me a short spoken answer, and let me inspect the exact evidence on my Mac.
args.why_useful: A success boolean is not enough for an unattended shell/browser action. The owner needs a human answer (which files, apps, tabs, and external effects changed) plus a durable evidence bundle when something surprising happens. This correlates the Mac receipt with the browser inspection and the pendant turn instead of making the owner reconstruct it from logs.
args.model_tier: cheap background summarizer over structured diffs; realtime only to speak the result and answer a follow-up
args.latency_budget: Collect pre/post snapshots opportunistically; final summary in under 3 s for a normal action, with a dashboard evidence card available within 10 s
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for collection; about $0.001–$0.005 for a structured diff summary, dominated by model tokens when stdout or browser state is large
args.security_concerns: Never upload raw environment variables, cookies, page bodies, or unrestricted stdout. Store sensitive evidence locally with a short retention period, send only redacted paths, app/tab titles, hashes, exit status, and explicitly requested excerpts. No new confirmation gate is required under the owner's policy.
missing: pre/post snapshots tied to one request across filesystem/git, running app, and browser tab state
a receipt schema containing real exit code, pid, argv, effective cwd, timeout, and output hashes
redaction and retention rules for evidence bundles
a dashboard route to open the evidence bundle from a spoken result

args.user_asks: Stop the thing you are doing on my Mac right now when I say 'stop' or press the pendant's cancel control, and tell me whether it actually stopped.
args.why_useful: The current cancel endpoint only sets an AbortController; a running shell can continue for its full 120-second timeout, and computer-use work is not cancellable in production. A real stop path prevents an accidental long-running command, gives the owner immediate control from the wearable, and never falsely reports cancellation.
args.model_tier: No model needed for the kill and acknowledgement; use the cheap tier only to summarize the terminated step and decide whether a later resume is safe
args.latency_budget: Pendant intent acknowledged locally in under 100 ms; relay dispatch under 500 ms; child process group terminated and confirmed within 2 s; if confirmation fails, report 'stop requested, still running' rather than success
args.cost_estimate: No per-request model cost for the control path; modest Mac engineering work for process-group tracking and one status event
args.security_concerns: The cancel token must be bound to the active owner session/job, reject stale job IDs, and kill only the recorded process group. It must not delete files or undo completed effects. Browser cancellation should stop the current automation loop but cannot rewind a submitted web action. Send only job ID, step label, and terminal status to the pendant.
missing: run_shell execution with AbortSignal and process-group/child PID capture
computer-use loop cancellation wired by every production caller
a terminal-state handshake from Mac to relay rather than optimistic cancellation
a dedicated pendant cancel intent using the existing second button and outbox/status-beacon machinery
post-cancel classification of completed, interrupted, or unknown side effects

args.change: Instrument every run_shell action with a truthful execution envelope: invoke through a process API that records argv (while preserving the owner's unrestricted command capability), effective cwd, start/finish monotonic timestamps, pid/process-group, timeout, signal, numeric exit code, stdout/stderr byte counts and hashes, and a redacted environment fingerprint. Record the original submitted action and any silent rewrite separately, then link the envelope to jobId, ledgerId, and receiptId. Make cancellation send the signal to the process group and settle the receipt only after reaping or explicitly marking the process unknown.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the agent says a command failed, stopped, or changed something, the owner can trust exactly what happened and recover without guessing. It also makes the pendant's running/completed/failed beacon truthful instead of merely reflecting a request flag.
args.effort: Medium: computerControl executor, actionReceipts, jobTracker, ledger close paths, and boot reconciliation; add a small local evidence viewer rather than a new model.
args.risk: Changing exec plumbing can break shell semantics, especially pipelines and shell built-ins. Preserve a compatibility mode using /bin/sh -c but still capture the spawned shell's pid/group; test rewrites and timeout behavior. If telemetry fails, execution should continue but mark the receipt incomplete.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage (roughly 1–4 KB per action plus bounded output metadata); no extra model calls. Periodic pruning is needed for the existing 120-job/1 MiB stores.
args.latency_impact: Under 20 ms bookkeeping overhead per action; cancellation becomes faster and deterministic instead of waiting up to 120 s.
args.security_impact: No gates or reduction of FULL_CONTROL_MODE. Do not persist raw env or secrets; hash variable names/values after redaction. Treat command strings, paths, and output as sensitive local data with bounded retention.
depends_on: A reliable jobId-to-ledgerId association
orchestrator calling closeLedger on all terminal paths
process-group tracking in run_shell
boot-time reconciliation of processing jobs
