args.why_useful: A wearable that speaks whenever a Mac job or browser watch changes is actively disruptive. The Mac knows the foreground meeting/presentation state, the browser knows which session generated the event, the relay can rank urgency, and the pendant can defer audio without losing the event. No single node can make that decision reliably.
args.model_tier: Deterministic local policy for detecting presentation/call state and queueing; background model only for digest grouping; realtime reserved for an actually urgent alert
args.latency_budget: Enter quiet mode within 1 s of the Mac entering a call/presentation app; urgent alert under 2 s; digest within 5 s of leaving quiet mode
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for state detection and queueing; under $0.005 for an occasional grouped digest, dominated by summarization and speech
args.security_concerns: Keep meeting titles, browser URLs, and event text local by default; send only urgency class and a redacted digest to the relay. The owner explicitly opts into which events count as urgent. Never infer or announce private call content.
missing: Mac foreground-app and call/presentation detection exposed as a signed event stream
a relay-side per-owner quiet-mode policy with urgency classes and expiry
browser events carrying source/session and urgency metadata
pendant deferred-audio inbox with an explicit 'quiet but not lost' state
dashboard controls to inspect, reprioritize, or discard queued notifications

args.user_asks: Before I send this, check the open browser draft and any attached Mac files for secrets, private data, wrong recipients, and mismatched numbers; give me a spoken risk summary and leave the draft untouched.
args.why_useful: Today the browser can hold the authenticated draft and the Mac can hold the source files, but neither can reliably compare them and explain accidental disclosure before submission. This is a genuinely cross-surface preflight: it prevents a costly send without taking ownership of the final send action.
args.model_tier: Background model over locally extracted text and structured recipient/file metadata; realtime only for the short result
args.latency_budget: Under 10 s for a normal draft plus up to five local attachments; immediately report which attachment or page could not be inspected
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per preflight depending on attachment text and OCR volume; local extraction dominates latency, model tokens dominate API cost
args.security_concerns: This processes highly sensitive drafts and files. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser bridge, pass only encrypted bounded excerpts or local findings to the model, redact credentials and financial identifiers, retain no copy after the result, and never mutate or submit the draft. The owner remains the final sender.
missing: a browser route that extracts the current draft, recipients, and attachment references without submitting
a Mac-local attachment reader and secret/PII detector
cross-source numeric and recipient consistency checks
a privacy-preserving analysis contract with deletion/retention guarantees
a pendant response that can state 'not inspected' rather than implying safety

args.user_asks: After any task, tell me exactly what left my Mac or browser session, which model or service saw it, and let me erase the local record without undoing the work.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has no plain-language data-egress account across shell output, browser pages, relay events, and model context. A privacy receipt makes the hive trustworthy: useful work can remain unrestricted, while the owner can see whether a page, file excerpt, URL, or secret crossed a boundary.
args.model_tier: Deterministic egress classification and local accounting; no model needed except an optional cheap natural-language summary
args.latency_budget: Receipt generated alongside each event with under 100 ms overhead; spoken summary under 2 s on request; deletion action acknowledged immediately and completed within 5 s
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero compute and model cost; bounded local metadata storage, with optional $0.001 summary
args.security_concerns: The receipt itself is sensitive and must never contain the secret it describes. Store content hashes, data classes, destination, purpose, and retention—not raw tokens or page bodies. Deletion must erase local receipt payloads without pretending remote services forgot data; the pendant must say when deletion cannot be verified.
missing: a shared data-classification vocabulary across Mac, browser, relay, and model calls
egress hooks around shell stdout, browser inspection/results, pipeline audio/events, and prompt assembly
a local append-only privacy receipt with bounded retention and verified deletion
a dashboard and pendant query for per-task egress summaries
explicit remote-retention disclosures from each model/service

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Quiet-mode urgency management** — suppress non-urgent pendant notifications during calls or presentations, then provide a digest afterward.
2. **Pre-send privacy and consistency check** — inspect an authenticated browser draft and Mac attachments for secrets, recipient errors, private data, and mismatched figures without changing or sending anything.
3. **Cross-system privacy receipts** — report what data left the Mac or browser, which model/service received it, and what local records can be deleted.

args.user_asks: “Run this command on my Mac, and if it fails, diagnose it and try the safest repair automatically; tell me exactly what changed.”
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell step loses its exit code, has no automatic retry, and leaves the owner to restate the task. This would turn the Mac from a fire-and-forget executor into a dependable operator: capture the real exit status and bounded output, have a cheaper background model classify the failure, retry only idempotent repairs, and speak the final result through the pendant.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the owner's short request and final spoken answer; background/cheap model for failure classification and repair-plan generation; no expensive model on routine retries.
args.latency_budget: First command starts immediately (<1 s after relay dispatch). On failure, diagnosis and one repair attempt within 10–30 s; pendant says 'still working' locally rather than holding the voice turn open.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one realtime turn plus 1–2 cheap classification calls; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per failure, dominated by model context and any shell output sent off-device.
args.security_concerns: The Mac remains maximum-access as the owner requires. Full stdout/stderr and environment must not be uploaded; redact secrets and send only exit code, signal, bounded tail, cwd, and a command fingerprint. Automatic repair must be restricted to a generated plan whose effects are shown in the durable receipt; destructive or network-side repairs require an explicit owner request. Pendant should announce whether the repair actually ran.
missing: execFile/spawn-based shell runner that records exit code, signal, pid, argv, start/finish/duration, and bounded stdout/stderr
failure classifier and idempotency/repair planner
job retry endpoint with exactly-once action identity and a durable parent-child job link
pendant result protocol for intermediate retry state and final receipt

args.user_asks: “Take the table or list on the authenticated page I’m looking at, turn it into a local CSV/Markdown file, and put the result in my project.”
args.why_useful: The browser is the only node that can read sessions the Mac shell cannot access, while the Mac is the only node that can create and manipulate a useful local artifact. This closes a daily gap without copying credentials or requiring the owner to manually download, clean, and rename data.
args.model_tier: Realtime only to resolve the owner's target and destination; a cheap background model extracts/normalizes the already-captured table and validates row/column counts. Use no expensive model for file writing.
args.latency_budget: Capture in 2 s, write and validate in under 10 s for ordinary pages; speak a short completion plus path. If the page is paginated, continue in background and report progress through the pendant beacon.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per invocation; extraction tokens dominate, and the browser page text can be reduced to a table capsule before model use.
args.security_concerns: Keep page contents on the Mac/relay boundary and never send cookies or DOM scripts to a cloud model. Require the owner to name or confirm the destination when ambiguous. Write atomically to a new file, preserve the source URL/time and row count, and never overwrite an existing artifact silently.
missing: browser action to extract structured table with provenance and pagination cursor
Mac action to atomically create a validated artifact from that capsule
relay correlation that binds browser commandId, local jobId, and output receipt
spoken error when a page changes or pagination cannot be completed

args.user_asks: “Even with no LTE or relay connection, let the pendant control my Mac over its USB cable: press the button to pause/resume the current job, and tell me locally whether it worked.”
args.why_useful: The hardware is physically attached today but unregistered with the relay, so the most immediate useful path is currently unavailable by design. A local USB control plane gives the owner a dependable emergency and pause control in airplane mode, during relay outages, or while developing firmware—without pretending a cloud command completed.
args.model_tier: No model for the button edge, serial framing, job lookup, or pause signal. Realtime is used only if the owner asks a spoken follow-up after reconnection.
args.latency_budget: Button-to-Mac acknowledgement under 150 ms over USB; LED/local tone under 250 ms. Reconciliation with relay occurs asynchronously when connectivity returns.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; one serial protocol and a small local daemon. Main cost is engineering and testing crash/reconnect cases.
args.security_concerns: Bind commands to the physical USB device identity and a per-installation challenge key; never accept arbitrary shell text over serial. Only expose pause/resume/abort of jobs previously created by this owner, reject stale sequence numbers, and persist an acknowledgement with job ID, old state, new state, and monotonic counter. Do not claim pause if the child process cannot actually be signalled.
missing: nRF9160 USB-serial control framing and persistent sequence/ack record
Mac local-agent serial listener for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*
real process-group pause/resume/cancel semantics in run_shell and computer-use jobs
relay reconciliation that merges locally acknowledged controls without replaying them

args.user_asks: “What did I change today, and where? Give me a trustworthy spoken summary with links or file paths.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has separate job history, browser provenance, action receipts, and pendant events, but no cross-surface timeline. A single answer would cover edits made by shell, browser, and local actions, distinguish observed from executed, and let the owner recover an exact artifact or page instead of relying on memory.
args.model_tier: Cheap background indexer builds normalized event records and hashes; realtime model only summarizes the already-filtered time window when asked. Use deterministic joins for job IDs, receipt IDs, URLs, and paths rather than spending model tokens on bookkeeping.
args.latency_budget: Incremental indexing costs under 1 s per completed job; a spoken daily summary should return in under 3 s from the local index. Detailed provenance can open in the dashboard afterward.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero per event; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per spoken query depending on event count. Storage is a bounded local SQLite/JSON index, not cloud transcript retention.
args.security_concerns: Keep raw command strings, page text, and file names local; expose only redacted summaries and exact links/paths requested by the owner. Mark every item as executed, observed, proposed, or failed, and include source timestamps. Do not infer a file changed from a plan or browser observation. Permit deletion by date and avoid indexing secrets in environment variables or page bodies.
missing: append-only normalized event index joining jobId, actionId, receiptId, browser commandId, pendant turn ID, and file/path hashes
instrumentation for shell exit/signal and file before/after metadata
browser provenance events for navigation/read/write and resulting URL
query route that returns a bounded, redacted change set to relay and dashboard

transcript.text:
Round 176 produced three new, recorded capabilities:

1. **Authenticated page → local artifact**  
   Extract a table from the current Safari session, validate it, and write CSV/Markdown into the active Mac project with provenance and row counts.

2. **USB-tethered pendant control**  
   While LTE/relay is unavailable, the physically connected pendant can pause/resume/abort an existing Mac job over USB, with truthful local acknowledgement and stale-command rejection.

3. **Cross-surface “what did I change today?”**  
   Join Mac jobs, shell/file receipts, browser activity, pipeline events, and pendant turns into a redacted, trustworthy spoken timeline with exact paths and URLs.

Discovery confirms Safari has nine online tabs and `home-macbook-bridge` is online. The pendant remains physically testable over USB but is not relay-registered. The granted `mac_read_diagnostics` schema still does not resolve as a live tool, despite `/machine-context` and `/health` working through HTTP.

What is still needed is implementation rather than another wrapper:

- A structured browser table-extraction result with pagination/provenance.
- An atomic Mac artifact writer and browser-command/job/receipt correlation.
- A USB serial listener for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*`, with authenticated sequence-numbered control frames.
- Real process-group pause/resume/cancel semantics; current cancellation is cooperative and does not stop a running shell child.
- Durable cross-surface event indexing, including shell exit status, signal, PID, and file before/after hashes.
- A bounded, redacted timeline query for relay voice responses and dashboard display.

One proposal collided with an existing failure-recovery capability, so I did not restate it.

args.user_asks: “Keep working on this project while I’m away: use my authenticated browser and Mac files, make only progress that is reversible, stop at the first ambiguity, and leave me a spoken morning handoff with exactly what changed and what needs me.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner can delegate a task or run a routine, but cannot safely leave a multi-surface project in progress across sleep, relay restarts, browser-session changes, and Mac disconnects. This would be a true resumable work session: the browser supplies authenticated context, the Mac edits local artifacts, the relay remains the durable coordinator, and the pendant reports blockers rather than fabricating completion.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for step selection, checkpoint compression, and routine progress checks. Use realtime only when the owner starts the task, resolves an ambiguity, or requests the spoken handoff. Escalate to the expensive tier only for genuinely ambiguous decisions.
args.latency_budget: A task may run for hours with no conversational connection. Each individual step should begin within 5 s of its predecessor; reconnecting should yield a concise state summary within 2 s. The morning handoff should be generated from checkpoints, not replay the entire transcript.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.20 per multi-hour task depending on page volume and number of decisions; browser extraction and model context dominate. Deterministic file operations and checkpointing should cost no inference tokens.
args.security_concerns: The owner explicitly authorizes the project scope at start, but the system must never broaden it. Keep authenticated page content and local files on-device whenever possible. Every step needs a before/after capsule, reversibility classification, source URL/path, and checkpoint ID. Stop on permission prompts, destructive operations, changed page structure, conflicting edits, or uncertain recipient/destination. The pendant must say “stopped for your decision,” never “done,” when the relay or Mac disappears.
missing: durable cross-surface workflow state machine with checkpoint, lease, pause, resume, and stop-on-ambiguity semantics
exactly-once step identity spanning browser command IDs, Mac job IDs, action receipts, and relay retries
reversible local artifact transactions and browser undo/rollback metadata
heartbeat and ownership handoff across relay restart, browser disconnect, and Mac sleep
morning handoff generator that distinguishes completed, attempted, blocked, and unverified work
pendant protocol for queued, checkpointed, blocked, and resumed states

args.user_asks: “Compare the number or status in this authenticated web portal with the matching local file, and tell me which source is stale—without changing either one.”
args.why_useful: The browser can see private portal state and the Mac can inspect local project files, but today they are separate observations. The owner needs a trustworthy discrepancy answer before acting: identify matching records, show both timestamps and evidence, explain the conflict, and leave all sources untouched.
args.model_tier: Cheap model or deterministic parsers perform normalization, key matching, timestamp comparison, and arithmetic. Realtime is only for the final spoken explanation when the owner asks.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 s for ordinary pages and files; paginate or parse larger sources in the background while reporting that comparison is incomplete rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: $0.001–$0.02 per comparison; model cost is dominated by irregular table normalization. Most structured CSV/JSON comparisons should be local and effectively free.
args.security_concerns: Do not upload portal credentials, cookies, or full private documents. Return minimal evidence slices, source URLs/paths, observed timestamps, and confidence. Treat absence and stale data as distinct states; never update either source unless the owner explicitly asks afterward.
missing: shared comparison request with source selectors and matching-key hints
browser structured extraction plus local file parser with common provenance format
deterministic diff engine for values, timestamps, and missing records
spoken evidence capsule that can be reopened in the dashboard

args.user_asks: “Watch this portal page and the corresponding local file together. If either changes in a way that affects the other, alert me on the pendant with the exact conflict; otherwise stay quiet.”
args.why_useful: A browser watch alone cannot know whether a local draft has become stale, and a file watch alone cannot interpret the authenticated source. Coupling both lets the owner work normally while receiving only actionable cross-source conflicts instead of noisy page or filesystem notifications.
args.model_tier: Deterministic hashes, field extraction, and debounce first; a cheap background model interprets only changed fields. Realtime is not used for monitoring, only for the owner's follow-up question or spoken alert phrasing.
args.latency_budget: Detect ordinary changes within 30 s, with a quiet-period debounce of 5–10 s. Alert audio should begin within 2 s of a confirmed conflict; suppress repeated alerts until the owner acknowledges or the conflict changes.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for hashes and structured fields; approximately $0.001–$0.02 per meaningful change requiring interpretation. The dominant cost is extracting changed authenticated page content.
args.security_concerns: Store only selected fields, hashes, URLs, paths, and timestamps—not continuous page text or file contents. Require explicit pairing of a page and file and an expiry time. Never auto-edit either source. Include confidence and evidence snippets in every alert, and mark monitoring as paused when browser authentication or the Mac disappears.
missing: paired browser/page-watch and local-file-watch subscription model
field-level normalization and change correlation with debounce/deduplication
relay notification policy that routes only actionable conflicts to the pendant
expiry, pause, and owner-acknowledgement state persisted across reconnects

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Resumable, stop-on-ambiguity project work** across authenticated browser sessions, Mac files, relay restarts, and pendant handoffs.
- **Cross-source discrepancy checking** between a private portal and local files without modifying either.
- **Paired browser/file monitoring** that alerts only when a meaningful change creates a conflict.

They require durable workflow checkpoints, exactly-once cross-surface IDs, structured browser and file provenance, field-level diffing, restart/reconnect leases, and pendant states for blocked/resumed work. None should claim completion when the browser, Mac, or relay disappears.

args.user_asks: When I say “take care of this” into the pendant, have the system finish the task across my Mac and logged-in browser, then tell me exactly what changed and leave me a one-command way to undo or resume it if anything failed.
args.why_useful: Today the voice, browser, and Mac surfaces can each act, but the owner has to manually bridge them and cannot tell whether a partial result is safe. This makes the whole hive behave like one accountable assistant: inspect the active tab and project, execute the smallest complete workflow, produce evidence, and preserve a resumable recovery point.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic routing for status, tab listing, and receipts; use the background/planner tier for decomposition and verification; reserve realtime only for the short spoken acknowledgment and final result.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; gather context in 2 seconds; ordinary workflows under 20 seconds, with a spoken progress update at 5 seconds. Long jobs continue asynchronously and are queryable from the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one planner call plus deterministic Mac/browser actions; roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on verification context. The dominant cost is sending page/project context, so send only selected DOM/text and receipt summaries.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page text and local file paths may leave the Mac for planning; redact tokens, cookies, and unrelated tabs. Mutations remain allowed under the owner's maximum-access policy, but the spoken result must distinguish completed, partially completed, and merely proposed. Undo/resume must be explicit and idempotent.
missing: A cross-surface transaction envelope joining one pendant turn, browser command IDs, Mac job IDs, and action-ledger receipts
A verifier that compares intended effects with observed post-state before claiming completion
A durable resume/undo bundle exposed as a single owner-facing job

args.user_asks: If a terminal task fails, let me ask the pendant “why did that fail?” and get a useful diagnosis plus a safe, ready-to-run recovery—not just “exit 1.” Include the exact command, project directory, duration, exit code, relevant stderr, and what the agent would try next.
args.why_useful: The current Mac shell flattens failures, discards the exit code, has no argv or environment fingerprint, and cancellation cannot stop a running child. The owner currently has to reproduce failures manually. A forensic answer would turn a dead-end command into a recoverable action while preserving the owner's deliberate full-control policy.
args.model_tier: Deterministic collection and classification first; a cheap background model summarizes stderr and proposes recovery; realtime only speaks the concise diagnosis. Escalate to planner only when multiple recovery branches or project context are needed.
args.latency_budget: Return the first diagnosis within 3 seconds of asking; recovery proposal within 8 seconds. Never rerun automatically merely because diagnosis is available; keep a long-running repair asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for receipt lookup and known exit-code classes; about $0.002–$0.01 for summarizing a bounded stderr excerpt. Cost is dominated by sending logs, so cap and redact output.
args.security_concerns: Commands and stderr can contain secrets, paths, and credentials. Store a redacted forensic capsule, never the inherited environment; preserve a local hash and allow the owner to request raw output. Recovery commands inherit maximum access and must be clearly labeled as a new mutation, not an automatic retry.
missing: Shell execution receipts with exit code, signal, pid, argv/cwd, timeout-vs-process-exit distinction, and redacted environment fingerprint
A failure taxonomy (nonzero exit, timeout, signal, output overflow, cancellation) and recovery planner that knows which failures are retryable
A pendant query that binds to the last failed Mac job and streams its diagnosis

args.user_asks: Take the document I’m looking at in Safari, extract the useful fields, and file it on my Mac where it belongs—without uploading it anywhere else. Tell me which tab and file you used, what you extracted, and show me the destination before/after when I ask from the pendant.
args.why_useful: This is a genuinely cross-node job: only the browser has the authenticated document, only the Mac can manipulate the local filesystem, and only the pendant gives the owner a hands-free request and trustworthy completion signal. It eliminates download-find-open-copy-rename bookkeeping while keeping sensitive documents local after capture.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic browser inspection/download and local file operations; use a background model for field extraction and destination classification; use realtime only for the spoken confirmation. Use vision only when the page is rendered and text extraction is insufficient.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second, identify the active document within 3 seconds, and finish ordinary PDFs/images within 15 seconds. If a login challenge or ambiguous destination occurs, pause with a precise question rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per document, mostly extraction/verification tokens; local file transfer and hashing are free. Keep the document bytes on the Mac and send only schema-limited extracted fields to the planner.
args.security_concerns: The browser session may expose financial, medical, or work documents. Require origin/tab provenance, same-device transfer, MIME/size limits, malware scan, secret/PII redaction in model context, and an audit record of source hash, destination, and transformation. Never claim success until destination hash and readable file state verify.
missing: A browser command that transfers a download or selected document bytes to the Mac agent without routing content through the relay/model
A local extraction and file-placement action with SHA-256 provenance, collision handling, and atomic write
A cross-surface privacy contract that restricts planner context to extracted fields while retaining full bytes locally

args.change: Instrument run_shell at the child-process boundary with spawn/execFile-style metadata while preserving the raw command capability: capture pid, normalized cwd, start/finish monotonic times, timeout and signal cause, numeric exit code, bounded stdout/stderr digests, and a redacted environment fingerprint. Persist the raw submitted action and any pre-dispatch rewrite beside the executed action, link the receipt to its job and ledger IDs, pass AbortSignal to the child, and reconcile processing jobs on boot as interrupted rather than leaving them permanently running.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks what happened, the system can answer truthfully, stop a hung command, and resume or diagnose work after the Mac agent restarts. It makes maximum access more useful rather than restricting it: every command remains possible, but failures and partial completion stop being mysteries.
args.effort: Medium-high: replace exec with a signal-aware child process wrapper, extend receipt/job schemas and redaction, close ledgers on all orchestrator paths, add boot reconciliation, and test timeout/cancel/restart/rewritten-action cases.
args.risk: Changing process execution can alter shell quoting, signal behavior, and output timing. Roll back behind a feature flag to the existing exec path; keep the original command string and result so a failed migration is diagnosable.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and CPU for metadata/hashes; no additional model call. Bounded output retention may reduce disk pressure compared with current unbounded result strings.
args.latency_impact: Under 10 ms instrumentation overhead; cancellation becomes effective during a command instead of waiting up to 120 seconds.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding gates. Redact environment values and sensitive output, retain only names/fingerprints by default, and ensure AGENT_TOKEN/LLM keys never enter receipts.
depends_on: A schema migration for action receipts and job records
A tested child-process wrapper that preserves /bin/sh command semantics
Ledger close and job-to-ledger correlation in orchestrator.js

args.name: browser_export_local_artifact
args.why: The browser extension is the only node that can access an authenticated document, while the Mac agent is the only node that can safely place and process the bytes locally. Existing browser actions expose tabs/pages and command results but do not provide a same-device, provenance-preserving artifact transfer.
args.why_existing_tools_insufficient: browser_run_actions and POST /browser/result can inspect pages and report results, but no discovered route transfers selected/downloaded bytes to a local Mac path with source hash, MIME, and size limits. mac_run_actions can manipulate local paths only after the artifact exists.
args.expected_output: A receipt containing command_id, source tab URL/title and origin, destination path, byte count, MIME type, SHA-256, startedAt/finishedAt, and whether the transfer was atomic and same-host without relay upload. Fail closed on size/type mismatch or stale tab.

result.note: Queued for the orchestrator. If it is granted, it will be resolved against the running system when you call it — real and read-only means it runs, anything else means you get a description or a refusal with the nearest real capabilities. Carry on with what you already have and do not wait on this.

args.finding: The Mac agent, relay, and Safari extension are online simultaneously; Safari has 9 tabs with active X tab and authenticated Gmail tab, and Accessibility, Screen Recording, and automation permissions are all granted.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status and GET /browser/status returned online=true, browser tabCount=9, relay.macBridgeOnline=true, permissions.ready=true.

transcript.text:
Round 177 produced three capabilities and one Mac harness change:

1. **Cross-surface “take care of this” workflows**  
   The pendant can delegate a task spanning the active Safari tab and Mac project, then report exactly what changed with resume/undo information.

2. **Truthful shell failure diagnosis**  
   Asking “why did that fail?” would return the actual command, project directory, duration, exit code, stderr, timeout/signal cause, and a recovery proposal instead of a flattened “exit 1.”

3. **Authenticated browser document → local Mac filing**  
   The system could take a document from the active Safari session, extract fields, file it locally, and verify source/destination hashes without uploading the document to the relay.

4. **Mac shell execution envelope**  
   I proposed recording process metadata, exit codes, signals, timeout causes, redacted environment fingerprints, rewritten-vs-submitted commands, job/ledger links, effective cancellation, and boot-time interrupted-job reconciliation—without reducing the owner’s unrestricted shell access.

I also requested a new read-only capability, `browser_export_local_artifact`, for same-device transfer of authenticated browser downloads to a Mac path with MIME, size, provenance, and SHA-256 verification.

What I still need is that artifact-transfer capability and the underlying execution-receipt work. The Mac, relay, and Safari extension are currently online together, so the cross-node workflows are testable now.

args.user_asks: Let me give the pendant a bounded delegation such as “until Friday, watch my authenticated work tabs, keep a private queue of items that need me, and stop immediately when I say revoke that delegation.” Show me what it is allowed to do, let me revoke it from anywhere, and give me a daily spoken exception report rather than narrating every routine action.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently leave a multi-day, browser-authenticated objective running with an explicit scope, expiry, live revocation, and accountable exception queue. Existing routines can schedule work, but they do not create a revocable delegation spanning browser sessions, Mac execution, relay wakefulness, and a wearable control surface.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for scheduled polling and exception ranking; deterministic rules enforce scope, expiry, and revocation; use realtime only for the owner's revoke command and the short daily report. Escalate to the planner only for ambiguous items.
args.latency_budget: Revoke acknowledgement under 2 seconds when the relay is reachable and under 1 minute after a reconnect. Daily report under 30 seconds. Polling must be asynchronous and never hold a voice session open.
args.cost_estimate: Low recurring cost: deterministic page checks dominate, with one small background summarization call per report. A typical workday should cost roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on page volume; transmit only changed snippets and hashes.
args.security_concerns: This operates inside authenticated browser sessions and may see confidential work. The delegation needs an explicit allowlist of origins, actions, data fields, and destination folders; a hard expiry; a revocation record replicated to relay, Mac, and pendant; and a guarantee that no outbound message or irreversible mutation is sent without a separately granted capability. All observations should remain local unless the owner opts into relay summarization.
missing: A first-class delegation object with scope, origin/action allowlists, expiry, purpose, and revocation epoch
A relay-backed revocation fanout that reaches browser and Mac workers even while a poll is active
An exception queue that correlates browser observations, Mac jobs, and pendant reports without treating routine polling as a voice conversation

args.user_asks: Before I let you change anything across my Mac and logged-in browser, let me ask “what happens if you do that?” and hear a concrete impact preview: files, tabs, messages, and irreversible side effects, with a replayable simulation that uses the same inputs but performs no writes.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must trust a planner’s prose or inspect scattered previews. A cross-surface dry run would make powerful automation understandable before it acts, especially when one request spans an authenticated tab and local files. It is not an approval gate: the owner can still choose maximum-access execution, but gets a factual diff and explicit side-effect inventory first.
args.model_tier: Run deterministic read-only inspection and filesystem/browser snapshotting first; use a background planner to explain the resulting diff; realtime speaks only the compact impact summary. Do not invoke the expensive tier unless the simulation is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: For ordinary workflows, preview within 5 seconds and execution can begin immediately afterward if requested. Large projects or pages may continue asynchronously, with the pendant stating exactly which inputs remain uninspected.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model call for the raw diff and one small explanation call, around $0.002–$0.02. Store hashes and structural summaries rather than duplicating file or page contents.
args.security_concerns: Simulation must not trigger downloads, network writes, form submissions, clipboard changes, or shell side effects. Authenticated content stays on-device by default. The preview must disclose uncertainty, stale snapshots, hidden scripts, and any action that cannot be faithfully simulated.
missing: A universal dry-run contract for Mac, browser, shell, and computer-use actions that returns predicted effects and confidence
Snapshot isolation and diffing for browser state plus local files, including a freshness/version check immediately before execution
A receipt that binds the preview input hashes to the later real execution so the owner knows whether the world changed between them

args.user_asks: When I say “private mode” into the pendant, keep doing the task but stop speaking names, message contents, and sensitive page text aloud; give me only neutral progress tones and coded summaries until I say “normal mode.” Apply it consistently to the pendant, Mac notifications, browser overlays, and dashboard.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot safely use the system in a meeting, on transit, or around another person because privacy is currently a per-surface guess. A single wearable command should change disclosure policy everywhere while preserving task execution and truthful completion/failure signals.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy propagation and redaction; no model call for mode changes. Background summarization may continue only over already-authorized local data, producing a redacted exception digest. Realtime is limited to neutral confirmations.
args.latency_budget: Mode change acknowledgement under 500 ms locally and under 2 seconds across the relay. Every surface must converge within 3 seconds; stale surfaces must fail closed to neutral output.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; local redaction and policy fanout dominate. A small persistent state record is cheaper than repeatedly sending privacy instructions in prompts.
args.security_concerns: Privacy mode must be enforced below model prompting so a model cannot accidentally reveal sensitive text. Redact TTS, logs, overlays, browser command results, and dashboard previews; preserve encrypted local records for later owner review. The pendant needs an offline cached mode and age indicator so it never claims remote enforcement when disconnected.
missing: A signed privacy-policy epoch propagated from pendant through relay to Mac, browser, and dashboard
Central redaction middleware covering TTS, logs, overlays, browser results, and spoken job receipts
An offline-safe pendant state machine that distinguishes locally active privacy mode from remotely acknowledged mode

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities the owner cannot have today:

- **Bounded, revocable multi-day delegation** across authenticated browser sessions, Mac work, relay scheduling, and pendant control, with explicit scope, expiry, live revocation, and exception-only reports.
- **Cross-surface impact simulation** that previews files, tabs, messages, and irreversible effects before execution, using snapshot hashes to prove whether the real execution matched the preview.
- **Global private mode** activated from the pendant, suppressing sensitive speech, overlays, notifications, browser results, and dashboard content across every surface while preserving neutral progress and failure signals.

They require, respectively:

- A first-class delegation object and relay-wide revocation epoch.
- A universal dry-run contract, isolated browser/filesystem snapshots, and preview-to-execution hash binding.
- Signed privacy-policy propagation, enforcement below the model layer, centralized redaction, and an offline pendant privacy state.

args.subject: Novel cross-node ideas
args.body: Round 178: any recent proposals to avoid duplicating? I need 3 ambitious Mac-centric capabilities beyond observability/recovery.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: Take the result of the last terminal command, put the relevant value into the form currently open in Safari, and tell me exactly what you filled.
args.why_useful: This is a genuine handoff between two private contexts: the Mac shell has local files/commands, while Safari has authenticated sessions. Today the owner must copy values manually and risk putting the wrong output in the wrong field. The pendant provides a short spoken request and receives a concise, auditable result.
args.model_tier: background for extracting and normalizing terminal output; realtime only for the spoken request and final confirmation
args.latency_budget: 2-5 seconds for command/output lookup and form inspection; under 10 seconds for filling and returning a field-by-field report
args.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap extraction call plus one browser inspection/action; roughly $0.01-$0.05, dominated by vision only when the form has no semantic labels
args.security_concerns: Terminal output and authenticated form contents remain on the Mac/browser bridge except the minimal extracted value sent through the relay. Never infer a field when labels are ambiguous; return a preview of field/value pairs and require the owner to say submit for irreversible submission.
missing: A typed handoff object linking a shell job/result to a browser command, with provenance and redaction of secrets
Browser action support for filling from an explicit value map and returning the resulting DOM/displayed values
A relay response that can speak the field-by-field receipt back to the pendant

args.user_asks: Keep watching this build/test command and interrupt me through the pendant only when its state changes, it fails, or it needs a decision.
args.why_useful: A 120-second shell action is treated as one opaque job today. The owner cannot leave a test/build running, walk away, and get a useful spoken delta; they either poll or miss the failure. This turns the Mac into an unattended worker while preserving the pendant as the attention channel.
args.model_tier: background model for periodic log summarization and state classification; realtime only to deliver the short alert and collect a decision
args.latency_budget: Detect process exit immediately; summarize meaningful log changes within 10 seconds while suppressing repeated noise
args.cost_estimate: One cheap incremental summarization call per meaningful log chunk, typically $0.01-$0.10 per hour depending on output volume; local hashing/filtering should dominate normal idle cost
args.security_concerns: Logs may contain source code, paths, or secrets. Keep raw logs on the Mac, send only bounded redacted deltas to the relay, and let the owner choose whether alerts include a line excerpt. The watcher must never silently restart or kill a process.
missing: A detached process/watch action with a durable cursor and process-group identity, rather than execAsync's single 120-second call
Incremental stdout/stderr tailing and exit-code/process-state reporting in the job journal
A relay-to-pendant alert route with deduplication and a 'snooze this watcher' response

args.user_asks: Find every recurring subscription visible in my authenticated browser and local receipts, reconcile duplicates, and give me one spoken list of what is charging me, with links to cancel each one.
args.why_useful: The browser can see logged-in account pages and the Mac can search downloaded receipts, but neither surface alone can reconcile them. The owner gets a high-value financial inventory without manually searching tabs, email exports, and Downloads; cancellation remains an explicit later request.
args.model_tier: background model for extraction, deduplication, and date/amount normalization; realtime only for the final spoken summary
args.latency_budget: 30-90 seconds for a bounded set of open authenticated tabs plus local receipt folders; return progress if a source is slow
args.cost_estimate: $0.05-$0.30 per inventory, mostly browser/page extraction and OCR of receipts; cache document hashes so unchanged receipts cost nothing on later runs
args.security_concerns: This is sensitive financial data. Keep raw pages/receipts local, transmit only normalized merchant/amount/frequency/cancel URL, redact account numbers, and never click cancellation or export data without a separate explicit ask. Require source citations for every line and mark uncertain matches.
missing: A local-only file search action that returns structured receipt candidates without uploading raw documents
Browser extraction across authenticated tabs with per-field provenance and an explicit allowlist of pages
A cross-surface deduplication schema and spoken summary with citations/uncertainty

args.change: Add a USB-tethered local pendant session: auto-discover /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, bind the nRF9160 button/audio stream to the Mac relay as a first-class device even when LTE registration is absent, and route spoken replies/status back over the ESP32 bridge. Persist a session UUID and reconnect cursor so unplug/replug does not duplicate a turn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can wear and use the real pendant on the Mac today instead of waiting for LTE registration; the same button request can inspect Safari, run a local command, and speak the result with honest offline/link status.
args.effort: Medium: serial framing/baud discovery, bridge lifecycle, turn-id replay tests, and one local device registration path.
args.risk: Malformed serial frames or reconnect races could duplicate audio or commands. Gate only by exact turn ID/cursor and keep the existing truthful link beacon authoritative; on ambiguity drop the frame and report disconnected rather than guessing.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for local turns; roughly 1-3% Mac CPU while active and small bridge development cost. No new hardware.
args.latency_impact: USB local round trips should reduce request/reply latency by roughly 100-500 ms versus waiting for an unregistered LTE path.
args.security_impact: USB is a local trust boundary: bind only the two enumerated serial identities, do not expose the serial protocol on LAN, and keep bearer credentials out of firmware. Local commands still follow the owner's deliberate full-control policy.
depends_on: A serial protocol adapter for the nRF9160 and ESP32 firmware
A local relay device-registration/session route
Turn-idempotent audio and event forwarding
The already accepted audio_link_truth_and_recovery and truthful_action_status_beacon behavior

transcript.text:
Round 178 produced three new capabilities and one immediate integration change:

1. **Terminal-to-Safari value handoff** — extract a value from a local shell result, fill the authenticated Safari form, and speak back an exact field/value receipt. The missing piece is the typed bridge between `/execute` results and browser field actions.

2. **Long-running command watcher** — monitor builds/tests and alert the pendant only on meaningful state changes, failures, or decisions. This needs detached process groups, incremental stdout/stderr cursors, exit-code reporting, and deduplicated pendant alerts.

3. **Subscription reconciliation** — combine authenticated browser pages with local receipts, deduplicate recurring charges, and speak a cited cancellation list without performing cancellations. This needs local-only structured file search, browser provenance, and cross-surface normalization.

4. **USB-local pendant session** — use the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 serial devices as a first-class local pendant path, even before LTE registration. This would make the real wearable usable on the Mac immediately, with turn-idempotent reconnect behavior and truthful link status.

What I still need is not another shell permission or another renamed diagnostics tool. The unresolved work is:

- A serial adapter/session-registration route for the two live USB devices.
- A typed shell-result-to-browser handoff contract.
- Detached process and incremental log APIs.
- Local structured receipt/file search that does not upload raw financial documents.
- Browser field extraction/fill with provenance and displayed-value verification.
- A relay event path that can deliver deduplicated alerts and receipts to the pendant.

The attempted `mac_read_diagnostics` call did not resolve in the live inventory; direct authenticated routes such as `/health`, `/machine-context`, `/jobs/:jobId`, and `/journal/:jobId` remain the reliable discovery paths.

args.user_asks: Remember this value for the next form I open, then fill only the matching field when I say 'use the remembered value'.
args.why_useful: The owner frequently transfers one-time identifiers, totals, tracking numbers, and account references between spoken conversation and authenticated forms. A short-lived, provenance-labeled value slot would remove error-prone retyping without creating a permanent memory of sensitive data.
args.model_tier: Realtime for extracting the value from the spoken turn and matching the active field; no background model unless the field label is ambiguous
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to acknowledge capture; under 3 seconds to fill after the explicit 'use' command
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per use; dominated by realtime inference only when speech contains multiple candidate values
args.security_concerns: Store only an encrypted, expiring value plus source turn and intended field class; never persist it in general memory or logs. Refuse to fill a differently typed field, show the masked value on the pendant, and expire after one successful use or 10 minutes.
missing: An ephemeral encrypted value-slot service with one-use semantics
Browser field-type discovery and a value-class compatibility check
A pendant command/result protocol for capture, expiry, and successful consumption

args.user_asks: If a travel booking, delivery, or appointment changes, find the best replacement in the authenticated pages I already use, update my local calendar draft, and tell me the tradeoff through the pendant.
args.why_useful: Time-sensitive changes require combining authenticated browser portals, local calendar/files, and a low-attention spoken interface. The owner should not have to notice an email, compare alternatives, copy details, and repair their calendar manually while traveling or working.
args.model_tier: Background model for monitoring and comparing alternatives; realtime only for urgent spoken interruption and the owner's choice
args.latency_budget: Detect a watched change within 2 minutes; produce a bounded comparison within 30 seconds; never silently finalize a booking or payment
args.cost_estimate: $0.05-$0.50 per change, dominated by authenticated page inspection and alternative comparison; unchanged pages should cost almost nothing via hashes
args.security_concerns: Travel, delivery, and appointment pages reveal sensitive location and schedule data. Keep raw pages local, send only normalized options, and require explicit owner selection before any purchase, cancellation, or external message. Every calendar edit needs an undoable receipt.
missing: A generalized authenticated page-watch rule with semantic change detection
A local calendar-draft action that can reconcile time zones and conflicts
A structured alternative-comparison and owner-selection protocol spanning browser, Mac, and pendant

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 6 of 7 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /watches. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: When the web app breaks, collect the exact browser state and the relevant local logs, reproduce it once, and give me a ready-to-send bug report with evidence and a minimal next step.
args.why_useful: The browser holds the authenticated failure state while the Mac holds the project and server logs; either node alone loses half the diagnosis. The owner gets a useful report instead of repeatedly explaining a failure or sending screenshots without context.
args.model_tier: Background model for log correlation, reproduction, and report drafting; realtime only for the spoken diagnosis and a short follow-up question
args.latency_budget: Collect evidence in 5 seconds, attempt one bounded reproduction in 30 seconds, and return a report draft within 60 seconds
args.cost_estimate: $0.05-$0.40 per incident, mostly vision/log-context processing; local hashing and filtering should avoid resending unchanged logs
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents, cookies, source code, and logs are highly sensitive. Keep raw evidence on the Mac, redact tokens/cookies/customer data before model calls, attach only selected snippets and screenshots, and never send the report externally without explicit owner action.
missing: A browser diagnostic snapshot including console/network errors and DOM state without exporting session secrets
A local log correlation/search action keyed by timestamp, project, and request ID
An evidence bundle format with redaction, reproducibility metadata, and a draft-only external-share action

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- One-use, expiring spoken values for accurately filling matching browser fields.
- Change-aware travel, delivery, and appointment recovery across authenticated browser pages, local calendar, and the pendant.
- Evidence-backed web incident diagnosis combining browser state, Mac logs, reproduction, and a draft bug report.

Each was recorded with the required missing components, privacy boundaries, latency, cost, and existing routes/surfaces it would build from.

args.user_asks: When something I asked you to do fails, tell me on the pendant exactly what broke and offer to repair or retry it; if I ask later, 'what happened?', show the command, app/tab, error, and whether anything changed.
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell action loses exit code, cancellation cannot stop a running command, and jobs, receipts, and ledgers do not join cleanly. The owner should not have to inspect JSON or guess whether a browser action partially happened. This turns opaque failures into a trustworthy, actionable answer across the worn interface and Mac.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to understand the short spoken question and speak the result; use a cheaper background model to normalize receipts, classify failure, and draft a repair plan. The Mac executes only after the normal owner instruction policy.
args.latency_budget: Pendant failure beacon immediately; structured incident capsule within 2 seconds after job completion; spoken explanation under 3 seconds. Repair can run asynchronously with progress pushed to the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.03 per incident depending on whether diagnosis needs a model; most incidents are deterministic receipt/error formatting. Storage is a small bounded incident record.
args.security_concerns: Command strings, stderr, URLs, and browser titles may contain secrets or personal data. Redact environment values and known token patterns before relay storage, retain locally by default, and require explicit confirmation before retrying a non-idempotent repair. Never claim success without a receipt.
missing: Capture shell exit code and signal instead of flattening exec errors
Record effective timeout, pid, and a redacted environment fingerprint
Close the action ledger and persist a jobId↔ledgerId link
Make cancellation pass an AbortSignal to the child process
Add a bounded incident endpoint and pendant push event
Define retry/idempotency metadata for repair plans

args.user_asks: Let me say 'pick up where I left off' and have the pendant reopen the exact work state from my last interrupted task—active Safari tab, app/window, project and branch, terminal directory, and the unfinished step—then ask one concise question if re-entry is ambiguous.
args.why_useful: A Mac restart, bridge disconnect, or abandoned multi-step task currently leaves the owner to reconstruct context manually. This is not a bookmark: it is an automatically generated, resumable work capsule tied to an interrupted execution, with a safe re-entry action and a spoken disambiguation path.
args.model_tier: Generate and rank capsules in the background with a cheap model and deterministic host collectors; use realtime only for the owner's spoken resume request and one clarification. Mac-planner performs the re-entry actions; browser-extension restores the authenticated tab without exporting page contents.
args.latency_budget: Create capsule on interruption/restart in under 5 seconds; answer the spoken request in under 2 seconds; restore app/tab/window in under 5 seconds, then report the exact unresolved step.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.015 per capsule; collection is local and deterministic, with model cost only for summarizing the unfinished step. Bounded local storage under a few MB.
args.security_concerns: Capsules can reveal sensitive app names, URLs, project paths, and session identifiers. Keep page bodies and credentials out; encrypt or hash sensitive fields, retain on the Mac by default, and require confirmation before replaying a mutation. Reject stale capsules after project/branch changes.
missing: Boot-time reconciliation that marks processing jobs interrupted rather than leaving them forever running
Automatic interrupted-job capsule creation from job and action-ledger state
Collectors for foreground app/window, terminal cwd/git state, and active browser tab
A durable capsule schema with freshness and stale-state checks
A Mac action to focus an existing window and browser command to select a specific tab
Relay storage/push route for capsule summaries

args.user_asks: Tell me when my personal computer setup is unhealthy, and fix the harmless parts automatically: 'my pendant says the Mac is unreachable', 'Safari bridge is stale', or 'why is this slow?' should produce a spoken diagnosis with the exact stale component and one-click repair, not a generic offline message.
args.why_useful: The relay, Mac bridge, browser extension, and pendant can each be alive while the path between them is broken. The owner currently sees fragmented health signals and may not know whether to restart an app, reconnect USB, or wait for the relay. A cross-node health explanation saves the most frustrating daily failures.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic probes and a cheap background classifier for health snapshots; reserve realtime for the spoken question and terse explanation. Do not spend the expensive model on periodic polling.
args.latency_budget: Relay detects a missed heartbeat within 30 seconds; pendant receives a local status pattern immediately and a spoken diagnosis within 3 seconds of asking. Harmless repair (restart bridge, reopen extension host, reconnect polling) should complete within 15 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.001 per health cycle with deterministic probes; occasional model explanation <$0.01. Network and local polling dominate, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Health data exposes hostnames, app inventory, tab URLs, and connectivity. Send only booleans, timestamps, component IDs, and redacted error classes to relay; keep detailed diagnostics on Mac. Automatic repair must be limited to reversible service/app restarts and should leave an audit receipt.
missing: A signed end-to-end health envelope with monotonic timestamps and component identity
USB serial probes for the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 (currently attached but pendant is not LTE-registered)
A relay route that correlates Mac, browser, pendant, and bridge heartbeats into one causal status
Typed reversible repair actions and receipts for restarting/reconnecting local agents
Pendant push mapping from component-specific health state to the existing truthful status beacon

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 7 of 8 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /watches/health. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.change: Replace run_shell's opaque exec-only observation with a compatibility-preserving command supervisor: retain the raw command and /bin/sh -c semantics for FULL_CONTROL_MODE, but launch each child in its own process group, capture exit code/signal, pid, effective timeout, start/finish monotonic times, bounded stdout/stderr tails plus an on-disk full transcript, and a redacted environment fingerprint. Wire cancellation to terminate the process group and close every execute ledger with its jobId before marking the job complete.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When a command hangs, fails, or partially changes the Mac, the owner gets an honest answer and a real stop button instead of a forever-running job and a vague 'Failed'. The agent can repair or retry based on evidence rather than repeating blindly.
args.effort: Medium-high: supervisor wrapper, receipt schema migration, process-group lifecycle, redaction, boot reconciliation, and regression tests for shell rewrites and large output.
args.risk: Changing process launch can break commands that depend on inherited shell behavior, signals, or cwd. Keep /bin/sh -c and env inheritance initially, canary the supervisor behind a flag, and fall back to current exec only on launch failure; never lose the original command transcript.
args.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost; a bounded transcript ring may add tens of MB locally. No new cloud spend if detailed output stays on Mac.
args.latency_impact: <50 ms launch overhead; cancellation becomes immediate rather than waiting up to 120 s. Large-output capture becomes more reliable because the user-facing response is bounded while the transcript is durable.
args.security_impact: Do not store raw environment values; hash names/values with secret-pattern redaction. Raw stdout/stderr remains local and access-controlled. This improves auditability without adding an approval gate or reducing the owner's deliberate full-control policy.
depends_on: Preserve FULL_CONTROL_MODE and unrestricted shell semantics
Add jobId↔ledgerId linkage and call closeLedger on all terminal paths
Implement process-group-aware cancellation in computerControl.runShell
Add boot-time reconciliation for processing jobs
Expose structured failure/incident data to relay and pendant

args.change: Add a tethered-pendant session mode in the Mac bridge: auto-discover /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* (nRF9160) and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA (ESP32 audio bridge), open both with framing/version negotiation, and expose one local voice session to the relay even when LTE registration is absent. Route button/audio events over USB, keep relay job IDs and replay cursors in a crash-safe local spool, and hand off to LTE later without duplicating a turn.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The hardware is physically on the owner's Mac today but currently behaves as if it does not exist because the pendant is not registered with LTE. This makes the wearable testable immediately at a desk: press the real button, speak through the real bridge, hear the reply, and retain work when the cable or relay briefly drops.
args.effort: High: serial protocol implementation, dual-port discovery, audio clock/backpressure handling, pairing, local spool integration, and an end-to-end test harness using both boards.
args.risk: USB reconnects, stale device nodes, framing corruption, and duplicate audio turns could produce clipped or repeated replies. Require device identity/version handshake, CRC and sequence numbers, bounded replay cursors, and an explicit route transition record; fall back to the current network path when negotiation fails.
args.cost_impact: No recurring model cost beyond normal voice turns; modest Mac CPU/USB bandwidth. Firmware changes should fit existing RAM by keeping buffers small and reusing the accepted audio recovery state.
args.latency_impact: USB tethering should reduce round-trip transport latency versus LTE by tens to hundreds of milliseconds; discovery/reconnect under 2 seconds. Audio must use backpressure rather than queueing stale frames.
args.security_impact: USB serial is local but still a control boundary: authenticate the paired board identity and encrypt or MAC control frames; never expose raw serial commands to the LAN. Keep transcripts and replay spool local until relay acknowledgement.
depends_on: Implement the pending mac_usb_serial_diagnostics request or an equivalent fixed serial discovery probe
Define a versioned nRF9160↔ESP32 framing/audio protocol
Bridge USB session events into POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio
Persist turn/replay cursor with the existing pendant_store semantics
Teach the relay to accept a transport=usb-tethered session and later hand off to LTE
Use truthful_action_status_beacon and audio_link_truth_and_recovery state transitions

args.finding: The Mac agent, relay, and Safari extension are all online and authenticated; FULL_CONTROL_MODE and computer-use are enabled, Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted, Safari has 9 tabs with x.com active, and the relay reports macBridgeOnline=true. The granted mac_read_diagnostics schema still does not resolve in this live inventory.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status returned HTTP 200 with agent.ready-equivalent permissions, relay.reachable=true, browser online=true, and 9 tabs; GET /jobs returned completed browser_list_tabs receipts.

args.user_asks: Make sure this gets done by morning, and only wake me if you need a decision: keep the authenticated browser task and Mac work alive across disconnects, retry transient failures, verify the final result independently, and tell me on the pendant if the goal is blocked or complete.
args.why_useful: Today the system can dispatch actions, but a multi-step goal dies as soon as one command fails, the bridge disappears, or a browser command goes stale. The owner cannot delegate an outcome—only a sequence of steps. This would turn the pendant into a genuine asynchronous agent: it carries the goal while the owner is away, uses the Mac and authenticated browser session together, and interrupts only for an irreversible choice or missing information.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for goal decomposition, transient-error classification, checkpoint verification, and scheduling. Use the realtime model only when the pendant must ask a concise decision question or report completion. Deterministic planners should handle known retryable actions without model calls.
args.latency_budget: Accept the goal in under 3 seconds and provide a durable queued confirmation immediately. Resume within 10 seconds of a Mac/browser reconnect. Retry with bounded exponential backoff; wake the owner within 30 seconds of a true blocker and within 5 seconds of verified completion.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.10 per delegated goal depending on number of checkpoints; most polling, retries, and verification are deterministic. Mac/browser execution and relay storage dominate infrastructure cost, not speech.
args.security_concerns: A long-lived goal can mutate authenticated web accounts while the owner is absent. Require an explicit scope and expiry, forbid silently broadening the goal, keep credentials in the browser session, and stop at payment, deletion, sending, publishing, or other irreversible boundaries. Store only redacted checkpoint evidence and give the owner a pendant-visible cancel/status path.
missing: A durable goal state machine separate from one-shot jobs, with expiry, checkpoints, dependencies, and wake conditions
Real action retries and idempotency keys for Mac and browser operations, with a distinction between transient and semantic failure
A browser-session lease/heartbeat that can detect stale authenticated tabs and resume the same tab without exporting secrets
Independent postcondition verification actions and evidence capsules
A scheduler that can run a goal while the owner and realtime model are offline
A pendant command/status protocol for queued, running, blocked, expired, and verified-complete goals
A single cancellation path that terminates active Mac processes and withdraws pending browser commands

args.user_asks: When a website needs me to sign in or approve something, tell me on the pendant which site, account, and exact action it is requesting; let me approve that one request by pressing the button, without sending my password or exposing the page to the cloud.
args.why_useful: Authenticated browser sessions are the strongest reach in the system, but the owner has no trustworthy bridge between a remote browser prompt and a physical, private decision. Today an agent either stalls on MFA/approval or asks for sensitive credentials in conversation. A signed, origin-bound approval lets unattended work proceed while keeping secrets and the final consent with the wearer.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic browser instrumentation to identify origin, account label, requested operation, and challenge type; use a cheap model only to summarize ambiguous page text locally. Realtime should speak only the short approval prompt. Never use the expensive model to handle credentials or OTP values.
args.latency_budget: Detect and push an approval card within 2 seconds of the browser challenge; button approval reaches the extension within 1 second; report success or rejection within 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.005 per approval, mostly relay/event overhead; no credential transcription or large page upload. A small local approval ledger is the main storage cost.
args.security_concerns: This is a high-risk authorization surface. Bind each approval to exact origin, tab, account, action hash, expiry, and nonce; reject navigation or DOM changes after preview; never transmit passwords, OTPs, cookies, or page bodies through relay. Require a distinct physical press and show an unmistakable local pending pattern; log both approval and browser result. A stale or mismatched challenge must fail closed.
missing: Browser extension instrumentation for a signed, structured approval request and action hash
A relay route that transports only redacted challenge metadata and nonce-bound responses
Pendant firmware support for a one-shot approval decision distinct from ordinary conversation recording
Mac/browser executor enforcement that an approval cannot be replayed on another tab, origin, or action
A local audit receipt joining the physical press to the browser result
Origin/account verification that does not rely solely on model interpretation of page text

args.user_asks: If I say 'privacy now' or press the pendant's privacy control, immediately stop listening, mute/stop playback, pause cloud work, hide sensitive browser tabs, and lock or cover the Mac; when I return, tell me exactly what was paused and restore only what I explicitly resume.
args.why_useful: The system can reach the owner's microphone path, authenticated browser, Mac screen, and cloud jobs, but there is no single physical privacy boundary. In a meeting, public place, or unexpected visitor situation, the owner should not have to find the right app, tab, audio route, and pending job individually. One local action should make the whole hive quiet and leave a truthful recovery trail.
args.model_tier: No model is needed for the emergency transition: firmware and deterministic relay/Mac handlers execute it. Use realtime only to confirm the owner's later spoken resume request; use a cheap background process to summarize what was paused.
args.latency_budget: Local microphone/playback mute and pendant indication under 100 ms; relay pause and browser/Mac privacy actions under 2 seconds. If disconnected, local mute and a durable pending privacy command happen immediately and reconcile on reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost; small local state record and one relay event per transition. Screen lock/tab hiding uses existing Mac/browser control paths.
args.security_concerns: Privacy mode must be fail-safe and local-first: never depend on cloud acknowledgement to mute audio. Do not destroy evidence or silently cancel irreversible work; freeze it, mark its state, and expose a physical cancel/restore policy. Browser tab hiding must not export URLs or page contents. The pendant needs a distinct physical control or a firmware-safe edge, not a gesture that delays recording.
missing: A dedicated physical privacy input or firmware action with priority over conversation state
A local audio gate that mutes capture and playback independently of relay availability
Relay-wide pause semantics for active pipelines, scheduled goals, and pending browser commands
Mac actions to lock/blank display and browser actions to hide or restore a specified tab set
A durable privacy epoch so late completions cannot speak or reveal data after the transition
A truthful resume manifest reporting paused, completed, failed, and unknown work

transcript.summary: Recorded three capabilities that are not available to the owner today: durable overnight outcome delegation with retries and verified postconditions; origin-bound physical approval for authenticated browser requests without exposing credentials; and a local-first whole-hive privacy mode that mutes, pauses, hides, and reports state across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. Each requires new cross-node state/protocol work rather than merely exposing an existing route.
