args.user_asks: I tap the pendant and say “where did I leave off?” Have it give me a 30-second, actionable resumption brief from my Mac, browser, and unfinished AI work.
args.why_useful: This is the highest-value everyday behavior: after walking away, sleep, or a crash, the owner gets the exact next step instead of reconstructing state across Terminal, Safari, and the pendant. It only works as a hive: the pendant supplies the request and audio, the Mac supplies project/job state, Safari supplies authenticated page context, and the relay joins and speaks it.
args.model_tier: deterministic collection first; background model summarizes; realtime only handles the spoken request and delivery
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds for collection and a 20–30 second spoken answer; cap browser extraction at the active tab plus one recently relevant tab.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost if receipts, active project, active tab, and recent job records are structured; one short background summarization call when joining heterogeneous evidence dominates.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated URLs and terminal/project names must stay on the Mac/relay boundary and never be sent to an external browser. Return provenance and age for every claim; omit page bodies unless the owner explicitly asks.
missing: A single resume-snapshot endpoint joining GET /jobs/:jobId, GET /journal/:jobId, GET /projects/active, GET /machine-context, and browser active-tab inspection
A compact relay intent/response envelope that carries the pendant turn ID and evidence ages
A background summarizer that refuses to infer a next step when evidence is stale or contradictory

args.user_asks: When I say “that failed—fix it,” explain the failed Mac command in plain language, show the exact evidence, try one safe recovery with the right project directory, and tell me precisely what changed.
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell action loses exit code, PID, environment provenance, and often the real working directory, so the owner has to debug blind. This turns the Mac from fire-and-forget into a useful recovery partner without adding approval gates or reducing FULL_CONTROL_MODE.
args.model_tier: deterministic receipt/error parser and bounded retry planner; realtime only for the spoken exchange
args.latency_budget: Parse immediately; first diagnosis under 1 second; one recovery attempt within 10 seconds. Never loop retries.
args.cost_estimate: Most failures need no model call if exit code/signal/stderr/ cwd are typed; a small planner call only for selecting a recovery command. Cost is dominated by the exceptional planner call.
args.security_concerns: Record a redacted environment fingerprint, not secret values; preserve the unrestricted execution policy the owner chose. Recovery must include command, cwd, inputs, and before/after receipts in the spoken and durable result. A recovery that can delete or publish data must be reported as such, not silently guessed.
missing: Shell receipts with exit code, signal, pid, timeout-vs-exit distinction, argv-or-original-command, cwd, and a hashed environment allowlist
A failure classifier that distinguishes missing executable, wrong cwd, permission, timeout, network, and nonzero application result
A one-recovery planner that can query GET /projects/active and recent receipts, then emits a linked POST /execute job with an explicit parentJobId
Boot-time reconciliation that marks jobs interrupted by agent restart instead of leaving them processing forever

args.user_asks: When the relay or LTE is unavailable but the pendant is plugged into my Mac, let me say “stop that,” “save this,” or “what is running?” and have the Mac act locally, then queue a truthful result for later delivery.
args.why_useful: The hardware is physically present today even though the pendant is not LTE-registered. A dropped WAN link should not make a wearable attached by USB useless: emergency stop/status and durable capture are precisely the actions that must work at the edge. The pendant gives an unambiguous physical request, the USB serial path reaches the Mac, and the relay later reconciles the result rather than inventing success.
args.model_tier: deterministic local intents for stop/status/save; no cloud model while offline; background reconciliation and optional speech summary when relay returns
args.latency_budget: LED acknowledgment under 150 ms, local status under 1 second, stop dispatch under 2 seconds; reconnect reconciliation in the background.
args.cost_estimate: No API cost for local intents; a few hundred bytes of serial traffic per event. A short relay summarization call only when queued events are merged after reconnection.
args.security_concerns: Only accept a signed, paired USB device nonce and monotonically increasing intent sequence; reject stale/replayed frames. “Stop” must target a specific active job and report whether it was actually interruptible (current shell cancellation is cooperative). Never transmit terminal output or browser content merely to acknowledge a local intent.
missing: A real framed USB serial protocol between /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* (nRF9160) and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA (ESP32 bridge), with CRC, sequence, and replay protection
A Mac local-intent daemon that maps three bounded intents to GET /jobs, POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel, and POST /capture without contacting the relay
A durable outbox reconciliation route carrying local intent/result IDs into the relay when reachable
A cancellation implementation that passes AbortSignal to child processes, so local “stop” can actually terminate a running shell instead of merely marking it

args.finding: The Mac agent is online with FULL_CONTROL_MODE true, relay reachable, Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, and Safari extension online with 9 tabs; active tab is X at https://x.com/home. The pendant LTE device remains offline, but the USB-connected hardware is available per system context.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status returned agent.fullControlMode=true, relay.reachable=true, browser online=true/tabCount=9; GET /jobs returned a successful browser_list_tabs receipt.

transcript.text:
Round 185 findings:

- Mac agent is online with unrestricted execution enabled.
- Relay is reachable.
- Safari bridge is online with 9 tabs; active tab is X.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions are granted.
- The pendant remains LTE-offline, but the USB-connected hardware is usable today.
- Routing telemetry currently has no samples or pricing data, so model-cost optimization cannot yet be measured.

I recorded three capabilities:

1. **“Where did I leave off?”** — join Mac project/job state with the active authenticated browser tab and speak a concise resumption brief through the pendant. The recorder flagged it as close to an existing “restore my working context” proposal, so the genuinely new part is the evidence-age/provenance join and refusal to infer from stale state.

2. **“That failed—fix it.”** — preserve shell exit code, signal, PID, timeout status, cwd, and redacted environment provenance; diagnose the failure and attempt exactly one linked recovery. This builds on the unrestricted shell policy rather than adding gates.

3. **Offline USB local mode** — while the pendant is USB-connected but relay/LTE is unavailable, support local `stop`, `save`, and `what is running?` intents, then reconcile results with the relay later. This needs real serial framing and actual process interruption, not merely marking a job cancelled.

What I still need:

- **The pending USB serial diagnostics capability** for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`; the current diagnostic grants cannot inspect these devices.
- **The pending browser artifact export capability**, so authenticated Safari evidence can be handed to the Mac/relay without inventing a new browser path.
- New implementation work for typed shell receipts: exit status, signal, PID, timeout distinction, and environment fingerprint.
- A real parent-job/recovery link between `/execute`, receipts, journals, and retry attempts.
- Boot-time reconciliation for jobs left `processing` after an agent crash.
- USB intent framing with CRC, sequence numbers, pairing, replay rejection, and a durable relay reconciliation path.
- Actual `AbortSignal` propagation into shell child processes so the pendant’s local “stop” command can terminate work rather than only request cooperative cancellation.

args.user_asks: Let me ask, “What did you do on my behalf about the rent email?” and get a chronological, source-linked answer covering what I said on the pendant, what the Mac changed, what Safari showed or submitted, and what is still unresolved.
args.why_useful: Today the system can perform work across surfaces but cannot answer forensically what happened to one real-world matter. A single trace would prevent duplicate replies, expose an unnoticed failure, and let the owner correct the agent with facts rather than memory. This is a cross-surface capability: no individual node has the complete story.
args.model_tier: Deterministic correlation and redaction first; a background model turns the trace into a short answer; realtime only handles the spoken query.
args.latency_budget: Return a bounded 60-second spoken answer within 4 seconds for the last 7 days; older searches can run in the background and notify the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Low when correlation uses indexed IDs, timestamps, URLs, and action types; one short summarization call dominates cost for a multi-step matter.
args.security_concerns: Search must be owner-scoped and preserve source boundaries. Do not expose full email or page bodies by default; speak snippets with links and timestamps. Sensitive browser fields and shell environments stay local unless explicitly requested.
missing: A durable cross-surface matter ID that can be attached to a voice turn, Mac job, browser command, capture, and relay event
An indexed event store with normalized timestamps, causal parent IDs, and explicit success/failure/unknown states
A provenance query endpoint that returns source excerpts and redaction metadata rather than an opaque summary
A retention and deletion control for matter traces

args.user_asks: Before I send this, let me ask the pendant “have I already sent something like it?” and get a duplicate-risk answer across Mail, authenticated Safari pages, and previous Mac actions without opening or editing anything.
args.why_useful: Duplicate messages, payments, forms, and support requests are a costly failure mode that no single surface can detect. The system should compare the owner’s intended subject/recipient/amount and semantic content against recent sent evidence, while making clear when it cannot prove absence.
args.model_tier: Deterministic candidate retrieval and exact field matching first; a background model compares only capped, redacted candidate text; realtime speaks the confidence and evidence.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for a 30-day search; return immediately with “not enough evidence” rather than waiting indefinitely for an authenticated tab.
args.cost_estimate: Low for structured fields and hashes; model cost is limited to a few candidate snippets and only for semantic similarity.
args.security_concerns: Never crawl all private content indiscriminately. Require an explicit scope (mail, current browser origin, or Mac action history), keep credentials and unrelated messages out of the prompt, and distinguish “no match found” from “not searched.” No mutation is allowed in this capability.
missing: A consented, read-only Mail search adapter and a browser-side sent-action/evidence index
Canonical normalization for recipient, amount, subject, URL, form target, and content fingerprint across Mail, Safari, and Mac receipts
A temporal duplicate query with explicit search coverage and confidence, including an auditable list of matches
A pendant response format that can speak uncertainty without collapsing it into yes/no

args.user_asks: Do not tell me an action is done until you independently verify its intended outcome—for example, confirm the form's success receipt, the file's expected contents, or the calendar event's actual fields—and tell me what could not be verified.
args.why_useful: An action receipt currently proves that a command or click ran, not that the owner’s goal happened. Independent outcome verification prevents the most dangerous false confidence: a submitted form that was rejected, a file written to the wrong project, or a calendar event with the wrong time. The pendant gets a truthful spoken result while Mac and Safari provide the observables.
args.model_tier: Deterministic verifier with typed predicates and fresh reads; background model only translates ambiguous page/file evidence; realtime delivers the verdict.
args.latency_budget: Verification within 2 seconds for local files and 5 seconds for browser outcomes; if an external confirmation is delayed, say “dispatched, not verified” and schedule a background check.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model call when predicates are typed (file exists, URL/status/title matches, event fields equal); exceptional semantic page verification costs one small background call.
args.security_concerns: Verification must be read-only and bound to the exact action ID, target tab, path, or event. Never treat a similar page or stale screenshot as proof. Do not leak private page contents; return only the predicate result and minimal evidence. Require explicit expiry for delayed checks.
missing: An owner- or planner-supplied outcome predicate attached to every mutating action
Fresh postcondition readers for files, browser submissions, Calendar/Mail, and shell-generated artifacts
A verifier ledger that records expected predicate, observation timestamp, evidence hash, and verified/failed/unknown state
Pendant and relay vocabulary that separates accepted, executed, verified, and contradicted

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

- Cross-surface “what happened about this matter?” trace
- Duplicate-risk search before sending or submitting
- Independent outcome verification before claiming completion

args.user_asks: “That Mac task failed—explain the real cause and retry it the right way.”
args.why_useful: Today a failed shell job collapses exit status and error details, cannot be resumed, and cancellation cannot stop a running process. This capability would turn a dead-end failure into a bounded repair: identify whether it was timeout, missing dependency, transient network, or a bad path; propose the smallest correction; then rerun with the original job linked to the repair and report the result on the pendant.
args.model_tier: A cheap background classifier diagnoses stderr/exit metadata and chooses a repair template; realtime is used only for the owner-facing explanation and explicit spoken retry request.
args.latency_budget: Diagnosis under 1 second from stored receipt; retry starts immediately and streams a one-line progress state to the pendant. Long commands remain asynchronous.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic classes; $0.002–$0.01 for an uncommon model diagnosis, plus normal command cost. Do not resend full stdout; send bounded excerpts and structured exit data.
args.security_concerns: The repair model sees command, cwd, stderr, and selected environment names. Secrets must be redacted. Automatic retry is acceptable for the owner's maximum-access policy only when the repair is mechanically local (timeout/path/temporary network); destructive or externally visible commands must be reported as non-retryable, not silently replayed.
missing: Capture the actual exit code, signal, timeout-vs-killed distinction, and a redacted environment fingerprint in each run_shell receipt
A repair planner that emits a new action list with parentJobId and an idempotency key, rather than blindly duplicating side effects
A relay event carrying failure/repair state to the pendant's already-accepted truthful_action_status_beacon

args.change: Add a first-class detached task supervisor for long-running Mac work. run_shell actions that opt into task mode should launch under a small local supervisor with a stable task ID, captured pid/process group, monotonic start/finish times, exit code/signal, bounded stdout/stderr spool, heartbeats, and a boot-time reattach/reconcile pass. The relay polls task state independently of the HTTP request; a reconnecting pendant receives queued state transitions. Keep ordinary run_shell behavior unchanged, but expose task mode as a distinct action type so it cannot be confused with a completed synchronous job.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A build, export, download, test suite, or backup can keep running when the Mac agent UI, relay connection, or pendant link drops. The owner can leave, ask later “is that done?”, and receive the truthful result instead of a permanently processing job or having to rerun an uncertain side effect.
args.effort: Medium-high: supervisor daemon/process-group handling, durable task state, bounded spool, boot reconciliation, and relay event integration; one to two weeks for a robust implementation plus crash tests.
args.risk: Orphaned processes or duplicate reattachment could cause side effects. Use a stable task identity, process-group ownership, explicit adoption states (running/unknown/finished), and never rerun automatically after a crash. If reattach fails, report unknown rather than inventing completion. Cap output and reap abandoned tasks.
args.cost_impact: No model/API cost for supervision; small local disk writes and one low-rate relay poll/heartbeat per active task. CPU overhead is negligible outside active tasks.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms to task launch and makes status queries immediate; completion notification is event-driven rather than waiting for a request timeout.
args.security_impact: The supervisor inherits the same deliberate maximum-access policy, but should record a redacted environment fingerprint and never persist raw secrets in the spool. Process-group metadata and command strings stay in the authenticated local job store.
depends_on: A new task-mode action and stable task record schema
Repair the existing job↔ledger join and close ledgers at completion so task state is auditable
A relay task-status event consumed by truthful_action_status_beacon
Boot-time reconciliation that distinguishes an exited child from an unknown child

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “Do the browser task, then prove exactly what changed.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated browser work is where a mistaken click can matter most. The owner should receive a compact before/after witness—target URL and title, relevant DOM text or download hash, action sequence, and whether the page actually confirmed the change—rather than the agent merely saying it clicked a button. The pendant can announce success or uncertainty while the browser session remains private on the Mac.
args.model_tier: Deterministic DOM/state comparison first; a cheap text model summarizes the diff. Realtime only speaks the short result or asks for clarification when the witness is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Read-only witness under 1 second; mutation plus verification under 5 seconds for normal pages. Long downloads become asynchronous tasks.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model call, or $0.001–$0.01 for summarization. Hashes and structured DOM selectors are far cheaper than screenshots.
args.security_concerns: Never export full page content by default; scope evidence to the target element and origin. Strip tokens, email bodies, and form values. Keep authenticated evidence local unless the owner explicitly asks for relay delivery. A failed verification must be reported as unknown, not success.
missing: A browser action transaction that records before-state, intended locator/value, after-state, and a cryptographic artifact hash as one durable receipt
A local-only evidence filter that understands sensitive DOM fields and authenticated-origin boundaries
A relay-to-pendant result envelope supporting success, changed-but-unverified, and no-change states

args.finding: Mac agent is healthy with fullControlMode and computer-use loop enabled; Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted. Safari browser bridge is online with 9 tabs, active X tab, zero pending commands. Relay is reachable and Mac bridge online, but the physical pendant remains unregistered/offline.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status and GET /browser/status returned HTTP 200 at round 186; devices discovery shows home-macbook-bridge online and cloudflare-contract-test offline.

transcript.text:
Round 186 findings:

- Mac agent is healthy, full-control enabled, and computer-use enabled.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted.
- Safari bridge is online with 9 tabs and no pending commands; the active tab is X.
- Relay is reachable and the Mac bridge is online.
- The physical pendant is still not relay-registered, but the USB-attached pendant remains testable locally.

I produced four new proposals:

1. **Screen-and-context orientation:** ask “What am I looking at, and what should I do next?” using the active screen, browser tab, project, and latest job state.
2. **Failure-aware Mac task repair:** explain the actual failure and retry with structured diagnosis, rather than losing exit-code and timeout information.
3. **Detached long-running task supervisor:** let builds, downloads, and exports survive relay/UI disconnects and report truthful completion later.
4. **Browser action witness:** after an authenticated browser mutation, provide a scoped before/after proof with DOM evidence or artifact hashes.

What is still needed:

- Implementation work joining the existing capture, browser, project, job, and pendant-event routes into those user-facing flows.
- Durable shell metadata: exit code, signal, timeout distinction, process identity, redacted environment fingerprint, and job-to-ledger linkage.
- A detached-task supervisor with crash reconciliation and relay status events.
- Browser transaction receipts with sensitive-field redaction and before/after verification.
- The previously requested **USB serial diagnostics** and **browser local-artifact export** remain outstanding; I did not re-request them.

args.user_asks: “Read and summarize what is on my screen, but keep everything confidential—nothing from this screen may leave my Mac.”
args.why_useful: The owner can use the pendant around passwords, work, finance, or private messages without choosing between usefulness and privacy. Today the computer-use path can inspect the screen, but it does not offer a verifiable local-only mode; the owner cannot reliably know whether pixels or OCR context reached the relay/model.
args.model_tier: A local Mac OCR/layout model performs extraction and redaction; only the resulting short summary or synthesized audio leaves the Mac. Use realtime for the final spoken exchange, never for the raw screenshot.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds for a normal screen; under 6 seconds for a dense document. If local inference is unavailable, fail closed rather than silently falling back to cloud vision.
args.cost_estimate: No per-request cloud vision cost in the normal path; local CPU/GPU use is the dominant cost. A small realtime turn costs only the final response/audio tokens.
args.security_concerns: The privacy promise must be technically enforceable: disable network upload for the raw capture, show a persistent local-only indicator in the Mac agent and a distinct pendant tone, keep raw pixels in memory only, and provide a receipt proving the model endpoint was local. Redaction must cover passwords, payment fields, tokens, private messages, and browser form controls. If any component cannot attest to local execution, return “cannot provide privately.”
missing: A local-only vision/OCR execution path with network isolation for raw capture buffers
A signed privacy-mode receipt spanning capture, OCR, summarization, and audio delivery
A pendant-visible privacy state and fail-closed transport rule
A policy router that prevents /capture or browser inspection payloads from entering relay logging or cloud prompts while this mode is active

args.user_asks: “For the next ten minutes, let you work only in this browser tab, then revoke access automatically.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets practical delegation without permanently exposing every authenticated session. Today browser and Mac permissions are broad and durable; there is no spoken, tab-scoped lease whose expiry is independently enforced across the browser extension, Mac agent, and relay.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the spoken lease request; enforcement is deterministic and does not rely on a model remembering the deadline.
args.latency_budget: Lease activation under 1 second; expiry and revocation must occur within 1 second of the deadline even if the model or relay is busy.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; a small local timer and browser permission state are the main resources.
args.security_concerns: The lease must bind to tab ID, window ID, origin, permitted action classes, issuing turn, and absolute expiry. The browser extension and Mac agent must reject commands after expiry independently, including queued commands. Revocation state must survive relay loss and Mac restart; no cloud component should be able to extend the lease silently.
missing: A signed, tab-scoped capability lease understood by both browser extension and Mac agent
Local expiry enforcement in the extension and action dispatcher, including queued-command rejection
A pendant acknowledgment and unmistakable expired/revoked state
Lease audit records that omit page contents and credentials

args.user_asks: “Find the exact text I was looking at earlier and bring me back to it.”
args.why_useful: The owner often remembers a fragment, not a URL or filename. Today the system can inspect the current browser and Mac state, but it cannot search a private, time-indexed trail of the owner's previously viewed screen regions, selected text, browser pages, and project files, then restore the exact tab/scroll position with evidence.
args.model_tier: A local indexing process performs OCR/text hashing and retrieval; a cheap text model ranks matches. Realtime only asks a disambiguating question or speaks the selected result.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the common recent-history window; under 8 seconds for a larger local index. Restoration should be explicit and deterministic after the match is selected.
args.cost_estimate: No recurring cloud cost if the index and embeddings stay local; disk usage and periodic local embedding compute dominate.
args.security_concerns: Index only explicitly opted-in windows/origins and encrypt it at rest. Never upload raw screen history. Support immediate purge and per-origin exclusion. Results must show timestamp and source so an old match is not mistaken for current state.
missing: A local, encrypted, opt-in visual/text trail with retention and purge controls
Stable browser scroll/selection restoration primitives and Mac window-state capture
A retrieval protocol joining browser tab IDs, screen regions, project files, and pendant timestamps
A spoken disambiguation/result envelope that can restore only after the owner chooses a match

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- Verifiable **Mac-local private screen summarization**.
- **Spoken, tab-scoped temporary browser leases** with automatic revocation.
- **Searchable private visual/text history** that restores the exact prior tab or screen position.

args.user_asks: “Why did that task fail, and what exactly happened?” Give me a spoken, evidence-backed postmortem for the last thing I asked the pendant to do.
args.why_useful: Today the owner gets a vague failed message. This would join the pendant turn, relay pipeline, Mac job/action receipts, shell stderr/exit status, and browser command result into one causal timeline, distinguishing planner failure, transport loss, command failure, and partial completion. It turns an opaque autonomous system into something the owner can actually diagnose hands-free.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short spoken explanation; a cheap background summarizer builds the causal trace from receipts and journal records.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the first answer from existing records; under 10 seconds if a background trace must be assembled.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.01 per explanation; dominated by realtime speech response, not log collection.
args.security_concerns: Shell output and authenticated browser metadata may contain secrets. Redact environment variables, cookies, tokens, and likely-secret patterns before relay/model exposure; provide a local-only detailed view in the dashboard and speak only the minimum evidence.
missing: Capture shell exit code, signal, pid/process-group, effective cwd, timeout, and rewritten-command provenance in the durable receipt.
Persist a common correlation ID from the pendant turn through relay job, Mac job, action ledger, and browser command.
A server-side causal-trace assembler and redaction layer; current /jobs and /journal are separate and do not join reliably.

args.user_asks: “Keep working on this until it is actually finished, even if the Mac agent restarts or the browser loses its connection.” Treat this as one durable mission and tell me only when it reaches a verified stopping condition.
args.why_useful: A multi-step browser-plus-Mac task currently behaves like a sequence of one-shot jobs: a crash, browser disconnect, or transient command error strands it and leaves the owner guessing. A durable mission would checkpoint after every observable milestone, reattach after restart, retry only explicitly idempotent steps, and require a fresh verification before claiming success.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for checkpoint classification and retry planning; realtime model only for owner updates or ambiguity.
args.latency_budget: No extra latency for individual steps; recovery within 15 seconds of agent/browser heartbeat returning. Spoken updates should begin within 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per mission depending on retries and browser screenshots; most checkpoint work is deterministic.
args.security_concerns: Persist only task intent and step hashes, never page cookies or raw shell environment. A replay must reject non-idempotent steps unless an explicit compensating action exists. Owner must be able to say “stop” from the pendant and see the exact checkpoint.
missing: A durable mission record distinct from transient jobs, with step preconditions, idempotency class, checkpoint and verified-stop predicate.
Boot reconciliation that converts stale processing jobs into resumable missions, closes ledgers, and can terminate/reap orphaned shell process groups.
Browser heartbeat-aware resume and a cross-surface cancel/stop command that reaches the actual child process.

args.user_asks: “What am I looking at, and what is the next useful action?” Use the active Safari page, the visible Mac app, my active project, and the last few pendant turns to answer in one short spoken response; if I say “do it,” carry out that next action.
args.why_useful: This is the core hive-mind experience: the browser alone cannot know the local project or voice context, and the Mac alone cannot see authenticated page semantics. It eliminates the costly ritual of explaining context aloud and makes the pendant a hands-free bridge from perception to action.
args.model_tier: Cheap vision/text model fuses screenshot and DOM summaries; realtime model speaks the concise answer and resolves the owner's “do it” confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Initial answer within 3 seconds, action dispatch within 1 second after “do it.” Capture can happen concurrently across Mac and browser.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.04 per query, dominated by screenshot/vision tokens; cache unchanged DOM and project summaries to avoid resending context.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and screenshots leave the device only for the requested turn; redact password fields, payment data, and hidden DOM. Never execute inferred actions without the explicit follow-up phrase. Keep a local audit link to the exact screenshot/DOM snapshot used.
missing: A synchronized snapshot API that atomically captures active window, active Safari tab/DOM inspection, active project, and recent pendant turn ID.
A cross-surface fusion prompt/cache with provenance so the answer cites which surface supplied each fact.
A confirmation-bound handoff that converts the selected next action into /execute or browser command without losing the snapshot correlation.

args.finding: Mac agent, relay, and Safari extension are all online. Relay last saw Mac bridge at 2026-08-08T03:13:27Z; Safari active tab is X Home with 9 tabs. GET /browser/inspections is empty even though GET /jobs contains a recent successful browser_read_page receipt with evidence capsule.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status, GET /browser/inspections, GET /jobs

transcript.text:
Discovered live state:

- Mac agent: online, full-control mode enabled, Accessibility and Screen Recording granted.
- Relay: reachable; Mac bridge online.
- Safari extension: online with 9 tabs; active tab is X/Home.
- Browser inspections are currently empty, despite `/jobs` containing a successful recent `browser_read_page` job and evidence capsule. That inconsistency matters for reliable cross-surface context.

I recorded this finding. I produced three capabilities this round:

1. **Spoken, evidence-backed task postmortems** — “Why did that fail?” with a joined pendant → relay → Mac → browser timeline.
2. **Durable missions** — tasks that checkpoint, recover after restarts, retry only idempotent work, and stop only after verification.
3. **Cross-surface situational awareness** — “What am I looking at, and what should I do next?” using Safari, visible Mac state, active project, and recent pendant context.

What is still needed is implementation rather than another diagnostic wrapper:

- A common correlation ID spanning pendant turns, relay jobs, Mac jobs, action ledgers, and browser commands.
- Durable shell facts: exit code, signal, PID/process group, timeout, effective cwd, and rewritten-command provenance.
- A mission/checkpoint store with boot-time reconciliation and process-group cancellation.
- An atomic snapshot endpoint joining active Mac app, Safari DOM/page state, active project, and pendant turn.
- A fix for browser evidence discoverability: successful browser receipts should populate or link to `/browser/inspections`, rather than leaving that endpoint empty.
- Secret redaction before shell output or authenticated browser content is sent to the model or relay.

I do not need another tool request this round. The outstanding USB-serial diagnostics request remains pending; I will not re-ask for it.

args.user_asks: “Before you do that, prove that you are acting on the page and file I mean; if the browser, screen, and task history disagree, tell me exactly what conflicts instead of guessing.” Then, after I say “yes,” execute and verify the same target is still in focus.
args.why_useful: Today the system can read a browser page, inspect Mac state, and execute actions, but it has no owner-facing identity check that binds those observations to one target. A stale Safari tab, a changed URL, or a similarly named local file can produce a confidently wrong action. This capability would make the hive mind trustworthy for consequential everyday work without reducing its maximum access: it detects disagreement, explains it briefly through the pendant, and proceeds when the owner resolves it.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic matching first (tab ID/URL/title, window/app identity, file inode/hash, job/session ID); use the realtime model only to phrase a short conflict report and interpret the owner's resolution.
args.latency_budget: Target proof in 1–2 seconds; re-check immediately before dispatch and within 1 second after completion.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.001–$0.01 per action; deterministic identity checks dominate latency, with model cost only for ambiguous conflicts.
args.security_concerns: Do not send raw page contents or file contents merely to establish identity. Use URL, tab/window IDs, titles, hashes, and redacted metadata; treat a changed authenticated page as a conflict rather than silently refreshing or reusing stale evidence. Keep the proof bundle locally auditable.
missing: A first-class target identity/proof object shared by browser commands, Mac actions, and pendant turns, with observedAt timestamps and expiry.
Mac-side foreground-window and file identity capture (bundle ID, window ID, path/inode/hash) exposed alongside machine context.
Browser-side atomic tab identity plus DOM/content hash at both inspection and action time; current inspections can be empty even when a browser receipt exists.
An execution preflight/postflight hook that compares the proof object and records a verified-target result without turning maximum-access execution into a blocking policy.

args.user_asks: “Undo the last thing you changed, everywhere.” Reverse the browser mutation and the related Mac file or app change as one operation, and tell me if any part cannot be safely restored.
args.why_useful: The owner can already undo a narrow subset of Mac actions, but a real task often crosses an authenticated webpage and local files. A browser form submission, downloaded artifact, renamed file, or edited document currently has no coherent cross-surface rollback. This would give the pendant a practical safety net after autonomous work without imposing approval gates before it runs.
args.model_tier: Deterministic compensating-action engine for known mutations; realtime model only to explain irreversible portions and ask which partial rollback the owner wants.
args.latency_budget: A rollback plan should be spoken within 2 seconds; execute reversible steps within 5 seconds, with verification after each surface.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.02 per rollback; mostly deterministic storage and verification, with model cost only for ambiguous mappings.
args.security_concerns: Snapshots may contain authenticated form data and private files. Encrypt local snapshots, apply short retention and field redaction, never store passwords or payment secrets, and clearly report irreversible effects such as sent messages or external submissions.
missing: A cross-surface mutation bundle recording pre-state and compensating action for browser commands as well as Mac actions.
Browser primitives for restoring form values/navigation or issuing an application-specific undo, plus local file snapshot/version integration.
A dependency-aware rollback planner that reverses browser and Mac steps in safe order and marks partial failure explicitly.
Pendant-accessible lookup of the last completed mutation bundle, with retention and privacy controls.

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

- **Cross-surface target proof**: before acting, prove that the intended browser tab, visible app, file, and task history refer to the same target; detect conflicts instead of guessing, then re-check immediately before and after execution.
- **Cross-surface undo**: “Undo the last thing you changed, everywhere,” using mutation bundles and compensating actions across browser and Mac, with explicit reporting of irreversible portions.

Both require new shared identity/state contracts between the pendant, browser, relay, and Mac rather than another execution gate.

args.user_asks: “What actually needs my attention right now?” Give me a ranked, spoken answer that combines my live Mac work, authenticated Safari tabs, pending Mac actions, reminders/calendar, and anything the pendant has queued or failed; if I say “handle the first one,” carry it through the right surface and report the evidence, not just ‘done.’
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful everyday behavior: it turns four disconnected surfaces into one trustworthy attention queue. It is intentionally an interrupt-time triage, not another scheduled briefing: it uses the current foreground app and browser sessions, distinguishes actionable blockers from bulk notifications, and can immediately hand the selected item to the browser or Mac while the pendant remains the conversational control.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background ranker to normalize signals and cache a compact attention queue; use realtime only for the owner's spoken question and the final decision. Use the Mac planner/browser harness for execution and faculty-judgement/action for risk and evidence.
args.latency_budget: Initial spoken triage under 2 seconds from cached snapshots; refresh only stale sources in parallel within 5 seconds. Execution may take longer but must stream stage and evidence back to the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Typically one small background ranking call plus one realtime turn; roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on how much browser/page text is refreshed. Browser extraction and Mac work dominate latency, not token generation.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page text and local window metadata leave the browser/Mac only to the relay/model when needed; redact secrets and page bodies from durable logs. Never claim completion without a URL/file/job receipt. A destructive or externally communicative action should be announced before execution, while ordinary navigation, reading, and local organization can follow the owner's maximum-access policy.
missing: A cross-surface attention-item schema with source, urgency, freshness, evidence URL/path, and executable continuation token
A parallel snapshot collector for foreground Mac state, browser sessions/page watches, reminders/calendar, and pendant outbox/error state
A spoken continuation protocol that binds “the first one” to a stable item ID and returns receipts/evidence

args.user_asks: “Continue the thing that failed.” Identify the last incomplete browser/Mac workflow from my pendant history, explain the exact step and side effect state in one sentence, resume only the unfinished steps, and read back the final evidence or the precise blocker.
args.why_useful: Failures today strand the owner between a spoken request and a half-completed browser or shell job. This gives the wearable a durable ‘pick up where we stopped’ affordance across a relay restart, Mac restart, or browser reconnect, without redoing a sent email, submitted form, or moved file.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic ledger/journal reconciliation and a cheap classifier to locate the unfinished step; use realtime only to explain the checkpoint and converse if ambiguity remains. Use mac-planner/browser harness to resume and faculty-action to emit receipts.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint answer under 1.5 seconds from local journals; reconciliation and browser/Mac resume begin immediately and stream progress. A restart scan should complete within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually a small classification call, under $0.01, with realtime only if the checkpoint is ambiguous. The expensive part is re-opening and inspecting browser/Mac state.
args.security_concerns: Persist only action IDs, step hashes, redacted paths/URLs, and evidence digests—not shell environment or page secrets. Resume must be idempotent by action/step identity and explicitly avoid replaying completed external side effects. If state cannot be proven, stop and say what is unknown rather than retry blindly.
missing: Boot-time reconciliation that marks orphaned processing jobs and closes or classifies open ledgers
A stable job-to-ledger-to-browser-command correlation ID and idempotency key on every step
A resume executor that verifies preState/postState and skips completed side effects
Pendant protocol for asking for and announcing a resume, including stale/offline handling

args.change: Make run_shell execution produce a truthful, resumable command receipt without reducing FULL_CONTROL_MODE: invoke commands through a tracked child-process wrapper that records the original action and any rewrite, resolved cwd, sanitized environment fingerprint (never values), pid, start/finish/duration, numeric exit code/signal, bounded stdout/stderr digests, timeout/kill reason, and reversible/permanent classification. Pass the job abort signal to the child so cancellation can actually terminate it. On startup reconcile processing jobs and open ledgers: mark orphaned steps interrupted, close successful ledgers, and expose a verified resume plan keyed by jobId + actionId + step hash. Wire the documented SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS knob to the actual default, and add bounded concurrency/child cleanup.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant says a Mac task failed, the owner will know whether it timed out, was killed, exited 127, or completed before the relay dropped—and can say “continue” without rerunning a side effect. Long commands can stop when cancelled, and a Mac reboot no longer leaves the system confidently reporting ‘running’ forever.
args.effort: Medium-to-large Mac-agent change across computerControl, executor, jobTracker, actionLedger, orchestrator startup, and the resume endpoint; add crash and timeout integration tests.
args.risk: A wrapper can change shell signal and process-group semantics; roll out behind a receipt version, keep the current exec path as fallback, and compare results in dry-run tests. Never auto-resume a step whose post-state cannot be verified. Child process groups must be killed on timeout/cancel to avoid orphans.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; a few hundred bytes to a few KB of receipt storage per action, bounded by existing retention caps. Small CPU overhead for hashing and process tracking.
args.latency_impact: Negligible (<10 ms per command), with materially faster cancellation and recovery. Startup reconciliation adds at most a short scan of the existing capped stores.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability while preserving the owner's deliberate unrestricted capability. Environment values remain excluded; command and paths need redaction rules. Pid/exit metadata and hashes are safe to persist, but logs must not duplicate stdout containing secrets.
depends_on: A stable jobId-to-ledger correlation passed in planMeta
A real closeLedger call for every orchestrator execution path
Signal-aware shell spawn with process-group cleanup
A versioned resume/idempotency contract shared by Mac and browser actions

args.user_asks: “Run this on my Mac even if the relay is down.” While the pendant and ESP32 bridge are USB-attached, accept the spoken/button request locally, execute the Mac action, and return audio plus truthful LED status; when disconnected, queue the exact request and replay it once on reconnect instead of pretending it ran.
args.why_useful: The hardware is physically on the owner's desk today but has not registered LTE. This makes the wearable useful immediately in the real offline/USB state: a dropped cloud link no longer turns the pendant into a dead microphone, and the owner gets an honest local-vs-queued distinction.
args.model_tier: Use a small local/relay classifier for short commands and deterministic Mac actions; reserve realtime for spoken interpretation and responses. The pendant firmware only handles transport state, request IDs, durable outbox, and LED/audio truth—not language reasoning.
args.latency_budget: Button-to-local dispatch under 300 ms after USB framing; spoken result under 2 seconds for status/open/volume-type actions. Reconnect replay starts once and reports each state transition.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost while USB-local; one normal realtime turn only when cloud interpretation is needed. Main cost is firmware/bridge protocol and Mac local-agent integration.
args.security_concerns: USB-local requests inherit the owner's deliberate full-control Mac policy, but every request needs a nonce/request ID and a visible local/queued state. Store only encrypted or redacted request metadata in the pendant outbox; never cache credentials or arbitrary command output. Reject stale replay IDs and require idempotency for retries.
missing: A direct USB serial protocol between nRF9160, ESP32 audio bridge, and local-agent with framed request/response messages
Local speech/request routing when LTE/relay is unavailable, or a clearly defined subset of deterministic commands
Exactly-once replay integration between pendant_store OUTBOX and Mac job/action IDs
Audio reply path from local-agent through the ESP32 bridge to the pendant

transcript.summary: Produced four non-gating proposals: (1) a live cross-surface attention queue that ranks current Mac, authenticated browser, reminders, jobs, and pendant state and lets the owner handle the selected item; (2) “Continue the thing that failed,” with verified checkpoint/resume across Mac and browser; (3) truthful shell receipts, signal-aware cancellation, and boot reconciliation while preserving FULL_CONTROL_MODE; and (4) USB-local pendant operation that is useful now despite LTE not being registered. The most important new capability is the first: one spoken, evidence-backed answer to what actually needs attention now.

args.user_asks: “While you’re doing that, change the plan: skip the last email, save the draft, and tell me what remains.” Let me interrupt any running Mac/browser task from the pendant, have the agent checkpoint the current step, revise only the unfinished plan, and continue without restarting or duplicating completed side effects.
args.why_useful: Today a spoken request is effectively fire-and-forget once execution begins. The owner must wait, cancel ineffectively, or issue a second request that can conflict with the first. Mid-task steering makes the system feel like an assistant rather than a batch queue, especially for long browser workflows and shell jobs.
args.model_tier: Use a low-latency realtime turn only to capture the interruption and resolve its target; use a cheaper planner to recompute the remaining DAG from the checkpoint. Deterministic action execution and faculty-action enforce step identity and receipts.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the interruption on the pendant within 500 ms, checkpoint at the next safe boundary within 2 seconds, and present the revised remaining steps within 5 seconds. For a currently blocking process, use a real process signal rather than waiting for its original timeout.
args.cost_estimate: One small realtime interruption turn and one planner call, usually $0.01–$0.05; most cost is browser/Mac execution, not the dialogue.
args.security_concerns: The interrupt must bind to an unambiguous job ID and preserve an immutable record of what already happened. Never undo or resend a side effect merely because the plan changed. The owner’s stated maximum-access policy remains intact; the safety requirement is truthful checkpointing, not a new approval gate.
missing: A pendant interrupt frame carrying active job ID, revision number, and replacement instruction
Preemptible Mac shell and computer-use execution with process-group signaling and safe step boundaries
A plan-revision protocol that preserves completed action IDs and invalidates only the unfinished suffix
Browser command cancellation/replacement and a streamed state model shared with Mac jobs

args.user_asks: “What changed in the tabs I left open?” Compare authenticated Safari tabs with their last known snapshots, summarize only meaningful changes, identify which changes require action, and if I say “take care of it,” update the right page or create a local follow-up with a citation to the exact changed content.
args.why_useful: The owner loses time reopening the same tabs and reconstructing what changed. This turns the browser’s persistent sessions into longitudinal memory: it distinguishes a changed price/status/deadline from cosmetic page churn and connects a detected change to a concrete Mac action or spoken follow-up.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic snapshot hashing and a cheap diff extractor first; invoke a stronger model only for semantic change ranking and spoken compression. Use browser automation for authenticated inspection and Mac actions for local follow-ups.
args.latency_budget: Return a cached change list in under 2 seconds; refresh stale tabs concurrently within 8 seconds. A selected follow-up should begin immediately and stream its citation and result.
args.cost_estimate: Low: hashing/diffing is local; one small summarization call per changed tab batch, roughly $0.005–$0.03. Browser refreshes dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: Keep page snapshots local to the browser/Mac where possible, persist only hashes, extracted changed spans, URL, timestamp, and redacted citations. Respect authenticated-session boundaries and never expose unrelated tab content in spoken output. Do not act on a changed page if the DOM no longer matches the cited evidence.
missing: Versioned per-tab snapshots with semantic extraction and retention policy
A browser-side change detector that can compare authenticated content without exporting whole pages
A spoken diff/result format with stable tab IDs and exact citations
A bridge from a selected change to a Mac reminder, job, or browser action

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 9 of 10 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /watches. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: “Get the latest invoice from the portal and put it in my Taxes folder.” Use my already-authenticated browser session to locate and download the correct document, verify its date/amount against the page, move it into the right local project folder, and read me the saved path and evidence.
args.why_useful: This crosses the boundary no single node can cross: the browser has the authenticated portal, while the Mac has the private filesystem and the pendant is the quickest way to ask. It removes a tedious, error-prone transfer without asking the owner to copy links, download files, or explain where they belong.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap planner for folder and filename resolution; browser automation handles the authenticated download; Mac execution verifies file metadata/hash and performs the local move. Realtime only interprets the short request and reports the result.
args.latency_budget: Find and inspect the portal document within 10 seconds; download, verify, and file it within 30 seconds. Stream ‘found / downloading / verified / saved’ so silence is never mistaken for failure.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one small planning call, about $0.01–$0.04, plus browser/Mac execution. File transfer itself has no model cost.
args.security_concerns: The document crosses from an authenticated browser session to local storage and must not be sent to an unrelated cloud service. Keep content on the Mac/browser bridge, log only URL, metadata, checksum, and destination, and reject ambiguous invoices rather than choosing silently. Do not delete or overwrite an existing file without the owner’s explicit instruction.
missing: A browser download handoff that returns a local artifact handle rather than page text or a cloud URL
A Mac-side artifact verifier/mover with checksum, collision, and quarantine handling
Cross-surface provenance linking the portal URL, extracted invoice metadata, downloaded file, and final path
A policy for authenticated document handling and redacted receipts

args.user_asks: “Take care of whatever is on my screen.”
args.why_useful: This would be the single most useful everyday action: a button press or spoken phrase on the pendant hands the currently focused Mac window and authenticated Safari tab to one planner, which figures out the smallest useful next step, acts through the Mac or browser session, and tells the owner exactly what changed. Today the owner must explain which app/tab is relevant and manually bridge the wearable to the machine.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short intent and spoken result; a cheaper background planner handles screen/tab interpretation and execution, escalating to realtime only when ambiguity blocks action.
args.latency_budget: First acknowledgement under 700 ms; capture active-window/tab context within 2 s; simple actions complete within 10 s, with truthful_action_status_beacon and a spoken progress update for longer work.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 for a simple turn depending on screenshots and browser DOM; the expensive part is vision tokens, so send structured window/tab metadata first and a screenshot only when needed.
args.security_concerns: The Mac snapshot may contain private document names and the browser may expose authenticated data. Keep capture on the Mac where possible, redact secrets before relay, never infer authorization from screen content, and speak a preview when the inferred action is destructive. The owner’s maximum-access policy means no artificial gate for ordinary reversible work, but every result must say what actually ran.
missing: A single context-capture contract joining focused app, selected text, active Safari tab metadata, screenshot/DOM inspection, and the pendant turn ID
Planner routing that can choose Mac shell, typed Mac action, browser command, or mac-vision from that contract
A durable result receipt that links the spoken request, captured context, action job, browser command, and final evidence

args.user_asks: “Read me the important thing in the Safari page I’m on, and if it needs action, do it.”
args.why_useful: The owner can get a spoken, source-grounded answer without touching the keyboard: the browser extension supplies the authenticated page’s visible content and session identity, the Mac supplies which tab is actually foreground, and the pendant is the zero-friction output. If the page contains a task (approval, reply, deadline, form), the agent can execute it and read back the exact result rather than merely summarizing.
args.model_tier: A cheap extraction/classification model handles page text and identifies candidate actions; realtime is reserved for the two-sentence spoken answer and a follow-up question when multiple actions are plausible.
args.latency_budget: Foreground-tab confirmation under 1 s, extraction under 4 s, spoken answer under 6 s; actions continue asynchronously with a pendant status pulse and completion receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per page when DOM text is available; screenshots and vision are fallback costs. Browser content, not whole browser history, should be sent.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated content must remain scoped to the active tab and current browser session; do not include cookies or raw page source in relay logs. The agent must quote the page title/host and the evidence excerpt it used, and distinguish 'I read' from 'I acted'.
missing: A foreground-tab lock so the active Safari tab cannot silently change between capture and action
A browser-side 'read/actionable' result containing bounded text spans and stable element IDs rather than a screenshot-only observation
A spoken evidence formatter that cites host, page title, and the exact action receipt

args.user_asks: “Do it, but don't tell me it's done until you have verified the result.”
args.why_useful: This turns the system from an action launcher into a dependable assistant. After a Mac shell, UI, or authenticated-browser action, it independently checks the expected postcondition—file exists with the right contents, window state changed, message appears in Sent, form shows success—and reports success, failure, or uncertain state on the pendant. For high-value work, that is more useful than faster execution because it prevents confident false completion.
args.model_tier: A low-cost deterministic verifier evaluates typed postconditions and receipts; use mac-vision or a small model only when the state is visual/semantic. Realtime speaks the final three-state result, not the whole trace.
args.latency_budget: Verification begins immediately after each action; ordinary checks under 2 s, visual/browser checks under 8 s. If verification exceeds that, the pendant says 'still checking' and never upgrades to completed by timeout.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for filesystem/process/HTTP status checks; $0.01–$0.04 when a screenshot or DOM interpretation is required. This saves more expensive retries and owner time.
args.security_concerns: Verification must not perform a second mutation while checking. Evidence should be minimized and redacted, with host/app/page identity and hashes or bounded excerpts rather than full private content. Persist the precondition, intended postcondition, observed state, and confidence so an owner can audit what 'done' meant.
missing: An action schema carrying explicit preconditions and postconditions through POST /execute rather than only a free-form label
A verifier registry for shell, file, Mac UI, and browser assertions, including a third state of unknown
A cross-surface receipt join keyed to the same turn/job/action ID and firmware status-beacon update only after verification

args.change: Add a non-blocking execution trace around every run_shell and browser action: preserve the original submitted action before the silent rewrite, record resolved cwd, redacted environment keys (never values), start/finish timestamps, pid, exit code/signal, timeout-vs-exit distinction, stdout/stderr byte counts plus bounded tails, rewrite provenance, and a stable jobId/actionId/ledgerId join. Wire exec to an AbortSignal so cancellation can terminate the child, close the ledger on every terminal path, and mark processing jobs interrupted during boot.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant says a Mac task failed or is still running, the owner can know whether it timed out, exited nonzero, was rewritten, or died with the agent—and can retry the exact safe step instead of guessing or repeating a destructive command.
args.effort: Medium: replace exec with a spawned process wrapper, extend receipts and boot reconciliation, and add tests for timeout, cancellation, rewrite, crash, and retry.
args.risk: Changing process execution can alter shell quoting and signal behavior. Keep the existing command-string mode initially, feature-flag the wrapper, and retain the raw action in the local audit record for rollback/debugging.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage (bounded tails and metadata); no model API cost. A small CPU cost per process for tracking and hashing output.
args.latency_impact: Under 10 ms setup per shell action; cancellation and timeout become immediate instead of waiting up to 120 seconds.
args.security_impact: Do not persist environment values, especially AGENT_TOKEN and LLM keys. Hash or redact sensitive output before relay while retaining local bounded evidence.
depends_on: A durable action/job/ledger correlation ID passed from POST /execute
A closeLedger call in the orchestrator finally path
AbortSignal support in computerControl.runShell

args.change: Implement a two-phase foreground-tab lease: on a pendant request, atomically capture Safari window/tab identity, URL origin, title, DOM revision/hash, and selected text; reject any browser action if the tab/window or revision changes before execution, then reacquire and verify the same lease after the action. Return a bounded evidence span and an explicit stale-context result to the relay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask about or act on the page they are actually looking at without the assistant accidentally reading one tab and clicking another after Safari changed, a race that is currently invisible and particularly dangerous for authenticated work.
args.effort: Medium: extension heartbeat and inspection schema changes plus a lease store in the Mac agent; no new model is required.
args.risk: Dynamic pages may legitimately change their DOM and cause a false stale result. Retry one fresh inspection, then speak that the page changed rather than guessing. Never retain cookies or full page bodies in the lease.
args.cost_impact: Tiny local metadata store; usually no additional API tokens because the lease uses existing inspection data.
args.latency_impact: Adds one inspection/hash round trip, typically 200–800 ms; avoids expensive vision retries and mistaken actions.
args.security_impact: Improves session safety by binding actions to origin/tab identity; logs only origin, title, revision hash, and bounded excerpts.
depends_on: A browser inspection response with stable tab/window identity and DOM revision
A turn-scoped correlation ID shared by pendant, relay, Mac job, and browser command

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
What is still missing is not another shell wrapper or another status endpoint. The three connective pieces I would build next are:

1. **A turn-scoped context envelope** joining pendant turn ID, focused Mac app, foreground Safari tab, browser revision, screenshot/DOM evidence, and project/session.
2. **Explicit postconditions** on actions, so “completed” means independently verified rather than merely dispatched.
3. **A foreground-tab lease** that refuses to act if Safari changes between inspection and execution.

I also attempted a shell-observability change, but the recorder correctly rejected it as already covered by an existing backlog item. I will not rephrase that proposal.

transcript.summary: Produced three distinct owner-facing capabilities: “take care of whatever is on my screen” as a cross-surface handoff, source-grounded spoken Safari action, and postcondition-verified execution. Added a concrete browser-harness change: a two-phase foreground-tab lease that detects tab/DOM races before acting. The system already has the component routes; the missing value is their shared turn identity, evidence contract, and verification semantics.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the browser extension currently exposes a stable tab/window identifier and DOM revision/hash in its inspection payload. Without that, a safe foreground lease cannot distinguish a page that changed from the page that was originally inspected.

Added a concrete browser-harness change: a two-phase foreground-tab lease that detects tab/DOM races before acting. The system already has the component routes; the missing value is their shared turn identity, evidence contract, and verification semantics.
args.biggest_unknown: Whether the browser extension currently exposes a stable tab/window identifier and DOM revision/hash in its inspection payload. Without that, a safe foreground lease cannot distinguish a page that changed from the page that was originally inspected.

args.user_asks: “Only interrupt me for something that truly needs me now; otherwise handle it and give me a quiet digest later.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets an assistant that protects attention across the wearable, Mac, and authenticated browser instead of turning every notification into a spoken interruption. It can recognize that a calendar change, work message, browser alert, or failed Mac job is urgent, ask one concise question through the pendant when necessary, and defer everything else into a time-bounded digest with no repeated alerts.
args.model_tier: A cheap background classifier handles incoming events and urgency scoring; realtime is used only for an actually urgent interruption or the owner's reply. A daily digest can use a slower background model.
args.latency_budget: Ingest events within 3 seconds; urgent decisions within 5 seconds; non-urgent items are silent and summarized at the owner's next configured quiet-window boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per event with structured notification metadata; model cost is dominated by long message bodies, which should only be fetched for candidates near the urgency threshold.
args.security_concerns: Notification content can be highly private. Keep raw bodies on the Mac/browser where possible, send only extracted features to the relay, and make the pendant announce source and reason before reading sensitive text aloud. The system must never silently send, accept, cancel, or modify an external commitment merely because it classified it urgent.
missing: A unified event intake for Mac notifications, browser page watches, job failures, and relay events with deduplication and provenance
An owner-editable urgency policy that learns from explicit dismiss/defer/interrupt feedback without silently changing high-impact preferences
A durable quiet queue with expiry, escalation rules, and a spoken digest renderer shared by relay and dashboard

transcript.summary: Recorded a new attention-firewall capability: the owner can ask the pendant and Mac to decide which incoming events deserve an interruption, handle or defer the rest, and deliver one quiet digest. It requires a unified event intake, owner-editable urgency policy, and durable deduplicated quiet queue with escalation and spoken digest support.
transcript.biggest_unknown: The exact event sources and notification permissions available on the live Mac/browser harness are not established this round, and I did not probe further as instructed.

args.user_asks: "What exactly happened to the thing I asked you to do?" — Give me one spoken answer that joins the pendant request, the Mac actions, browser evidence, and any failure or partial completion, with timestamps and confidence.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must infer truth from scattered job, receipt, browser, and LED states. This would be the single most useful everyday behavior: after any hands-free command, the owner can ask once and get an honest causal account, including 'it never ran' versus 'it ran and the site rejected it'.
args.model_tier: background for receipt joining and summarization; realtime only to speak the already-built summary
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds when records exist; no fresh Mac round trip unless the owner explicitly asks for live status.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap background summarization call, roughly $0.001–$0.01; dominant cost is context if raw stdout/page text is resent, so pass hashes, excerpts, and structured receipts first.
args.security_concerns: Browser titles, URLs, shell paths, and failures can be sensitive. Keep raw bodies local, send redacted structured fields and evidence hashes to relay, and say when confidence is based on a stale cache. No mutation or confirmation is needed because this is read-only reporting.
missing: A join key linking jobId, ledgerId, action receipt IDs, browser command IDs, and pendant turn ID
A compact evidence-capsule join route that redacts raw stdout/page text
A spoken receipt formatter with explicit partial/unknown states

args.user_asks: "Stop that now." Make a pendant button press or spoken command terminate the currently running Mac shell or computer-use process immediately, then tell me whether it was killed, had already finished, or could not be reached.
args.why_useful: The current cancel signal is only checked between steps; a 120-second shell or computer-use action keeps running after the owner says stop. This gives the owner a real emergency brake for runaway UI automation, stuck scripts, or an accidental long command.
args.model_tier: deterministic control path; no LLM required for kill, with realtime only for the spoken acknowledgement
args.latency_budget: Issue the kill in under 300 ms after a live link; report the final process state within 2 seconds. If the Mac is unreachable, persist the cancel intent and report queued/unconfirmed rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; a small local process supervisor and one relay event dominate implementation, not model tokens.
args.security_concerns: This is intentionally powerful but scoped to the owner’s active agent job, never arbitrary PIDs. Use process groups so descendants are killed, record signal and final exit state, and make the pendant LED distinguish killed from unreachable. Do not infer completion from a lost connection.
missing: Run shell and computer-use actions under a tracked process-group supervisor with PID/start-time identity
A relay command route carrying a job-scoped cancel intent and delivery receipt
An abort path that calls killpg/Windows equivalent and settles the action ledger with interrupted status

args.user_asks: "Keep an eye on this authenticated page and only interrupt me if a change affects my work." Watch the browser session, compare a meaningful page change against the current Mac project/session, and send the pendant a short alert with the exact changed evidence and a quiet digest for everything else.
args.why_useful: The browser can see logged-in pages that the relay cannot, while the Mac knows which project and files are active. Combining them avoids noisy 'page changed' alerts and catches the rare change that actually matters, without requiring the owner to keep a tab open in their attention.
args.model_tier: background model for change classification and local-project relevance; deterministic page hashing/diffing and relay delivery; realtime only when the pendant alert is requested
args.latency_budget: Poll or event-deliver within 1–5 minutes depending on site support; classify in under 10 seconds; alert immediately only above the owner’s configured relevance threshold.
args.cost_estimate: Low ongoing cost: deterministic DOM/text hashes most cycles, one cheap background classification per substantive diff (roughly $0.001–$0.02). The dominant cost is authenticated page polling and occasional long page context.
args.security_concerns: Never export cookies, form fields, or full private pages. Keep snapshots in the browser/local Mac, transmit only redacted diff spans and evidence hashes, and require explicit opt-in per URL/session. Alerts should disclose stale/offline state and never claim a page was checked while Safari was disconnected.
missing: A browser watch definition that stores redacted structural/text diffs rather than only latest page text
A Mac relevance adapter exposing active project/session metadata without uploading files
A relay priority classifier and pendant alert queue with quiet-hours/digest semantics

transcript.summary: Produced three distinct cross-surface capabilities: (1) a single spoken, evidence-backed causal receipt joining pendant turn, Mac job, browser evidence, and partial/unknown states; (2) a real emergency stop that kills the active process group rather than merely setting a cooperative abort flag; and (3) relevance-filtered authenticated browser watches corroborated against the active Mac project, with quiet digests and high-priority pendant alerts. The live Mac bridge is online and Safari has nine tabs; /jobs confirms browser actions and /routing currently reports no sampled token usage. The granted mac_read_diagnostics schema still fails resolver matching in this run, so I could not obtain fresh host process/audio facts.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the browser watch and evidence-joining primitives already exist under routes not exposed by the summaries; their implementation needs a complete route/action inspection before engineering begins. For the emergency stop, the key unknown is whether the current Mac process launcher can expose and reliably kill descendant process groups without replacing the owner-approved FULL_CONTROL surface.
